<!-- Source: docs-site/podcasts.md -->

# Podcasts

ForeverLM can extract transcripts from Apple Podcasts episodes, making your podcast listening available as sources for AI-assisted learning.

::: warning Apple Podcasts is the supported podcast source
Podcast discovery and episode identity come from **Apple Podcasts**. Apple Podcasts caches its transcripts as files on your Mac, which ForeverLM reads directly when available.

Other podcast players — **Spotify**, Overcast, Pocket Casts, and the rest — are not supported, because they don't make transcripts easily available: transcripts either don't exist or stay locked inside the player, with no local files or public API another app could read.

If you normally listen elsewhere, you can still get an episode into ForeverLM: find it in Apple Podcasts and open its transcript view once, and ForeverLM will pick it up from there.
:::

## How Episodes Are Discovered

ForeverLM queries your local Podcasts database for episodes you have played since the start of 2026 and checks whether a transcript is available.

This requires **Full Disk Access** in macOS System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access. Setup asks for it before the Podcasts step: **Open System Settings**, add ForeverLM with the **+** button (macOS does not list it until you do), turn it on, then **Relaunch ForeverLM**.

## Choosing Shows in Setup

Setup's Podcasts step lists every show you follow in Apple Podcasts and every show with an episode you played, with how many episodes would come in, before anything is imported. Tick the shows to bring in; every show starts ticked.

- **Ticked:** the episodes you play arrive, with their transcripts.
- **Unticked:** the show's episodes never become sources. The same as **Never Import** in a show's menu.

**Untick All** and **Tick All** set every show at once. The import starts when you press Continue, so a show you turned away is never fetched. To bring a show in but keep it out of the list, chat, search and reviews (its transcripts are then not cleaned up by AI, so it costs nothing), choose **Hide** from the show's menu in the sidebar later.

## Transcript Availability

Apple Podcasts downloads transcripts on demand. They are **not** available by default. To make a transcript available:

1. Open **Apple Podcasts** on your Mac.
2. Navigate to the episode.
3. Click **Transcript** in the episode detail view. This triggers Apple to download and cache the transcript locally.

Once cached, ForeverLM can extract it. If Apple has no accessible transcript, the episode remains available for transcript recovery.

Hidden shows and episodes do not use the automatic transcript worker. Unhiding one starts its pending transcript work again.

## Hiding and the Whole Show

A single episode hides from its right-click menu (**Hide**) and comes back from Hidden Items. Hiding one episode is visual only: it stays in your knowledge, so chat, search and reviews still use it. Hiding a show (right-click an episode, **Hide *show***) is stronger: its episodes leave the list and are kept out of chat, search and reviews as well, so a show you never asked for stays quiet. Unhide one episode from Hidden Items and that episode is back in both. Nothing is deleted either way. The bottom of the Podcasts list then ends with a quiet **N hidden shows** row; click it for the Hidden Items page, where each show unhides in one click and expands to its hidden episodes. While you are searching, that row instead says how many hidden items match, so a search that comes up short because the show was hidden says so.

Unhiding a show brings its episodes back, including any that another device hid one by one while the show was hidden. An episode you hid yourself before hiding the show stays hidden. A show that is not hidden but has hidden episodes appears in Hidden Items with a **Show all** button that reveals them together.

Discovery imports the episodes you listened to. For a show you want in full, right-click any of its episodes and choose **Follow *show*: Import All Episodes**. Every episode Apple Podcasts holds locally for that show is added now, played or not, and from then on each new episode that appears in Apple Podcasts is imported on the next sync, whether or not you have played it. Episodes already in your library are left alone, and everything queues for transcripts like any other episode. **Unfollow *show*** stops the automatic import and keeps what was added. Following a show in ForeverLM assumes you follow it in Apple Podcasts too, since that is where the episode list comes from. In the Podcasts list, an episode you have played sorts by when you last played it, and one you have not played sorts by its publish date, so a whole catalog falls into episode order.

## What You Listened To

An episode you play in Apple Podcasts counts as listening on the day you played it, the same as listening in ForeverLM: it is on that day of your Schedule's history and the Planner's log, and "quiz me on the podcasts I listened to last week" finds it. Any play counts, even a few minutes, because Apple keeps when you last played an episode and not how much of it you heard; it is never marked finished. Each sync looks back 30 days, so the first one after you update brings in the last month. Hidden shows and hidden episodes are left out.

## Private and Member Feeds

A paid subscription usually arrives in Apple Podcasts as a private feed with a longer name — "The Peter Attia Drive - Private Subscriber Feed (🔓 for …)". Apple transcribes only the public catalog, never a private feed, so an episode from a member feed has no transcript of its own. ForeverLM resolves it to the same episode in the show's public edition: the public show is the one the feed's name begins with, and the episode is the one with the same number, or the same title when the feed carries no numbers. The row keeps its place in your library and takes the public episode's transcript. An episode with no public twin — a members-only bonus, an AMA the public feed carries only as a preview — reports **No matching episode found on Apple Podcasts**, and **Transcribe Audio** remains available for it.

An episode's show notes are never its content. A podcast row that only holds the episode's web page — an older import did this for private feeds — is not ready; it queues for its transcript like any other episode.

If Apple says an episode has no accessible transcript, ForeverLM automatically searches YouTube when the YouTube plugin is connected. A show's upload is often titled differently from its episode, so ForeverLM looks first at the videos the episode's own web page links, then at the show's YouTube channel for uploads from around the episode's release (once an earlier episode's transcript came from that channel), and only then searches YouTube. It proposes video matches in the reader, saying when one is linked from the episode's page or on the show's channel, but never chooses one itself. Confirm that a video is the same episode before selecting **Use Transcript**; only then are its captions attached to the Apple Podcasts source. An AI assistant connected over MCP does the same with `find_podcast_on_youtube` and, once you confirm the video, `import_podcast_youtube_transcript`, which also takes a YouTube link you found yourself.

## Transcript Cleanup

An episode's transcript reads the moment it is fetched, Apple's or one from **Transcribe Audio**: each speaker's turn under its label, cut into paragraphs at sentence ends, with no AI involved. Then, in the background, ForeverLM uses the model selected for **Transcript Formatting** to make it easier to study, and the formatted transcript takes the plain one's place:

- Adds paragraph breaks at natural topic transitions
- Replaces diarized speaker IDs with real names when the episode evidence is clear
- Removes confidently identified sponsor messages and ad reads, including their promotional transition lines

The model identifies exact spans rather than rewriting Apple Podcast transcripts. ForeverLM deletes a proposed ad only when both boundaries match one unambiguous, bounded passage; uncertain passages remain. Editorial discussion of a company or product, guest affiliations, disclosures, credits, and substantive content are preserved.

Formatting runs two episodes at a time and picks up where it left off after you quit, so a first import of hundreds of episodes is readable at once and formatted in turn. An episode you asked for (confirming a match, **Transcribe Audio**, fetching a transcript again) goes first. A hidden episode is not formatted unless you asked for it, and a transcript you changed meanwhile, such as by naming its speakers, is never formatted over. **Stop** under Running in the background leaves the rest waiting until you resume it. Past your daily background AI limit a newly fetched transcript is still formatted, while the clean-up of older transcripts waits for the next day.

When a confirmed YouTube video supplies a missing podcast transcript, the same podcast-specific ad cleanup runs while the captions are formatted for readability.

## Using Podcasts with AI

Once transcripts are extracted, they appear as sources in Studio. Select them and your AI assistant can:

- Summarize key points from the episode
- Quiz you on specific claims or mechanisms discussed
- Compare ideas across multiple episodes or with your other sources

In the [in-app Chat](/in-app-chat#citing-a-moment), a citation into an episode can carry the moment the passage was spoken (`[2 · 12:34]`); clicking it scrolls the transcript to that segment. In a [Memory review](/in-app-chat#memory-review), tell the tutor "keep podcasts quick" to have every podcast reviewed with the recall question only.

## Tips

- Episodes with long-form interviews and technical discussions work best.
- Make sure to open the transcript view in Apple Podcasts **before** trying to extract.
- Podcast sources use local file paths, ensuring they're tied to the actual transcript you listened to.

---

<!-- Source: docs-site/x-posts.md -->

# X Posts

ForeverLM lets you sign in with one or more X (formerly Twitter) accounts and sync their saved bookmarks as sources.

::: tip
X setup also appears in the [Plugins](/external-plugins#x-bookmarks) guide.
:::

## Signing In

You do not need an X Developer account, API subscription, or client ID.

1. Open **Plugins -> X** on the icon strip, or select the **X** tab in the Library.
2. Click **Connect**.
3. Sign in to X and approve ForeverLM's access.

ForeverLM uses its production X app and OAuth 2.0 PKCE. Your authorization is limited to your own X account and can be revoked from either ForeverLM or X.

## More Than One Account

**Plugins -> X** shows each connected account on its own card, with when it last synced. Click **Add Another Account** to connect a further one: X signs you in as whichever account your browser is signed in to there, so sign in to the other account on x.com first. Signing in again as an account that is already connected refreshes it instead of adding a second card.

**Sync** and **Disconnect** on a card act on that account only, and an account that needs signing in again says **Reconnect needed** while the others keep syncing. Disconnecting an account stops its bookmark sync; the posts it already brought in stay.

## Syncing Bookmarks

Tap **Sync Bookmarks** in the X sidebar tab to sync every account, or **Sync** on one account's card. New bookmarks are fetched and added to your source queue. Each post appears with the full tweet text, author, and any included URLs.

## Posting

Your AI assistant can post to X through the [MCP connection](/mcp-tools) when you ask it to. With one account connected it posts as that account; with several, it has to say which one.

## Tips

- Bookmark threads and long-form note tweets for the richest source material.
- Short one-liner tweets rarely have enough substance for meaningful learning.

<!-- Source: docs-site/external-plugins.md -->

# Plugins

Plugins are optional. On the Mac, **Plugins** is a place of its own on the icon strip, under Library, as in Codex. Its head has two tabs, **Plugins** and **Skills** (your [chat skills](/in-app-chat#skills)), and a search. The Plugins tab lists **Installed** first — every plugin that is connected, or connected and needing a reconnect — then the **Built-In** plugins and **Your Plugins** that are not connected yet. Every built-in plugin, Slack included, shows **Connected**, **Reconnect needed** or **Not connected**. Selecting one opens its page there, under a breadcrumb (**Plugins › Slack**; click **Plugins** or press ⌘[ to go back), with its controls and, under **Includes**, the ForeverLM tools it brings to a chat and to an assistant over MCP. A row's **⋯** (or a right-click) has **Open**, **Open in Other Window** and **Copy Link**, a `foreverlm://plugins/…` address that opens the page again. Settings has no Plugins. The web library has the same place on its rail for the plugins the browser can reach: Google Drive, Slack, Linear, GitHub and Notion, with the same tabs, Installed first and the same breadcrumb; skills do not reach the web yet, so its Skills tab says they are written in the Mac app.

Plugins run only after you explicitly connect them. ForeverLM never scans X or YouTube on app startup. A selected Google Drive folder refreshes on app activation, when its tab opens, or when you refresh Studio.

There is no Zotero or Paperpile plugin, by design. A paper has to live in your ForeverLM library, its PDF in your iCloud container, before the app can search it, read it aloud, chat about it, or review you on it, and a plugin that pointed at a record in another database would enable none of that. The route is a one-time import instead, from setup's Papers step or by an assistant with the ForeverLM plugin; see [Papers](/papers#coming-from-a-reference-manager).

Don't see your service here? You can [build your own plugin](/build-your-own-plugin) for any service you can reach with code — it runs on your side with ingest-only access, and an AI assistant can write it for you in minutes. The guide includes Read AI as a worked example.

## Google Drive

Use the Google Drive plugin to import meeting recordings, transcripts, and notes from folders you choose. Drive shortcuts are followed to their underlying files, so shared Meet recordings and transcript Docs import the same way as files owned directly in the selected folder.

1. In ForeverLM, open **Plugins -> Google Drive**.
2. Select **Connect Google Drive** and approve read-only Drive access in your browser, once.
3. Back in ForeverLM, choose your meeting folder from My Drive, Shared with me or a shared drive, or search for it by name.

Google's read-only Drive permission (`drive.readonly`) can read files across your Drive, but ForeverLM's plugin traverses and imports only folders you explicitly link. OAuth tokens stay in your Apple Keychain and are not sent to ForeverLM servers.

If Google Drive stops working, ForeverLM says so in an orange bar above the meeting recording and at the top of the Meetings list, with a **Reconnect Google Drive** button. Reconnecting asks Google for access once more and refreshes the folders you already linked; you do not choose them again. If the browser page goes nowhere, **Cancel** stops the wait. The linked folder refreshes when the Drive tab opens, when the app becomes active, or when you refresh Studio.

Open an imported meeting recording and select **Find mentioned papers** to read its complete transcript and notes for academic papers participants explicitly discussed or recommended. A recording-only session is transcribed on-device first. Web Studio's **Find papers** reader action opens the same source in the Mac app and starts that scan. Resolved candidates can be added through the normal paper import pipeline; incomplete mentions remain visible as unmatched rather than being silently discarded. The same workflow is available to MCP assistants through `scan_meeting_for_mentioned_papers` and `list_video_cited_papers`.

Opening a Drive meeting plays the recording in ForeverLM through the plugin's authenticated read-only session. The recording is kept only in the disposable app cache. If Google Drive supplies a transcript Doc, it appears as the **Transcript** section; if the meeting has only notes and a recording, ForeverLM transcribes the recording on-device when opened and syncs the transcript alongside the notes. Web Studio embeds the Drive preview and offers **Get transcript** when the Mac still needs to generate one.

## Calendar

The Calendar plugin makes the Mac's Calendar app your day. The **Now** chip at the bottom left of the Studio window shows today's events, and an assistant plans your day by adding events to the calendar, in a chat with `/plan` or from Claude or ChatGPT with the ForeverLM plugin.

1. In ForeverLM, open **Plugins -> Calendar** and click **Turn On**. macOS asks once whether ForeverLM may use your calendars.
2. Under **Calendars in your day**, tick the calendars that make up your day. Until you change the list, every calendar but Birthdays is shown.
3. Under **New events go to**, pick the calendar new events are added to, or leave it on the Calendar app's default.

Access is granted to this Mac by macOS and never leaves it, and the calendar choice is this Mac's. ForeverLM writes only the events you or an assistant add, and never changes an event with other people on it; you change a meeting in the Calendar app. An event ForeverLM adds shows in the Calendar app at once and reaches your phone through your calendar account. **Turn Off** stops ForeverLM reading the calendar; every event stays where it is.

### Google, Outlook and other calendars

There is no separate Google Calendar plugin: ForeverLM reads whatever the Mac's Calendar holds.

- To see a Google calendar, or a Microsoft 365, Exchange or Outlook calendar (where Teams meetings live), add the account in **System Settings -> Internet Accounts** and switch on **Calendars** for it. Its calendars then appear in the Calendar app and in ForeverLM's list.
- To see a calendar you only have a link to, such as a published Outlook calendar or a class timetable, subscribe to it in the Calendar app with **File -> New Calendar Subscription…** and its `webcal://` or `.ics` link.

A subscribed calendar is read-only, so it cannot be where new events go.

## X Bookmarks

Use the X plugin to sync saved X bookmarks into Studio as sources.

1. In ForeverLM, open **Plugins -> X**, or select the **X** tab in the Library.
2. Click **Connect**.
3. Sign in to X and approve ForeverLM's access.

After connecting, use **Sync** on the X plugin page or **Sync Bookmarks** in the Studio X tab. You can connect more than one X account: each has its own card on the plugin page, with its own **Sync** and **Disconnect** (see [X Posts](/x-posts#more-than-one-account)).

There is no developer setup: ForeverLM supplies the production OAuth client and X API access. Each person authorizes only their own X account.

## YouTube

Use the YouTube plugin to import either **Liked videos** or videos from a playlist in your account named **ForeverLM**, and to follow any number of **channels**. Connect as many Google accounts as you like: each account has its own import source, which is one of the two and can be changed later. Followed channels belong to you, not to an account, and sit alongside whatever the accounts import.

The plugin imports **metadata only** — a video's transcript (and slides) are fetched on demand the first time you open or review it, not when it's imported.

Connecting YouTube is read-only. ForeverLM reads only the source you select.

### Set Up YouTube

1. In ForeverLM, open **Plugins** on the icon strip.
2. Select **YouTube** and click **Connect**. Google asks you to grant read-only access to your YouTube account.
3. To add another account, click **Add Another Account** below the account cards and sign in with the other Google account. Each account is its own card, labelled with its channel name, with its own **Disconnect**.

There is no Google Cloud setup: YouTube signs in against ForeverLM's own OAuth client.

ForeverLM opens a temporary `127.0.0.1` callback while Google sign-in is in progress, and requests this Google scope:

```text
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.readonly
```

### Choose What to Import

After connecting an account, choose its source (each account chooses for itself):

- **Liked videos** — choose whether to import existing and future likes or only future likes. Raw transcripts are imported automatically. AI formatting is a separate opt-in because formatting a large history can use substantial credits.
- **ForeverLM playlist** — create a playlist in YouTube named exactly `ForeverLM`; all of its current videos import, and later changes stay in sync. The playlist may be public, unlisted, or private.

If more than one playlist in an account is named ForeverLM, rename the extras before selecting it. Switching an account's source keeps videos already imported and changes what ForeverLM follows from then on. When several accounts import Liked videos, they share one **Liked videos** list, and an unliked video is only archived while a single account is connected, because the list does not record which account liked a video. If Google revokes an account's access, its card says **Reconnect**; reconnecting the same channel brings back what it imported. Disconnecting an account forgets its choices.

### Follow Channels

Under **Followed channels**, paste a channel's address (`youtube.com/@handle`, `/channel/UC…`, or an older `/c/` or `/user/` link) or just its `@handle` and click **Follow**. ForeverLM resolves the channel, imports its newest 50 uploads into a group named after the channel in the YouTube tab, and from then on imports every new upload with the plugin's refresh. Nothing is archived when a video leaves a channel.

The back catalog beyond those 50 stays on YouTube; to bring an older run of videos in, add the channel's uploads or a curated playlist as a course. **Stop Following** keeps the videos already imported. Transcripts follow the same rules as other plugin imports: captions are fetched on first open, and AI formatting only runs when **Format new transcripts automatically** is on.

### Automatic Import

Turn on **Automatically import new videos** to keep every account's selected source and every followed channel fresh. One account failing does not stop the others. Followed channels are read with the first connected account's access. ForeverLM also refreshes them when you refresh the Videos tab.

::: tip Watch Later is not available
Google's YouTube Data API does not expose the Watch Later playlist, so it can't be followed. Liked videos and ordinary playlists are supported.
:::

## Slack

Slack is managed in the app. The **Slack** row in **Plugins** shows **Connected** or **Not connected**, and its pane lists every connected workspace with a switch per channel for what ForeverLM may read; a switch takes effect the moment it is flipped. **Connect Slack…** (or **Connect Another Workspace…**) opens Slack's own consent screen in a sheet over the window and finishes the connection without leaving the app, and each workspace card has **Disconnect…**, which revokes its tokens at Slack. The same page is still available at app.foreverlm.com/slack-connect for a browser you are already signed in to, and it is where a workspace connected before a newer read scope existed is asked to grant it again. ForeverLM reads Slack as you and never posts. The connection lives on your ForeverLM account, not on the Mac, so it survives restarts, updates and reinstalls; the Mac reaches it with its own Sign in with Apple session, which the app renews on its own while you keep using it. It also follows the account if Apple ever re-issues your Sign in with Apple identity, as a change to the app's Sign in with Apple grouping or developer team does: the first request from the new identity moves the workspace connections and their channel choices across, so nothing has to be connected again. The tools an assistant gets from it are listed in the [MCP Tools Reference](/mcp-tools#slack).

You can connect more than one workspace. The Slack page lists every workspace on your account; choose one to pick its channels, and **Connect another workspace…** takes you back to Slack, which asks which workspace to add. Each workspace has its own channel choices and its own permissions, so a workspace connected before a permission existed is asked to grant it on its own. A chat reads and searches across all of them at once: every channel, message and file an assistant is shown says which workspace it came from. **Disconnect this workspace** revokes that workspace's tokens at Slack and leaves the others as they are; its channel choices are kept, so connecting it again brings them back.

## Linear

Linear is connected in the **Linear** row of **Plugins**, and you can connect more than one workspace. The page lists each connected workspace as its own card, with the Linear user the reads are made as and its own **Disconnect**; **Add Another Workspace** opens Linear's consent screen in a sheet, which asks which workspace to add, and **Connect Linear** does the same when none is connected. The Linear page of your ForeverLM account at app.foreverlm.com does the same in a browser. The connection is read-only by construction. ForeverLM asks Linear for the single `read` permission, reads issues, comments, teams and projects as you when a chat asks, and never creates, edits, comments on or assigns anything; there is no code path that writes to Linear. The row shows **Connected** (or **2 connected**, and so on) or **Not connected** because the Mac asks the ForeverLM gateway that holds the grants. A chat reads every connected workspace at once and says which one each result came from; an assistant can also name one workspace. Nothing read from Linear is kept between reads. The connections live on your ForeverLM account, not on the Mac, and follow it if Apple re-issues your Sign in with Apple identity, as the Slack connection does. Linear's access tokens expire after a day; the gateway renews them on its own, and a grant Linear no longer honours is reported as a reconnect for that workspace. **Disconnect** on a workspace's card revokes that grant at Linear and forgets it, and leaves the others as they are. The tools an assistant gets from it are listed in the [MCP Tools Reference](/mcp-tools#linear).

## GitHub

GitHub is connected on the web too: the **GitHub** row in **Plugins** links to the GitHub page of your ForeverLM account, where you authorize the ForeverLM GitHub App and choose where it is installed. Where ForeverLM can read is exactly where the App is installed: an organisation you administer, or your own account; **Add an organisation** on that page opens GitHub's install chooser, and `list_github_repositories` in a chat names the same link. The connection is read-only by construction. The App's permissions are Contents, Issues, Pull requests and Metadata, all read, and there is no code path that pushes, comments, merges or changes anything on GitHub; a chat that wants to act points you at the page. The row shows **Connected** or **Not connected** because the Mac asks the ForeverLM gateway that holds the grant, and the GitHub pane says the same in a sentence with a button that reads **Connect GitHub…** or **Manage GitHub…**. Nothing read from GitHub is kept between reads. The connection lives on your ForeverLM account, not on the Mac, and follows it if Apple re-issues your Sign in with Apple identity, as the Slack and Linear connections do. GitHub's user tokens expire after eight hours; the gateway renews them on its own, and a grant GitHub no longer honours is reported as a reconnect at the same page. **Disconnect GitHub** on that page revokes the grant at GitHub and forgets it. A notebook can be linked to the repository it is about, from the **Repository** section of its About on the Mac and in Web Studio or through the Project tools (`create_project`, `update_project`), so a chat in that notebook reads the right repository without being told. The tools an assistant gets from it are listed in the [MCP Tools Reference](/mcp-tools#github).

## Notion

Notion is connected in the **Notion** row of **Plugins**, and you can connect more than one workspace. The page lists each connected workspace as its own card with its own **Disconnect**; **Add Another Workspace** opens Notion's consent screen in a sheet, where you choose the workspace and tick the pages and databases ForeverLM may read, and **Connect Notion** does the same when none is connected. What ForeverLM can read is exactly what you shared: to add a page later, open it in Notion and choose **Connections** in its **•••** menu. The connection is read-only by construction. Its capabilities are read content and read user information without email, and there is no code path that creates, edits, moves or comments on anything in Notion; a chat that wants to act points you at the page. The row shows **Connected** (or **2 connected**, and so on) or **Not connected** because the Mac asks the ForeverLM gateway that holds the grants. A chat reads every connected workspace at once and says which one each result came from; an assistant can also name one workspace. Nothing read from Notion is kept between reads. The connections live on your ForeverLM account, not on the Mac, and follow it if Apple re-issues your Sign in with Apple identity, as the Slack, Linear and GitHub connections do. A grant Notion stops honouring is renewed by the gateway on its own, and one it will not renew is reported as a reconnect for that workspace. **Disconnect** on a workspace's card revokes that grant at Notion and forgets it, and leaves the others as they are. The tools an assistant gets from it are listed in the [MCP Tools Reference](/mcp-tools#notion).

<!-- Source: docs-site/build-your-own-plugin.md -->

# Build Your Own Plugin

ForeverLM deliberately ships very few built-in plugins. Any service you can
reach with code (Readwise, RSS, Zotero, Fireflies, a company wiki, …)
can feed your library through a **plugin you build yourself**, in minutes,
usually by asking an AI assistant to write it for you.

Your plugin runs on *your* side, with *your* credentials for the service,
and pushes sources into ForeverLM through the same MCP server your AI
assistants already use — under a restricted **ingest-only** permission that
keeps it safe even if the code is sloppy or the token leaks.

## Why this is safe

When your plugin connects, it asks for the `mcp:ingest` scope instead of
full access. An ingest-only connection:

- **can** add sources, update the sources *it* added, import papers through the
  complete paper pipeline, and check server status;
- **cannot** read your knowledge base, delete or modify anything else, touch
  your notebooks or Schedule, or use any other tool.

You approve it once, in the same consent flow as any assistant — the approval
screen says exactly this in plain words. Every source it adds is labeled with
the plugin's name, so you can always see what came from where, and one
command (`remove_connector_sources`, from Claude or any full-access assistant)
removes everything a plugin ever added. A plugin connects over MCP, so, like
any assistant, it works while your MCP is in its 7 free days or paid for. ForeverLM charges nothing per tool call, but the gateway
rate-limits every client, so a runaway script runs out of rope quickly.

## The recipe (give this to your assistant)

The fastest path: **ForeverLM → Plugins → Build Your Own →
Copy Setup Prompt** — that button copies this exact recipe with your personal
MCP URL already filled in. The same pane lists every plugin you've
approved, with its logo, how many sources it has added, and buttons to remove
its access or its sources.

Or copy the prompt from here and fill in the blanks yourself:

> Build me a small plugin script that syncs **[SERVICE — e.g. my Readwise
> highlights]** into ForeverLM, and set it up to run **[SCHEDULE — e.g. once a
> day]**.
>
> ForeverLM exposes an MCP server (Streamable HTTP) at my personal URL, shown
> in ForeverLM → Settings → MCP. The plugin must:
>
> 1. Register itself as an OAuth client: `POST {my-url}/oauth/register` with a
>    JSON body including `"client_name"` set to a short human name for this
>    plugin (this name labels every source it adds), optionally
>    `"logo_uri"` set to an https icon URL (shown next to the plugin in
>    ForeverLM's Settings), your redirect URI in `"redirect_uris"`, and
>    `"token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"`.
> 2. Do the OAuth 2.1 authorization-code flow with PKCE (S256) against
>    `{my-url}/oauth/authorize` and `{my-url}/oauth/token`, requesting
>    **`scope=mcp:ingest`**. I will approve the request in ForeverLM (or with
>    my pairing code if I'm not at my Mac). Store the refresh token and refresh
>    as needed — the granted scope survives refresh. If the token endpoint
>    answers `invalid_client`, ForeverLM no longer knows this registration: I
>    removed the plugin's access, or ForeverLM was reinstalled or moved to
>    another Apple account. Stop and tell me how to reconnect it; reconnecting
>    registers again with the same `client_name` and never reuses the old
>    `client_id`.
> 3. Speak MCP over `POST {my-url}/mcp`: `initialize` first (keep the
>    `Mcp-Session-Id` response header on later requests), then push content
>    with the `add_sources` tool. Each item: a **stable canonical `url`** (the
>    dedup key — same item must produce the same URL every run), `title`,
>    `source_type` (usually `"article"`), and the full plain-text `content`.
>    A meeting (`source_type: "meeting"`) also carries `occurred_at` — when it
>    took place, ISO 8601 — and `parent_group`, the recurring series it belongs
>    to (matched to an existing meeting group by id or title, case-insensitive,
>    or created); without them a meeting is dated by the moment it was pushed
>    and sits outside every series in the Meetings tab.
>    At most 50 items per call and ~1 MB per request; split beyond that.
>    Papers deliberately do not go through `add_source`: call
>    `import_connector_paper` with a public paper `url`, or call
>    `get_connector_inbox`, stage a local PDF in the returned plugin-specific
>    directory, and pass that path plus a stable public `source_url` to
>    `import_connector_paper`. This preserves the required Paper Metadata and
>    Source Content Cleanup steps.
> 4. Be idempotent: re-running must not duplicate anything (the server dedups
>    by URL and reports `already existed`). To refresh something that changed
>    at the service, re-push it with `"update_existing": true`; for a meeting
>    that also applies `occurred_at` and `parent_group`, so one re-push
>    corrects meetings first pushed without them.
> 5. Read the per-item results `add_sources` returns and fail loudly — print
>    anything that reports an error; never swallow failures.
> 6. Keep my service credentials (API key, cookies) local to the script. They
>    must never be sent to ForeverLM — ForeverLM only ever receives the
>    extracted text.
> 7. Keep the plugin's own state (tokens, per-item hashes, the last-run
>    watermark) in a SQLite file next to the script, mode `0600`, not in a JSON
>    file. A JSON blob is rewritten whole on every save, so an interrupted run
>    can truncate it and lose the refresh token along with the sync history.
> 8. Hold an exclusive lock for the length of a run, and exit immediately if
>    another run holds it. Where refresh tokens are single-use and rotate
>    (Read AI's do), two overlapping runs race on the same token and break the
>    chain for both. When the chain does break, report it and say which command
>    reconnects rather than failing silently.
>
> Note: ForeverLM's MCP URL only responds while the ForeverLM app is running
> on my Mac, so handle connection failures by skipping the run and trying
> again next time, not by erroring the schedule away. One exception: if the
> URL answers HTTP 502, 503 or 504 and `GET http://127.0.0.1:8522/mcp-url`
> (ForeverLM's own listener on this Mac, up only while it is connected)
> returns `{"url": …}` naming a different URL, my personal URL has moved.
> Save that URL, register there again under the same `client_name`, approve
> again, and carry on. A registration and its tokens belong to the URL they
> were made at, so never send them to the new one.

That's the whole contract. The assistant writes the script; you run it on
whatever schedule suits the material — a scheduled assistant task, `cron`,
launchd, or just "run it when I ask".

## Example use cases

These are worked examples of the recipe above, not product features. Your
assistant builds the plugin, it runs with your
credentials on your side, and you own it — we don't ship or support these as
extensions.

**Read AI meeting transcripts.** Fill the recipe in with: *"sync my Read AI
meetings into ForeverLM"*. Read AI's API uses OAuth 2.1 with rotating refresh
tokens (your workspace needs Downloads enabled under Workspace Settings →
Reports & Sharing). Have the plugin list recent ended meetings, fetch each
transcript, and push one source per meeting with `source_type: "meeting"`
semantics via `add_sources` — a stable URL per meeting id keeps re-runs
duplicate-free, `occurred_at` from the meeting's start time dates it, and
`parent_group` set to the series name (the title with tags like `[EF]` and
any trailing date stripped) files it inside its recurring meeting in the
Meetings tab. Name the plugin so it starts with "Read AI" (the example
registers as "Read AI Meetings"): ForeverLM then files its meetings under Read
AI and shows its health on the Read AI card. When the Meetings tab has Read AI
meetings and no plugin for them, its notice copies this recipe already
filled in for Read AI, with these notes attached — and since those meetings
arrived through a plugin once, the copy opens by asking your assistant to
find that plugin and reconnect it, and to build a new one only if none is
left.

**Anything with a feed.** Fireflies, Readwise highlights,
RSS — the shape is always the same: fetch with your credentials, extract plain
text, push with stable URLs. If you can curl it, it can be a plugin.

## Where your sources land

Plugin-added sources appear in your library like any other source, marked
with a plugin origin and the plugin's name. They join notebooks, the
Schedule, and reviews only when **you** (or your assistant, at your ask) put
them there — a plugin can never schedule its own content or push it into an
assistant's context.

## Removing a plugin

Two independent switches, both in **Plugins → Build Your
Own**, next to the plugin's name:

- **Remove Access**: the plugin's tokens stop working immediately; it would
  need your approval again to reconnect. Sources it added stay.
- **Remove Sources**: every source it added is dismissed and archived — and
  won't come back on its own. (An assistant can do the same via the
  `remove_connector_sources` tool.)

## FAQ

**Does my service password/API key go through ForeverLM?** No. Your plugin
holds the service credentials and only sends extracted text to ForeverLM.

**What if two plugins use the same name?** They'd share a label (and a
bulk-remove). Give each plugin a distinct `client_name`. A name that starts
with a meeting provider's brand — "Read AI …" or "Zoom …" — claims that
provider: its meetings file under it, and its health shows on that provider's
card.

**Can a plugin read what's in my library?** No. Ingest-only connections
can't read anything except server status, their private paper-staging path,
and the results of their own pushes (add results include the existing-source
id when a URL was already in your library).

**Why does it say the connection failed at night?** Your ForeverLM MCP URL is
served by the app on your Mac; if the app isn't running, plugins can't
reach it. They should simply retry on their next scheduled run.

**Can my personal URL change?** Rarely, but yes: it follows your Apple
account, so it changes if ForeverLM is signed in under a different one. The
old URL then answers "not running" for good. A plugin running on the same
Mac can ask ForeverLM for the current one at
`http://127.0.0.1:8522/mcp-url`, which answers only programs on that Mac and
only while ForeverLM is connected. It returns the URL and nothing else.
Plugins built from the recipe above follow the move on their own; you approve
them once more.

<!-- Source: docs-site/drag-and-drop.md -->

# Drag & Drop

The primary way to use your sources with Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, or Edison Scientific. Your library is your content folder: add sources, then drag them straight into any AI chat.

## How It Works

1. **Find the source** in the Library, or open it in the Reader.

2. **Drag it** into your Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, or Edison Scientific chat window: its row in the Library, or the title of the source open in the Reader. It arrives in the chat as a file.

That's it. No accounts, no configuration, no extra tools.

## Tips

- Each drag carries one source: drag each source you want the chat to read.
- A paper with its PDF arrives as the PDF. Articles, podcasts and other sources with text arrive as text files, and a source with neither arrives as a link to its web page.

## Optional: Persistent Access

If you'd rather not drag sources into every conversation, you can [connect an AI assistant](/setup-mcp). This lets Claude, Codex, Gemini, or Grok search your entire library, read any source on demand, and run review sessions — all without dragging.

ForeverLM provides a hosted Cloudflare relay for MCP. MCP requests and responses pass through ForeverLM-operated Cloudflare infrastructure in transit and are not logged or stored there.

| | Drag & Drop | MCP Server |
|---|---|---|
| **Setup** | None | Copy the matching assistant prompt |
| **Sources** | What you drag in | Entire library |
| **Interaction** | Upload files into chat | AI calls tools directly |
| **Best for** | Most conversations | Power users who want hands-free access |

---

<!-- Source: docs-site/learning-with-mcp.md -->

# Learning with AI

Once your sources are in Studio, you can use AI assistants to actively learn from them — either by [dragging sources into a chat](/drag-and-drop) or through a persistent [MCP connection](/setup-mcp). This page covers the main workflows: exploring sources, review, and Socratic dialogue.

## Exploring your sources

The simplest starting point: ask your AI assistant what you've been reading.

**Example prompts:**
- *"List my sources and give me an overview of what I've been reading lately."*
- *"Search my sources for anything related to attention mechanisms."*
- *"Read my latest paper and give me a one-paragraph summary."*
- *"Compare these two papers — what do they agree on, and where do they diverge?"*

Ask about "the notebook I have open" and your AI uses `get_app_context`, which names the notebook in each ForeverLM window, frontmost first, and reads the frontmost one's sources. Or let it search with `search_sources_semantic` to find relevant sources by topic, or `search_sources_keyword` to sweep the library for every mention of an exact word.

## Review sessions

The idea is simple: explain a concept from scratch, as if teaching it. If you can't explain it simply, you don't understand it yet.

ForeverLM's MCP tools support structured review sessions that track your understanding over time.

### Starting a session

Ask your AI assistant to quiz you:

- *"Start a review session on CRISPR-Cas9 mechanisms."*
- *"Test my understanding of transformer self-attention."*
- *"Quiz me on the paper I just read about partial reprogramming."*

The AI calls `start_review_session`, which searches your source library for relevant content and returns it as context. The AI then asks you to explain the concept.

### During the session

The AI asks questions, you explain, and the AI evaluates your understanding:

1. **You explain** the concept in your own words
2. **The AI evaluates** — checking for accuracy, depth, and whether you addressed mechanisms vs. just surface-level facts
3. **Follow-up probes** — the AI asks targeted questions about gaps or imprecise parts of your explanation
4. **Repeat** until the topic is thoroughly covered

The AI evaluates your answers directly in the chat.

### Ending a session

When you're done, the AI calls `end_review_session` with an overall score, summary, and exported chat transcript. You can review past sessions later with `get_review_sessions` and `get_review_session_transcript` to track your understanding progression.

### Example session

> **You:** Quiz me on oxidative phosphorylation.
>
> **AI:** *[starts a review session, loads your biochemistry sources]*
> Explain the chemiosmotic theory — how does the proton gradient drive ATP synthesis?
>
> **You:** So the electron transport chain pumps protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane, creating a gradient. Then ATP synthase uses that gradient to generate ATP.
>
> **AI:** Good start — you've got the high-level flow right. But let me probe deeper: *why* does the proton gradient specifically drive ATP synthase rotation? What's the physical mechanism that converts a concentration gradient into mechanical work?
>
> **You:** The protons flow through a channel in ATP synthase, and the flow causes a rotor subunit to spin. Each rotation mechanically changes the conformation of the catalytic sites, forcing ADP and phosphate together.
>
> **AI:** Excellent — you've nailed the rotary catalysis mechanism. Score: 0.9. One more: what happens to ATP production if you add an uncoupling agent like DNP?

## Socratic dialogue

Beyond structured review sessions, you can have free-form Socratic dialogue with your AI about any source:

- *"I just read this paper on diffusion models. Challenge my understanding — ask me hard questions."*
- *"I think I understand how RLHF works, but test me. Don't go easy."*
- *"Play devil's advocate on the claims in this source about longevity interventions."*

The AI has full access to your source text, so it can cite specific passages, catch misunderstandings, and push you to think more precisely.

## Tips

- **Name the sources or the notebook.** A connected assistant searches your whole library unless you name a notebook or particular sources; ask about "the notebook I have open" and it reads that one.
- **Be specific about topics.** "Quiz me on attention" is less effective than "Quiz me on multi-head attention scaling and why we divide by sqrt(d_k)."
- **Don't just answer — explain.** Explaining works because it forces you to articulate mechanisms, not just recall facts.
- **Review past sessions.** Ask *"Show me my past review sessions on [topic]"* to see how your understanding has progressed.
- **Use across sources.** The best learning happens when you connect ideas: *"I've read papers on both CRISPR and base editing — quiz me on the differences in their mechanisms."*

---

<!-- Source: docs-site/setup-mcp.md -->

# Connect an AI Assistant

The app is free; connecting an assistant is the paid part. MCP is free for 7 days from your first sign-in (no card, nothing to click), then $19 once, the Early user deal, with no subscription, in **Settings → Billing** on the Mac. It covers Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini, Claude Code and every other MCP client on your account. When the 7 free days are over and nothing is paid, only MCP locks: the connection stops and an assistant's tool calls are refused with "ForeverLM's MCP connection is not unlocked on this account. Open ForeverLM on your Mac to unlock it." The app keeps working, the in-app Chat is never locked, and nothing is deleted. Paying brings the connection back by itself. The iPhone shows no price, since it has no MCP connection.

::: tip Most people don't need this
The easiest way to use your sources with AI is to [drag & drop](/drag-and-drop) them directly from Studio. A persistent connection lets an assistant search your full library and run review sessions without dragging files each time.
:::

ForeverLM can host the connection from your private iCloud library, so the Mac app and Web Studio can both stay closed. Open Web Studio once, choose **MCP** in Chat, and complete the separate iCloud authorization for always-on access.

::: warning Hosted MCP privacy
Always-on MCP keeps a revocable iCloud session and an account-scoped cache of synced library metadata, notebooks, Schedule relationships, and saved reviews in ForeverLM-operated Cloudflare storage. Source files remain in iCloud and readable source text is fetched only when a tool requests it. MCP traffic is not end-to-end encrypted from ForeverLM infrastructure.
:::

## Official extensions

- **Claude:** ForeverLM works today as a [custom Claude connector](#claude-custom-connector) on web, desktop, and mobile, and as a [Claude Code plugin](#claude-code-plugin) from its public marketplace. It is **not** in the [Claude Directory](https://claude.ai/directory) or the Claude plugin directory yet; both submissions are in progress. Use the setups below until the listings exist.
- **ChatGPT and Codex:** the official ForeverLM plugin version 1.0.2 was resubmitted to OpenAI on August 31, 2026 and is in `Review`. OpenAI has not issued a public ForeverLM listing URL yet. The plugin will appear in the [ChatGPT Plugins Directory](https://chatgpt.com/plugins) only after approval and ForeverLM's separate publish action.
- **Grok:** ForeverLM works today as a [custom Grok connector](#grok-custom-connector) on web, iOS, and Android. It is **not** listed in the [Grok connector catalog](https://grok.com/connectors) yet. Use the custom setup below until a catalog tile exists.

Until the ChatGPT plugin is public, use the custom setup below. ForeverLM will replace that primary action with OpenAI's canonical listing link after publication; no draft or guessed link is used.

Until ForeverLM appears in the Grok catalog, use the custom Grok connector below. ForeverLM will replace that primary action with the live grok.com/connectors listing after xAI publishes it; no draft or guessed catalog URL is used.

## Claude custom connector

ForeverLM is not in the Claude Directory. Add it as a custom connector instead:

1. In Web Studio, choose **MCP** in Chat and authorize always-on iCloud access. **MCP ✓** confirms it is ready.
2. In Claude on the web, open **Customize → Connectors** (Settings → Connectors redirects there).
3. Choose **Add custom connector**, name it **ForeverLM**, and enter this MCP URL: `https://plugin.foreverlm.com/mcp`. Choose **Continue**.
4. Under **Authentication**, choose **Always required**. Claude's probe labels the server **None · Detected** because the gateway answers MCP discovery before sign-in; every data-bearing tool still needs your account, so keep sign-in required.
5. Under **OAuth client**, choose **No client ID — register one automatically**. ForeverLM registers Claude through Dynamic Client Registration.
6. Choose **Add**, open the new **ForeverLM** entry, choose **Connect**, and complete Sign in with Apple.
7. Ask Claude to check the ForeverLM connection.

Once added on claude.ai, the plugin is also available in Claude Desktop and on Claude mobile under the same account. On a Team or Enterprise plan the entry is shared with the whole organization, so removing it removes it for everyone.

::: info Why the icon can lag behind the brand
Claude draws a custom plugin's icon from Google's favicon cache for the site's root domain (`foreverlm.com`), not from the MCP host. That cache refreshes on Google's schedule, so a recently changed mark can keep showing its predecessor for a while after the site itself is up to date. A directory listing would carry the name and icon directly, which is why one is worth having.
:::

## Claude Code plugin

Claude Code and Cowork can install ForeverLM as a plugin today from its public marketplace, ahead of the directory listing:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add ForeverLM-HQ/foreverlm-plugins
claude plugin install foreverlm@foreverlm
```

Then run `/mcp` in Claude Code, choose **foreverlm**, and complete Sign in with Apple. The plugin bundles the remote MCP server and four skills: a paper-library migration that moves a [Zotero, Paperpile or Mendeley library](/papers#coming-from-a-reference-manager) into ForeverLM once; a chat export that brings a conversation held with another assistant into ForeverLM as a chat, with the Markdown it produced saved as Pages and its citations linked to your Sources; an AI cost review that reads your AI usage ledger, names the tasks and models behind the spend, and proposes cheaper model settings from the [MCP tools](/mcp-tools#settings) that it applies only once you approve them; and a walkthrough writer that explains a paper, book chapter or article the way a good textbook does, one point at a time with short questions after the points they test, and saves it as the source's walkthrough. Once ForeverLM is published in the Claude plugin directory, `/plugin` will offer it without adding the marketplace.

## ChatGPT custom setup

1. In Web Studio, choose **MCP** in Chat and authorize always-on iCloud access. **MCP ✓** confirms it is ready.
2. In ChatGPT on the web, open **Settings → Apps → Advanced Settings** and enable developer mode.
3. Return to **Settings → Apps**, choose **Create**, and add an app named **ForeverLM** with this MCP URL: `https://plugin.foreverlm.com/mcp`.
4. Choose OAuth authentication, scan the tools, and complete Sign in with Apple.
5. Open a new chat, enable ForeverLM from the tools menu, and ask ChatGPT to check the connection.

ChatGPT plan and workspace permissions determine whether custom MCP apps are available. See [OpenAI's current developer mode requirements](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-developer-mode-apps-and-full-mcp-connectors-in-chatgpt-beta).

## Grok custom connector

1. In Web Studio, choose **MCP** in Chat and authorize always-on iCloud access. **MCP ✓** confirms it is ready.
2. Open [grok.com/connectors](https://grok.com/connectors).
3. Choose **New Connector**, then **Custom**.
4. Name the plugin **ForeverLM** and enter this MCP URL: `https://plugin.foreverlm.com/mcp`.
5. Complete Sign in with Apple.
6. In a Grok conversation, enable ForeverLM from Plugins and ask Grok to check the connection.

The same plugin is then available in Grok on web, iOS, and Android. If **Custom** is missing, the Grok plan may not include custom MCP plugins. On Grok Business and Enterprise, a team administrator must first add the custom MCP server in the [xAI console](https://console.x.ai).

::: info Catalog listing vs. custom plugin
The Grok catalog does not yet include a ForeverLM tile. A plugin you add yourself is named **ForeverLM** and shows as custom. Keep using that until a catalog listing exists. Do not look for a ForeverLM catalog URL; none has been published.
:::

### Grok Build (CLI)

Grok Build is a separate terminal surface. Adding the server there does not publish ForeverLM in the grok.com catalog.

```bash
grok mcp add --transport http foreverlm "https://plugin.foreverlm.com/mcp"
```

Complete Sign in with Apple on first use, then ask Grok to call `get_mcp_status`.

## Meta Muse custom connector

Muse has no settings screen for custom connectors; it builds one when you ask it to in a chat.

1. In Web Studio, choose **MCP** in Chat and authorize always-on iCloud access. **MCP ✓** confirms it is ready.
2. In the Mac app, open **Settings → MCP** and choose **Copy prompt** on the **Meta Muse** row.
3. Open [muse.ai](https://muse.ai), start a chat, and paste the prompt. It asks Muse to build a Custom Connector named **ForeverLM** for `https://plugin.foreverlm.com/mcp`.
4. Complete Sign in with Apple on the ForeverLM page Muse hands you. The page names Muse as the app you return to.
5. Approve the connector's access when Muse asks, and let Muse save it as a skill so later tasks can use it.

ForeverLM is not in Muse's connector directory, so it runs as a custom connector, which Meta does not review.

## Other assistants

Grok users should follow [Grok custom connector](#grok-custom-connector) instead of copying a prompt.

Any assistant or agent that speaks MCP over HTTP with OAuth can connect on its own: give it `https://plugin.foreverlm.com/mcp`. It registers itself, and you sign in with Apple on a ForeverLM page that names the app you will be sent back to. If ForeverLM does not recognise that app, the page says so; continue only when you started the connection from that app yourself.

For an assistant without its own row, the Mac app's **Settings → MCP** has an **Other assistant** row. Its prompt names no product: it tells the assistant to add the server with its own MCP command, config file, or custom-connector screen, to use OAuth without a client ID, and to say plainly if it cannot reach remote MCP servers.

1. Open Web Studio and choose **MCP** in Chat.
2. Authorize always-on iCloud access and wait for **MCP ✓**.
3. In the Mac app's **Settings → MCP**, select **Copy prompt** on the assistant's row (**ChatGPT** for Codex, or **Gemini**), or on **Other assistant** for any other. Claude Code has [its own plugin](#claude-code-plugin).
4. Paste the prompt into that assistant.
5. Let the assistant complete the setup, then approve the connection when ForeverLM asks.

## Troubleshooting

**Your AI says hosted MCP is not connected:** Open [always-on MCP setup](https://app.foreverlm.com/mcp-connect.html), authorize iCloud, and then retry in a new conversation.

**Setup did not finish:** Return to Web Studio, choose **MCP**, and retry the separate iCloud authorization. The Mac and Web Studio do not need to remain open afterward.

---

<!-- Source: docs-site/mcp-tools.md -->

# MCP Tools Reference

This is the complete tool contract of the official ForeverLM remote plugin
used by ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Grok: every tool the Mac app declares,
plus `import_epub` and `open_foreverlm`, which the gateway answers itself
(`open_foreverlm` is the launcher for the plugin's own ForeverLM home in
ChatGPT and Codex, not a tool for the model). See [Connect an AI Assistant](/setup-mcp) for setup. Many tools
need the learner's Mac open and connected; each section says which.

A [plugin you build yourself](/build-your-own-plugin) connects to the same
server with an ingest-only permission that allows a handful of these tools
(see [Plugins you build](#plugins-you-build)).

`notebook_id` names a notebook and `list_notebooks` lists them, so "my
Bioelectricity notebook" is the notebook of that title. The tools said project
until 2026-10-04 (`create_project`, `project_id`); the old names are gone, not
aliased.

A listing or search from a Mac that is showing only part of the library for
now carries `narrowed`, a sentence that says so without naming what is left
out: a field in a JSON answer, or the first line of a text answer. An assistant
then tells the learner it cannot see what they named from that Mac, instead of
choosing the closest match. `get_mcp_status` says which Mac that is.

## Status and sources

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get_mcp_status` | none | Report connection mode and capabilities. Call this first. From the Mac, `icloud_account` says which iCloud account its library syncs with (`syncs_with_icloud`, `environment`, and `user_record_name`, the account's container-scoped CloudKit user record name, the same kind of id `list_teams` gives for members, once CloudKit has answered); ForeverLM on the web uses it to ask only a Mac on the learner's own account. `answered_by` says which Mac answered, since another Mac signed in to the same account can hold the connection: `app` and `build`, `device_id` (that Mac's ForeverLM sync id), `model`, and `computer_name`, which is left out while its answers are `narrowed`. |
| `list_sources` | none | List source metadata from the library. |
| `get_source_content` | `source_id` | Return canonical readable text for one exact source ID. |
| `inspect_paper_figure` | `source_id`, `figure_label`, `panel_label?`, `approved_spend_usd?` | See a figure of a paper as an image, rendered from the paper's own PDF on the Mac and cropped to the figure, with its caption and ForeverLM's explanation of it. `panel_label` crops to one subfigure. The first look at a figure runs the vision model. Needs the Mac open and connected. |
| `show_source_image` | `source_id`, `query?`, `page?`, `slide?`, `at?`, `crop?` | See a picture from a source as an image: a figure from a paper, chapter or article by label or caption words, a PDF page a listing named, or a slide captured from a video or recording. `at` captures the frame on screen at any time in a video (`4:25`, or seconds), and `crop` zooms in on part of a slide or frame. No filter lists the pictures; up to four matches come back as images. Needs the Mac open and connected. |
| `search_sources_semantic` | `query?`, `source_type?`, `added_from?`, `added_to?`, `limit?`, `threshold?`, `notebook_id?`, `exclude_notebook_id?`, `show?` | Search on-device source embeddings, optionally within one source type or by the local day a source was saved to the library (`added_from`, `added_to`, full `YYYY-MM-DD` days; a work's publication year belongs in `query`, never here). `query` may be left out when the type or the days name the sources. This requires an active Mac; hosted MCP reports the capability as unavailable instead of silently changing the result. |
| `search_sources_keyword` | `keywords`, `match?`, `limit?`, `snippets_per_source?`, `source_type?`, `notebook_id?`, `show?`, `source_ids?` | Find every source whose title, author, or text literally contains a word or phrase, as a case-insensitive substring, with a mention count and passages for each. This is the exhaustive sweep the ranked search is not: `uncoupler` finds a source that only says `uncouplers`. One call takes up to 30 keywords; `source_ids` limits the sweep to particular sources, such as the papers in a chat, and the answer names the keywords none of them contain. It requires an active Mac, because the full text lives there. |
| `list_shows` | `kind?` | List every podcast show and YouTube channel in the library with its episode count. Gives the exact names `filter_sources` and a search's `show` take. Needs the Mac open and connected. |
| `filter_sources` | `show?`, `author?`, `title_contains?`, `text?`, `source_type?`, `include_archived?`, `limit?` | List every source whose metadata matches: all of one show's episodes, every paper by an author, everything with a name in its title, byline or show. Case-insensitive substrings, combined with AND, never ranked or cut off by similarity. Needs the Mac open and connected. |
| `get_app_context` | — | What is open in the Mac app: the notebook each window holds, frontmost first, with its title, `notebook_id` and source count, then the sources the frontmost window's notebook reads. Call it only when the learner asks about what is open; it is never a default scope. |
| `get_sync_status` | — | iCloud sync health for this Mac: changes still waiting to upload, records CloudKit never acknowledged, quarantined conflicts, the container environment, whether iCloud is full, and how much of the learner's iCloud ForeverLM's files take. `migration` reports the library's move to the new iCloud store. Use it when items are missing or stale across devices, before concluding anything is lost. |

## Settings

Settings › Sources › **Search & AI** in the Mac app, per source family, and whether each family's tab is pinned. **Search & AI** is the knowledge boundary: a family switched off stays in the library but is left out of chat, semantic and keyword search, reviews, and every library tool above. **Tab** is whether the family's tab is pinned to the Studio tab bar; the tab bar pins it, and Settings has no switch for it. Hiding a single source is visual only and is not a setting here. Both tools need the Mac open and connected; the choice syncs to the learner's other devices.

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get_source_settings` | — | Every family (`articles`, `papers`, `books`, `courses`, `meetings`, `podcasts`, `youtube`, `x`) with `include_in_search_and_ai`, `pinned` and `can_unpin`, in the learner's tab order. |
| `set_source_settings` | `family`, `include_in_search_and_ai?`, `pinned?` | Flip one family's switches. Pass one or both. Unpinning the last pinned family is refused: the tab bar keeps at least one. Returns the family's row and `changed`. |

Settings › General › **Memory review** in the Mac app. The budget, the day's new cards, background card drafting and its corner card, and the switches follow the account; the hour and the receipts are the Mac's. Both tools need the Mac open and connected.

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get_memory_review_settings` | — | `budget_minutes`, `new_cards_per_day`, `auto_draft_cards`, `draft_nudges`, `prepare_review_questions`, `prepare_daily`, `ready_by_hour`, with `automatic_drafting` (sources drafted a day, this Mac's last run and what it left waiting, the sources that failed today), and `last_preparation` saying what this Mac last did about the morning. |
| `set_memory_review_settings` | `budget_minutes?`, `new_cards_per_day?`, `auto_draft_cards?`, `draft_nudges?`, `prepare_review_questions?`, `prepare_daily?`, `ready_by_hour?` | Change one or several, through the pane's own entry points: the reminder follows its switch and the runner re-reads its clock. `new_cards_per_day` (1–100) also sets how many sources are drafted in the background each day, one for every four new cards. Returns the settings and `changed`. |

Settings › Sources › **Zoom Transcripts**, the recordings only Zoom can convert. Zoom records a meeting held on the Mac as raw `double_click_to_convert_*.zoom` files and converts them when the meeting ends; a meeting ended before that, or with Zoom quit, leaves the raw files, which ForeverLM cannot read. The Meetings tab and the Settings pane list each such recording with **Convert in Zoom** and **Ignore**, and these two tools are those rows. Zoom asks "Files from unknown sources" before converting a recording its meeting did not convert on the spot. When the learner has allowed ForeverLM under Accessibility, ForeverLM answers that dialog itself and converts waiting recordings on its own, one at a time and at most twice each, never during a meeting; without that permission it opens nothing in Zoom on its own. Both tools need the Mac open and connected, and the list and the ignore list are that Mac's.

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `list_unconverted_zoom_recordings` | — | Every waiting recording with `folder_path`, `title` (the series' title when one matches, else Zoom's file-safe spelling), `started_at`, `last_written_at`, `raw_bytes` and `ignored`; a recording written in the last fifteen minutes is left out because Zoom may still be converting it. `converts_automatically` says whether ForeverLM may use Accessibility and so converts by itself. |
| `resolve_unconverted_zoom_recording` | `folder_path`, `action` | `convert` opens the raw file in Zoom on the Mac, where ForeverLM answers Zoom's unknown-source dialog when it may use Accessibility (`answers_zoom`) and the learner does otherwise, and ForeverLM then files and transcribes the result; `ignore` takes the recording off the Meetings tab and never files it, for a meeting that did not happen; `unignore` lists it again. Ask before converting a recording the learner did not mention: it is visible on their screen and the transcription is billed. |

**Automatic audio** — set only from chat; the Settings window has no pane for it: the switches that narrate sources as they arrive, one per kind — `article`, `paper`, `book`, `course` and `explainer`. An explainer is stored as an article-typed source but has a switch of its own, so "always generate audio for explainers" never means every article; with it on, `generate_explainer` and the Mac's Explain button start an explainer's audio with the selected voice and no cost quote. Each kind takes an optional natural-language rule, and automation runs only on a voice it may spend on: a free OpenRouter voice always, a priced one only after the paid-voice consent, an unpriced voice or another provider never. Both tools need the Mac open and connected; the switches, rules and consent sync to the learner's other devices.

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get_automatic_audio_settings` | — | Every kind with `enabled`, `filter`, `sources_without_audio` and, when the voice may run, the estimated characters and price; the selected `voice` and its rate; `automation_available` with an `unavailable_reason` when it is not; `allow_paid_voices`; and, for a priced voice, the `paid_consent_quote` that consenting would start. |
| `set_automatic_audio_settings` | `kind?`, `enabled?`, `filter?`, `allow_paid_voices?` | "Always generate audio for articles from Martin Picard" is `kind: "article"`, `filter`, `enabled: true` in one call. `kind` + `enabled` arms or retires one switch — refused while the voice cannot run; `kind` + `filter` saves the rule, evaluated over the waiting sources first and kept only on success, an empty string clearing it; `allow_paid_voices` is the account's consent, a spending decision to put to the learner first, and `false` stops a paid run. Returns the settings with `changed`. |

Settings › AI Usage › **API keys**: the learner's own OpenRouter key. It is how ForeverLM's AI is paid for: with one stored, OpenRouter bills the learner directly, at its cost, for everything ForeverLM sends through it, and ForeverLM adds nothing. The key covers text models (chat, reviews, background tasks) plus every voice, speech-to-text, image and video model OpenRouter serves, and the reader names that scope. While the key is stored, an AI balance left from before balance was retired pays for nothing (`balance_still_pays_for`). The key lives in the Mac's iCloud Keychain, so both tools need the Mac open and connected, and neither ever returns the key.

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get_own_router_key` | — | `configured`, the `router` (`openrouter`) and `key_suffix` (last four characters) when one is stored, what text is billed to, and where to get a key. |
| `set_own_router_key` | `router`, `key?`, `clear?` | Store or replace the key for `router` (`openrouter`), or remove it with `clear: true`. Returns the same payload as the reader plus `changed`. Ask before calling it with a key the learner did not just hand you. |

Settings › **Chat** (the Default Model), Settings › **Background** (the Text
and Multimodal models every background task runs on, a task's own model, and free models),
Setup's Meetings answer, and the AI usage ledger behind
Settings › AI Usage › **Activity**: what each feature runs on, what it cost, and
the catalogue prices to compare against. The report never invents a number: a call the ledger could not price is counted in
`unpriced_calls` and left out of every total, and a model the pricing table does not
know says `price_known: false`. The `ai-cost-review` skill in the plugin walks these
three from report to approved change. These need an active Mac:

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get_ai_usage_report` | `days?`, `from?`, `to?` | Spend for the period (default the last 30 days; or local `YYYY-MM-DD` bounds, `to` inclusive): `totals`, `by_task` with the models each task ran, `per_call` averages (tokens in and out, cache reads, cost per priced call) and the task's `current_route` (provider, model, which Background model or the Default Model it follows, its catalogue price), `by_model` with each model's price row, and `by_day`. |
| `get_ai_task_settings` | — | `default_model`, `background_text`, `background_multimodal`, every background task with the model it runs on and which it `follows` (`background_text`, `background_multimodal`, or `task_model` when it has a model of its own; a meeting task says `kept_off_free_model` while it runs on a paid model because its Background model is free, and `waiting_for_paid_model` when it has none to run on), `meetings_may_use_free`, and the `catalogue` grouped by maker with each model's price per million input, output, cached-input and cache-write tokens, `supports_vision`, `supported_efforts`, `route_can_carry_speed` and `selectable`, and `free_models`: OpenRouter's free models that can run text work (`text`) and work that reads images (`reads_images`), best first, with `free_model_blocker` saying why none can run when that is so. `accepts` lists exactly what the setter takes. |
| `set_ai_task_settings` | `target`, `provider?`, `model?`, `meetings_may_use_free?`, `hide_training_models?`, `host_for?`, `host?`, `host_fallback?`, `host_region?`, `backups_for?`, `backups?`, `task_id?` | Change one setting as the pane's own control does: `default_model`, `background_text` or `background_multimodal` with a catalogue `provider` and `model` ; `task_model` with `task_id` and a catalogue `provider` and `model` gives one background task a model of its own (a task that reads images takes only a model that does), and with neither sends it back to following; `task`, `effort`, `speed` and `reset` are refused; `docs` with a catalogue `provider` and `model` sets the model Edit with AI in a Page runs on, as the ForeverLM logo on its panel does, and `docs` with neither sends Pages back to the Default Model (a chat's own model pick never reaches Pages); `meetings` with `meetings_may_use_free`, Setup's Meetings answer: false keeps meeting tasks on a paid model while their Background model is free, true lets them use it; `data_privacy` with `hide_training_models` to flip Settings › Data & Privacy's "Don't show models that train on my data", which hides every model the catalogue marks `trains_on_inputs`; a free model that starts costing money, or stops being offered, is moved off every setting on its own, onto another free model that can do the same work (the Free Models Router first), and the learner is notified. `backups` with `backups_for` (`chat`, `background_text` or `background_multimodal`) and `backups`, the whole ordered list of at most ten backup models the setting's work moves to when its model is busy, fails or sends back nothing usable (`[]` removes them); every background task uses the backups of the Background model it runs on, and the chat's serve only a scheduled task's runs, never a chat the learner types in. A free model from `free_models` is taken for `background_text` or `background_multimodal` even before the catalogue lists it; it moves only that setting. Refuses any other model the catalogue does not list, a free model while `free_model_blocker` is set, a retired model, a hidden training model, a text-only model where images are read. Returns the resulting settings and `changed`. Ask before calling it. |

**Every other Settings control.** Anything the Settings window can change, chat can change too, through the same setter the pane calls. So can every setting that has no pane, which `get_app_settings` labels "(no pane)": the meeting-icon switches, the text-to-speech cost prompt and the like. The catalog tools cover the plain switches, pickers and sliders (General › Your name, Voice › Dictation, Recordings & Podcasts and Text to speech, Images and Videos, Sources › Reading Lists and Zoom Transcripts, Plugins › Google Drive and YouTube, the Activity layout, and the settings with no pane), and the rest have tools of their own below. What stays in the window needs the learner's own hand: signing in, a plugin's consent page, a Stripe payment, Apple's sharing sheet. `open_settings` shows that pane. All of these need the Mac open and connected.

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get_app_settings` | `pane?`, `setting?` | Every catalog setting with its `id`, `value`, `type` (`boolean`, `number`, `choice`, `text`, `string_list`), `reach` (`account` or `this_mac`) and the `options` its picker offers, plus `dedicated_tools` (the panes with a pair of their own), `actions` and `only_in_the_settings_window`. |
| `set_app_setting` | `setting`, `value` | Change one catalog setting exactly as the pane does. A choice outside the pane's options is refused with them. Returns the setting and `changed`. Model and voice pickers change what work is billed at; ask first. |
| `run_settings_action` | `action`, `approved_spend_usd?` | One of the buttons that act once, whether or not a pane still shows it: `sync_icloud_now`, `prepare_memory_review_now`, `draw_missing_meeting_icons`, `sync_x_bookmarks`, `clear_usage_ledger_warning`, and the iCloud pane's `confirm_this_mac_holds_my_library`, `upload_library_to_icloud_again`, `apply_old_library_removals` and `keep_old_library_removals`, and `replace_icloud_library`, which only an assistant presses when you ask: it deletes iCloud's copy of your library and uploads this Mac's from the start. |
| `open_settings` | `pane?` | Open the Settings window on the Mac at one pane, for a sign-in, a payment or the sharing sheet. `plugins` and a plugin's id (`x`, `youtube`, `google_drive`, `apple_calendar`, `slack`, `linear`, `github`, `notion`, `build_your_own_plugin`) open the Plugins place on the icon strip instead, at that plugin's page, where its consent page is opened. |
| `open_in_app` | `kind`, `id?` | Show a notebook, doc, chat, source, quiz or idea in the Mac's window as a click would, `space` (the Space's All list), or `plugins` (the Plugins place, at a plugin's page when `id` names one). Listing or loading a notebook changes nothing on screen; this does. |
| `get_plugin_connections` | `include_slack_channels?` | Plugins: which of X, YouTube, Google Drive, Calendar (the Mac's), Slack, GitHub, Linear, Notion and the learner's own plugins are connected, their accounts (every X, YouTube and Google account listed on its own, a YouTube account with its import source), Slack channels, followed and hidden YouTube channels, and what connecting each takes. |
| `disconnect_plugin` | `plugin`, `account_id?` | The pane's Disconnect, Turn Off or Remove Access for `x`, `youtube`, `google_drive`, `apple_calendar`, `slack`, `github`, `linear`, `notion` or `user_plugin`. `x` takes the account as `account_id` (its user id or @username) when more than one is connected, and disconnects that account only: its bookmark sync stops and the posts already imported stay. `youtube` takes the account as `account_id` (its channel id, or its channel title) when more than one is connected, and disconnects that account only: it stops importing, while followed channels and the videos already imported stay. `linear` and `notion` take the workspace as `account_id` (its id, or its name) when more than one is connected, and revoke that workspace only. `apple_calendar` turns the Mac's Calendar off for ForeverLM; every event stays in the calendar. Ask first. |
| `set_slack_channel_enabled` | `channel_id`, `enabled`, `team_id?` | A Slack channel's switch in Plugins › Slack. |
| `get_calendar_settings` | — | Plugins › Calendar: whether the Mac's Calendar is on for ForeverLM and macOS granted access, every calendar the Mac holds (iCloud, Google, Exchange, subscriptions) with whether it takes new events (`writable`) and whether it is part of the day (`on_day`), and `new_events_calendar`, where new events go. |
