<!-- Source: docs-site/icloud-storage.md -->

# iCloud Storage & Privacy

ForeverLM keeps your whole library on your Mac and syncs it through your own iCloud account to your iPhone, iPad and the web library. ForeverLM servers do not store your library.

## Your library syncs with iCloud

Every library syncs with iCloud; there is no setting to turn it off. The first step of setup explains it, and **Settings → Data & Privacy → iCloud** shows how sync is doing.

- Your library shows on your iPhone, iPad and the web library, and you can share with a [team](/teams).
- The synced copy uses **your own iCloud storage**. The free 5 GB fills quickly once papers, books and audio sync, so we recommend the **200 GB iCloud+ plan**. You can upgrade under **System Settings → Apple Account → iCloud** on a Mac, or **Settings → [your name] → iCloud** on an iPhone.
- A Mac that is not signed in to iCloud keeps its library on the Mac and starts syncing once you sign in. Setup and **Settings → Data & Privacy → iCloud** say so, with a button to open iCloud settings.

### How much iCloud ForeverLM uses

**Settings → Data & Privacy → iCloud** shows how much of your iCloud ForeverLM's files take up, split into the PDFs of your papers, books and course material, the text of your sources, and the files in ForeverLM's iCloud Drive folder, which are mostly Text to Speech audio. It counts what ForeverLM can measure itself. Apple keeps the exact figure for each app, which **Manage…** beside it opens.

### When iCloud is full

When your iCloud storage runs out, iCloud refuses new uploads. ForeverLM shows a notice, and **Settings → Data & Privacy → iCloud** says that sync has paused. Nothing is lost, and nothing needs moving: your library already lives on your Mac's disk, and iCloud only carries the copy your other devices read. Your changes stay on your Mac and upload once there is room. Until then your iPhone, iPad, other Macs and the web library get nothing new, so free up iCloud space or move to a larger plan. The same pane says when the Mac is not signed in to iCloud, which also stops sync.

## ForeverLM's new iCloud store

ForeverLM keeps your library in its own, redesigned area of your iCloud account.
What you will notice:

- **One Mac uploads your library; the others join it.** The first Mac that syncs
  sends your library's records first and then your files. Your other Macs catch up
  with it, and the iPhone, the iPad and the web library show your library as it
  arrives.
- **Coming from an earlier ForeverLM.** ForeverLM moved to this store in October
  2026, when it began to be published under its own developer account. Your
  library stayed on your Mac: on that Mac, **Settings → Data & Privacy → iCloud**
  offers **Upload my library to iCloud again**, which sends it to the new store
  once. ForeverLM no longer reads or changes the iCloud data earlier versions
  wrote.
- **Files sync as part of the library.** Papers, books and other originals sync with
  no size limit, so a paper is on your iPhone and in the web library even when it is
  large. Your iCloud storage still pays for it, so the advice about the 200 GB plan
  stands.
- **More of your library works without your Mac.** The web library and the hosted
  assistant connection read your library from iCloud directly, so the web library
  can search inside your sources and an assistant can read them while your Mac is
  closed, once you have allowed it.
- **Your place stays yours.** Where you got to in a source, your highlights, cards,
  review results and Schedule are your own records, stored under your own account
  and never part of a team.
- **If your iCloud data is removed.** When you delete ForeverLM's data in iCloud
  settings, ForeverLM stops syncing, keeps your library on your Mac and offers to
  upload it again. It never uploads on its own after that.

## How sync works

The synced copy lives in ForeverLM's private area of your iCloud account, and Apple handles sync and encryption:

- **At rest**: encrypted on Apple's servers with keys derived from your iCloud account.
- **In transit**: encrypted over TLS between your devices and iCloud.
- **On device**: protected by your device passcode and the Secure Enclave.

ForeverLM servers do not store your source library.

## What's synced to iCloud

| Data | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Library records | Sources and their content, your Schedule, reviews and settings |
| Source files | The PDFs, books and audio of papers, books and articles you've added |
| Artifacts | Pages, explorable explanations and review session records |

On the Mac, the library itself is a SQLite database and flat files in `~/Library/Application Support/ForeverLM`. That copy stays on the Mac beside the one in iCloud.

## Team data

A [team](/teams) is a shared area inside the iCloud account of the person who
created it, shared with the members through Apple's iCloud sharing. Everything
shared into a team (a notebook you move into your own team, or a copy of what you
give a team someone else owns) is stored there, including the PDFs and book files
that travel with a shared source, so a team counts against the creator's iCloud
quota and against nobody else's. Members receive the team through their own
iCloud account; ForeverLM servers hold no copy of a team, its roster or its
content. Leaving a team removes it from your Macs; deleting one removes it, and
everything in it, for every member. Each member's reading progress, highlights, review results and Schedule stay in that
member's own private container and never enter the team's storage.

## What ForeverLM servers do not store

- Your source content
- Your book or article PDFs
- Your podcast transcripts
- Your review session history

There are two important exceptions for traffic you explicitly enable:

- **AI providers:** if you configure an API key or use an external AI assistant, the selected source content or prompts you send go to that provider.
- **Hosted MCP relay:** if you connect an external assistant through MCP, requests and responses pass through ForeverLM-operated Cloudflare infrastructure before reaching your Mac. The relay does not log or store request or response bodies, but it is a trusted relay and is not end-to-end private from ForeverLM infrastructure.

External-assistant MCP traffic passes through ForeverLM-operated Cloudflare infrastructure in transit. The relay does not log or store request or response bodies.

## Offline access

On the Mac, your library is ordinary files on its own disk, so every source opens offline, and **Optimize Mac Storage** does not remove it.

On an iPhone or iPad, a source's text and files come down from iCloud, so one you haven't opened on that device before may need a connection the first time.

## Deleting your data

Your library is on your Mac and in your own iCloud account, so you have full control:

1. **Delete the app**: removes the app from that device. On a Mac, the library in `~/Library/Application Support/ForeverLM` stays until you delete that folder. iCloud data remains until you remove it.
2. **Delete from iCloud**: go to **Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > Manage Storage > ForeverLM** and delete the data.

No need to contact ForeverLM or request data deletion. You own it all.

# ForeverLM vs the Alternatives

There are a lot of tools in the "learn and remember more" space, and they're genuinely different products: AI research assistants, flashcard apps, read-later services, note-taking systems, podcast players. This page compares them honestly — including where each one beats ForeverLM.

**Where ForeverLM sits:** it's a source tracker plus learning loop. It gathers everything you read, watch, and listen to into one Mac-native library stored in *your* iCloud, schedules your week, and verifies understanding through [AI review](/why-quizzing) — with whichever AI you already use.

The five things that most distinguish it:

1. **Your data stays yours** — a local SQLite database and files in your private iCloud container, synced through your Apple account. No uploading your library to a vendor's cloud.
2. **The app is free. MCP: 7 days free, then $19 once. No subscription.** No tiers: the whole app is open, and only connecting an outside assistant over MCP is paid. The in-app Chat runs any model on your own OpenRouter key, billed by OpenRouter at its cost with nothing added, or free models for nothing. Or connect the Claude/ChatGPT/Gemini/Grok subscription you already pay for over MCP, which is what the $19 covers.
3. **Podcasts are first-class** — follow shows, get full episode transcripts, read, listen, and get quizzed on them.
4. **Any model, no lock-in** — MCP works with every major assistant; in-app Chat takes any model through your own OpenRouter key; your files stay in open formats on your disk.
5. **Review that tests understanding** — explain the source back; an AI tutor with the full text probes your gaps. Not self-graded cards, not one-shot quizzes.

The honest trade-off: **ForeverLM is Mac-centered** (macOS 14+). Its synced iPhone experience covers reading, listening, voice, source chat, and library access, while the web library covers source search and reading. There is no Android app, and source ingestion and the full learning workflow still require an Apple device. If you need full cross-platform parity, several tools below serve you better.

## The full comparison

| Tool | Best at | Pricing | AI | Retention/review |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ForeverLM** | Learning from the sources you keep, by AI review dialogue | **Free**; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Any (MCP or in-app Chat) | AI review dialogue, scheduled |
| [NotebookLM](/compare/notebooklm) | Study material and audio overviews from uploads | Free (capped); $7.99–$99.99+/mo Google AI bundles | Gemini only | One-shot quizzes/flashcards, no tracking |
| [Heptabase](/compare/heptabase) | Card-first whiteboards for thinking | $107.88–$647.88/yr, no free tier | Credit-metered (Gemini; more on Premium) | AI tutor on $215.88/yr tier; spaced repetition unshipped |
| [Anki](/compare/anki) | Memorizing with self-graded flashcards | Free (iOS $24.99 one-time) | None built in | Self-graded flashcards, SM-2/FSRS |
| [RemNote](/compare/remnote) | Notes with flashcards and exam scheduling | Free (capped); $96–$216/yr; $395 lifetime (AI extra) | Credit-metered (OpenAI/Anthropic/Google) | Flashcards + AI quizzes/grading, exam scheduler |
| [Quizlet](/compare/quizlet) | Memorization and shared class sets | Free; Plus $35.99/yr; Plus Unlimited $44.99/yr | Built-in study and tutoring features | Flashcards, Learn mode, tests, games |
| Mochi | Simple flashcards | Free offline; Pro $5/mo for sync | Minimal (GPT text fields, Pro) | Flashcards, simple two-button or FSRS |
| [Paper](/compare/paper-ac) | Study workspace with FSRS cards and quizzes | Free during its beta; paid plans announced, not priced | Grok, GPT, Gemini | FSRS flashcards, quizzes |
| [Memo](/compare/memo-cards) | AI flashcards with FSRS and Anki export | Free plan; Pro $120/yr; Max $300/yr | Unnamed modes, no BYOK | FSRS flashcards (cloze, image occlusion), Anki export |
| [Gistr](/compare/gistr) | AI notebook for video, podcasts, PDFs and articles | Free (500 credits/mo); $8–$40/mo | By tier; frontier models from $16/mo | Quizzes; no spaced repetition |
| [Sapience](/compare/sapience) | Local, canvas-first workspace of plain text | Not published (invite-only early access) | Not stated | None stated |
| [AnythingLLM](/compare/anythingllm) | Document chat on local or hosted models | Desktop app free; cloud $50–$99/mo | 40+ providers + local models | None |
| [Speechify](/compare/speechify) | Text to speech across devices | Free tier; Premium $29/mo monthly | Built-in summaries, chat, voice assistant | No learning schedule or linked active review |
| [ElevenReader](/compare/elevenreader) | Natural narration of PDFs, EPUBs and articles | Free mobile app; ElevenLabs services priced separately | GenFM AI-hosted podcasts from your content | None: builds a listening habit |
| [Readwise Reader](/compare/readwise) | Read-later and highlight hub | $9.99–$12.99/mo after trial | Ghostreader + MCP to external assistants | Daily Review resurfacing + self-graded Mastery cards |
| [Instapaper](/compare/instapaper) | Read-later queue with Kindle and Kobo delivery | Free; Premium $6/mo or $60/yr | Narration and voice playlists on Premium | Highlights and notes only |
| [Matter](/compare/matter) | Free reading queue for articles and newsletters | Free | Reading assistance | None |
| [Raindrop.io](/compare/raindrop) | Bookmarks, collections and web archives | Free; optional Pro subscription | AI Assistant and suggestions on Pro | None |
| [Glasp](/compare/glasp) | Social highlighting and shareable notes | Free; Pro $150/yr; Unlimited $360/yr | Summaries, transcription, AI clone | Highlight resurfacing only |
| [Snipd](/compare/snipd) | Podcast capture and highlights on your phone | Free (2 ep/wk AI); Premium ~$7–12/mo by region | Proprietary pipeline | None: exports to other apps |
| [Recall](/compare/recall) | Saving and summarizing everything you read and watch | Free (10 summaries/mo); $120/yr Plus; $456/yr Max | Auto-picked; choice only on Max | Spaced-repetition quizzes (paid tier) |
| [Zotero](/compare/zotero) | Free, open-source citation management | Free; file sync $20–$120/yr above 300 MB | Community plugins | None built in |
| [Paperpile](/compare/paperpile) | Cloud reference manager for Docs and Word | $99.60–$138/yr; academic pricing 50% lower | Ask AI sends PDFs to external assistants | None built in |
| [Papers](/compare/papers) | Reference management with AI across papers | Essentials $65/yr; Pro $130/yr; 40% academic discount | Chat with 1 PDF (Essentials) or up to 20 papers (Pro) | None |
| [Mendeley](/compare/mendeley) | Elsevier's reference library with Word citations | Free with 2 GB; Plus $55/yr; Pro $110/yr; Max $165/yr | Reading Assistant; Ask My Library on Pro and Max | None |
| [EndNote](/compare/endnote) | Professional bibliographies and manuscripts | $275 license; $150 student; $125 upgrade | EndNote Research Assistant | None |
| [Elicit](/compare/elicit) | Literature discovery, screening and systematic reviews | Free; Plus $132/yr; Pro $480/yr; Scale $1,068/yr | Reports, evidence tables, extraction, paper chat | None: research synthesis |
| [SciSpace](/compare/scispace) | Academic search, PDF explanation and writing | Free with credits; Premium from $12/mo billed annually | Literature Review, Deep Review, Chat with PDF | None: research synthesis |
| [Obsidian](/compare/obsidian) | Owning your notes as local Markdown | Free; Sync $4–8/mo | Plugins, bring-your-own-key | Community plugins only |
| Reflect | Fast networked notes | $10/mo billed annually, no free tier | GPT/Claude/Gemini, BYOK, MCP beta | None |
| [LiquidText](/compare/liquidtext) | Close PDF reading and spatial excerpts | Free Basic; paid plans vary by platform and region | Not a focus | None: active reading and synthesis |
| [MarginNote](/compare/marginnote) | PDF study with mind maps and flashcards | Pro $12.99 lifetime; Max $16.99/yr or $51.99 lifetime | Credit-based summary, Q&A, OCR, cards | Flashcards, FSRS, document and mind-map recall |
| [DEVONthink](/compare/devonthink) | Private Mac document databases | Standard $99, Pro $199, Server $499 (one year of updates) | AI chat with local or external models | None |

*Pricing verified against official pages in July 2026, and in October 2026 for Paper, Memo, Gistr, Sapience and AnythingLLM; the other rows follow each tool's own page, which says when its prices were checked. Prices change — always check the vendor's site. Annual-billed rates shown where vendors advertise them.*

## More head-to-head comparisons

### NotebookLM-style study workspaces

- [Paper (paper.ac)](/compare/paper-ac): a free-in-beta study workspace with FSRS flashcards, quizzes, podcasts, and a Notion-style editor
- [Memo](/compare/memo-cards): AI flashcards with FSRS, cloze and image occlusion, practice tests, and Anki export
- [Gistr](/compare/gistr): an AI notebook for YouTube, podcasts, PDFs, and articles, with notes pinned to timestamps
- [Sapience](/compare/sapience): a local, canvas-first workspace of plain text files, in invite-only early access
- [AnythingLLM](/compare/anythingllm): open-source document chat on local or hosted models, desktop or self-hosted

### Research libraries and academic tools

- [Papers (ReadCube)](/compare/papers): reference management, citation tools, and AI across papers
- [Mendeley](/compare/mendeley): Elsevier's reference library, Reading Assistant, and Word citations
- [EndNote](/compare/endnote): professional bibliography management and manuscript workflows
- [Elicit](/compare/elicit): literature discovery, screening, evidence extraction, and systematic reviews
- [SciSpace](/compare/scispace): academic search, PDF explanation, deep reviews, and writing assistance
- [DEVONthink](/compare/devonthink): private Mac document databases, automation, search, and AI chat

### Reading, listening, and capture

- [ElevenReader](/compare/elevenreader): natural mobile narration for PDFs, EPUBs, and articles
- [Matter](/compare/matter): a focused free reading queue for articles and newsletters
- [Instapaper](/compare/instapaper): read later, AI voice playlists, Kindle, Kobo, and permanent archives
- [Raindrop.io](/compare/raindrop): bookmarks, collections, highlights, web archives, and AI assistance
- [Glasp](/compare/glasp): social highlighting, YouTube and Kindle capture, summaries, and exports

### Studying and deep reading

- [Quizlet](/compare/quizlet): flashcards, Learn mode, tests, and shared course material
- [LiquidText](/compare/liquidtext): close PDF reading, spatial excerpt workspaces, and collaboration
- [MarginNote](/compare/marginnote): PDF study, mind maps, flashcards, OCR, and AI assistance

## Broader buying guides

- [Best NotebookLM alternatives](/compare/best-notebooklm-alternatives)
- [Best apps for listening to PDFs](/compare/best-pdf-listening-apps)
- [Best AI research library apps](/compare/best-ai-research-library-apps)

## Compare by what you're optimizing for

**"I want an AI to study my documents with"** → [NotebookLM](/compare/notebooklm) is the big-tech default; ForeverLM keeps the data in your iCloud, works with any model, and adds the retention loop NotebookLM lacks.

**"I want NotebookLM with flashcards built in"** → [Paper](/compare/paper-ac) (free while in beta) or [Memo](/compare/memo-cards) (FSRS cards with Anki export, on every platform). ForeverLM keeps the library in your iCloud, fills it on its own, and reviews by dialogue as well as cards.

**"I want my documents and models to stay on my machine"** → [AnythingLLM](/compare/anythingllm) runs document chat on local models, on any desktop or your own server. ForeverLM keeps the library in your iCloud and adds the learning loop AnythingLLM doesn't have.

**"I want to remember facts for an exam"** → [Anki](/compare/anki) (free, everywhere) or [RemNote](/compare/remnote) (integrated notes + exam scheduling). ForeverLM is better when the goal is understanding sources, not memorizing card decks.

**"I highlight everything I read"** → [Readwise](/compare/readwise) is the highlight hub. ForeverLM tracks the full sources instead and tests you on them.

**"I want everything read aloud"** → [Speechify](/compare/speechify) is the cross-platform TTS specialist. ForeverLM also reads articles, papers, and books aloud, then keeps the audio connected to Schedule, Chat, and review.

**"I want the most natural mobile voices"** → [ElevenReader](/compare/elevenreader) is a strong specialist. ForeverLM is better when narration needs to stay attached to research and review.

**"I manage academic papers"** → [Zotero](/compare/zotero) for the best free, open-source citation workflow; [Paperpile](/compare/paperpile) for a polished cloud workflow around Google Docs, Word, and team libraries. ForeverLM is for reading, listening, chatting across, and reviewing the papers—not replacing cite-while-you-write.

**"I am running a literature review"** → [Elicit](/compare/elicit) for structured screening and extraction, or [SciSpace](/compare/scispace) for broader academic search and deep review. ForeverLM is the library for what you decide to keep and learn.

**"I need citations and AI across my paper library"** → [Papers](/compare/papers), [Mendeley](/compare/mendeley), or [EndNote](/compare/endnote). Each is stronger at formal bibliography workflows; ForeverLM is stronger across source formats and active learning.

**"I want to own my notes forever"** → [Obsidian](/compare/obsidian) for writing your own notes; ForeverLM applies the same local-first philosophy to sources and review instead of notes.

**"I think on a canvas"** → [Heptabase](/compare/heptabase) has the most mature card-first whiteboards. ForeverLM now has an ideas-first Canvas over your library (in beta releases), and it ships the review loop Heptabase still has on its roadmap.

**"I annotate PDFs intensively"** → [LiquidText](/compare/liquidtext) for spatial excerpting or [MarginNote](/compare/marginnote) for mind maps and flashcards. ForeverLM is better when the sources extend beyond documents.

**"I learn from podcasts"** → [Snipd](/compare/snipd) for capture while listening on your phone; ForeverLM for full transcripts, scheduling, and being quizzed afterwards on your Mac.

**"I save everything and want AI to organize it"** → [Recall](/compare/recall) is the closest cousin: local-first, many source types, spaced-repetition quizzes at $120/yr. ForeverLM differs on depth of review, automatic ingestion, podcasts-as-transcripts, iCloud sync, and a free app (MCP is $19 once) instead of a required yearly subscription.

## The pricing picture, over three years

A subscription bills you every year whether or not you opened the app. Here's what three years costs on each tool's typical paid tier:

| Tool | 3-year cost (typical paid tier, annual billing) |
|---|---|
| Anki | $0–$24.99 |
| **ForeverLM** | **$0** for the app, **$19** once if you add MCP; plus OpenRouter usage at cost on your own key |
| Mochi Pro | ~$180 |
| Reflect | $360 |
| Readwise Full | ~$360 |
| Recall Plus | $360 |
| RemNote Pro + AI | ~$648 |
| Heptabase Premium | ~$648 |
| NotebookLM via Google AI Pro | ~$720 |

ForeverLM is the one row without a fixed total, and that's the honest answer: the app is free, MCP is $19 once, and the AI depends on the route you pick. Two routes, and you can mix them. The in-app Chat runs any model on your own OpenRouter key, which OpenRouter bills at its cost with nothing added by ForeverLM; its free models cost nothing. Driving ForeverLM over MCP from a Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok subscription you *already* pay for is what the $19 covers, and the subscription is already in your budget. In the app, some tokens also go to background work (transcript cleanup, paper metadata extraction) on the same key, with the model configurable per task. The app keeps a to-the-cent ledger of every conversation.

## Try it

ForeverLM is free, and MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once: [get it for Mac](https://foreverlm.com) and point it at your reading list. If you're on Windows or Android, we'd honestly point you at Recall or RemNote today.

# Best NotebookLM (Gemini Notebook) Alternatives in 2026

Google renamed NotebookLM to **Gemini Notebook** in July 2026, and it now lives at notebook.google.com. It is excellent at turning a bounded collection of sources into grounded answers, summaries, quizzes, reports, and Audio and Video Overviews. The best alternative depends on what feels limiting: isolated notebooks, source caps (50 per notebook free, 300 on Google AI Pro), Gemini-only AI, Google's cloud, usage that refills every five hours up to a weekly cap, weak citation management, or the lack of a long-term learning workflow.

There is no universal replacement. These are the strongest options by job.

## Quick comparison

| App | Best for | Main advantage over NotebookLM | Main trade-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ForeverLM** | A private library you intend to learn from | Local iCloud library, any model, podcasts, Schedule, and saved review | Full workflow is Mac-centered |
| [Elicit](/compare/elicit) | Systematic literature reviews | Searches, screens, and extracts evidence from scholarly literature | Research workflow rather than a personal knowledge library |
| [SciSpace](/compare/scispace) | Academic discovery and PDF explanation | Literature search, deep review, and writing tools | Cloud service focused mainly on papers |
| [Papers](/compare/papers) | Reference management plus AI | Citations, discovery, shared libraries, and chat across selected papers | Annual subscription and paper-centered scope |
| [DEVONthink](/compare/devonthink) | Private Mac document archives | Local databases, automation, OCR, and broad file management | More setup and no built-in learning loop |
| [Recall](/compare/recall) | Automatic AI organization | Many source types, knowledge graph, and quizzes | Paid tiers and vendor-managed sync |
| [Heptabase](/compare/heptabase) | Visual thinking | Whiteboards, cards, and spatial synthesis | No podcast pipeline; meaningful AI sits on higher tiers |
| [Readwise Reader](/compare/readwise) | Read-later and highlights | Excellent capture, reading, export, and resurfacing | Subscription and cloud-centered library |
| [Paper](/compare/paper-ac) | A free study workspace | FSRS flashcards, quizzes, two-host podcasts, slides, and a Notion-style editor, free in beta | Its cloud only; paid plans not yet priced |
| [Memo](/compare/memo-cards) | Flashcards for exams | FSRS cards with cloze and image occlusion, Anki export, every platform | Its cloud; usage on an unquantified "energy" meter |
| [AnythingLLM](/compare/anythingllm) | Fully local document chat | Open source, any model including local ones, desktop or self-hosted | No learning features; no sync between devices |
| [Gistr](/compare/gistr) | YouTube and podcast notes | Notes pinned to timestamps, cheap tiers, Android | Credit tiers; no spaced repetition |
| [Sapience](/compare/sapience) | A local canvas of plain files | Folders drawn as canvases, Obsidian vaults, AI memory as notes | Invite-only early access; little published |

## Best overall for long-term learning: ForeverLM

Both work in notebooks, but a NotebookLM notebook holds its own uploads, while a ForeverLM notebook draws on one library. Articles, papers, books, podcasts, videos, courses, and meetings accumulate in one local database, and a notebook points at the sources it uses instead of each notebook being uploaded in isolation.

The difference is clearest after the first answer. A source can be assigned to a day, read or heard, discussed with any supported model, and reviewed through a dialogue that asks you to explain it back. That review remains linked to the source. If your goal is to remember what you consume rather than generate artifacts from it, this is the strongest alternative. Moving over is one paste: a Gemini Notebook's link brings its sources, chats and notes into ForeverLM as a notebook ([Importing a Gemini Notebook](/studio#importing-a-gemini-notebook)).

## Best free study workspace: Paper

Paper does most of what Gemini Notebook does, plus FSRS flashcards, quizzes, two-host podcasts up to an hour and slide decks, inside a Notion-style editor, and it is free while in beta. Your library lives on its cloud, and its paid plans are announced but not priced.

## Best for flashcards and exams: Memo

Memo began as PDF2Anki, and cards are still its strength: FSRS scheduling, cloze and image-occlusion cards, practice tests, and export to Anki, on web, Mac, Windows, Linux and iOS. Choose it when the job is memorizing for an exam.

## Best fully local: AnythingLLM

AnythingLLM is open source and runs document chat on any of 40-odd model providers or on local models, so nothing has to leave your machine. It is a retrieval tool rather than a learning one: no flashcards, quizzes or schedule.

## Best for academic evidence: Elicit or SciSpace

Choose Elicit when you need a structured literature-review process: find papers, apply screening criteria, extract fields, and produce evidence tables. Choose SciSpace when you want a broader academic toolkit for discovery, deep reviews, PDF explanation, citations, and writing.

Neither is a direct replacement for a lifetime personal library. They are strongest before and during synthesis. ForeverLM is strongest after you have selected what matters.

## Best for citations: Papers

Papers combines a professional reference manager with PDF chat, cross-paper questions, search, related-paper discovery, collaboration, and cite-while-you-write tools. It is the better choice when the final deliverable is a manuscript or shared lab bibliography.

## Best for privacy and document control: DEVONthink

DEVONthink is the power-user choice for a private Mac archive. It handles documents, scans, mail, feeds, OCR, automation, and local databases with more depth than any AI-first research tool. Pick it when information management is the priority and you are comfortable designing your own workflow.

## How to choose

- Choose **ForeverLM** to keep, discuss, listen to, schedule, and remember sources across formats.
- Choose **Paper** for a free study workspace with flashcards and podcasts.
- Choose **Memo** for exam flashcards that export to Anki.
- Choose **AnythingLLM** for document chat on local models.
- Choose **Elicit** for systematic reviews and structured evidence extraction.
- Choose **SciSpace** for academic discovery and PDF explanation.
- Choose **Papers** for citations, shared scholarly libraries, and AI across papers.
- Choose **DEVONthink** for a private, automated Mac document archive.
- Stay with **Gemini Notebook** if Gemini, generated artifacts, and easy cloud notebooks already solve the job.

For the direct product breakdown, see [ForeverLM vs NotebookLM](/compare/notebooklm).

# Best Apps for Listening to PDFs in 2026

The best PDF listening app depends on what happens around the audio. Some apps are voice readers. Some are accessibility tools. Others keep the paper inside a research or learning workflow so you can ask questions and return to the evidence.

## Quick comparison

| App | Best for | What happens after listening? | Platforms |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ForeverLM** | Papers and articles that belong to ongoing research | Chat, notebooks, Schedule, and source-linked review | Mac and synced iPhone access |
| [Speechify](/compare/speechify) | Maximum voice and input breadth | Summaries and chat, without a learning schedule | Web, Mac, Windows, iOS, Android |
| [ElevenReader](/compare/elevenreader) | Natural mobile voices and generated podcasts | Mobile listening library and reading habit | iOS and Android |
| [Instapaper](/compare/instapaper) | A read-later queue with AI voice playlists | Highlights, notes, archive, Kindle, and Kobo delivery | Web, iOS, Android, e-readers |
| [Readwise Reader](/compare/readwise) | Articles, highlights, feeds, and resurfacing | Highlight export, Daily Review, and Mastery cards | Web, desktop, iOS, Android |
| [Matter](/compare/matter) | Simple free article listening | Clean reading queue, feeds, and highlights | iPhone, iPad, web |

## Best for research and learning: ForeverLM

ForeverLM cleans papers for narration, can skip reference clutter, and offers every speech model OpenRouter serves, free ones included. More importantly, the audio stays attached to the source.

You can pause and ask about a claim, compare the paper with another source, add it to a notebook, and finish with a review that tests your explanation. That makes it the strongest choice when listening is a way to study rather than only a way to consume text.

## Best specialist voice reader: Speechify

Speechify accepts a wide range of documents and scans, offers a large voice catalog, works across most major platforms, and supports very high playback speeds. It is the safer choice for accessibility, Android and Windows support, or anyone whose primary requirement is “read almost anything aloud.”

## Best mobile voices: ElevenReader

ElevenReader brings ElevenLabs voices to PDFs, EPUBs, articles, scans, and pasted text on phones and tablets. GenFM can also turn imported material into a conversational audio show. Choose it for natural narration and mobile convenience, especially on Android.

## Best read-later audio queue: Instapaper or Readwise Reader

Instapaper Premium combines AI voice playlists with a permanent archive, PDF support, Kindle digests, and Kobo integration. Readwise Reader is stronger when highlights, newsletters, feeds, YouTube, exports, and daily resurfacing are part of the same workflow.

## What to look for

- **PDF cleanup:** Does it skip headers, footers, equations, citations, and reference sections intelligently?
- **Voice options:** Are voices on-device, local, cloud-based, or tied to one subscription?
- **Position sync:** Can you move between reading and listening without losing your place?
- **Evidence access:** Can you return from audio to the exact page or source passage?
- **Learning workflow:** Does completion lead to notes, chat, scheduling, or active recall?
- **Privacy:** Does the PDF remain local, or must it be uploaded to a vendor service?

Choose the app based on the surrounding workflow, not a voice demo alone.

# Best AI Research Library Apps in 2026

An AI research library should do more than accept a few PDFs in a chat window. The useful distinction is what the product treats as permanent: a notebook, a bibliography, a document archive, a set of highlights, or a learning history.

## Quick comparison

| App | Library model | AI strength | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ForeverLM** | Local multi-format library in private iCloud | Cross-source Chat, MCP operations, and active review | Researchers and lifelong learners who want to retain sources |
| [Papers](/compare/papers) | Hosted scholarly reference library | PDF chat, selected-library chat, and AI search | Academic teams and citation-heavy workflows |
| [Mendeley](/compare/mendeley) | Elsevier-hosted reference library | Reading Assistant, Ask My Library, experiment comparison | Researchers using Word and Elsevier services |
| [DEVONthink](/compare/devonthink) | Local Mac document databases | AI chat plus powerful search and automation | Private document archives and advanced workflows |
| [NotebookLM](/compare/notebooklm) | Isolated hosted notebooks | Grounded Q&A and generated study artifacts | Fast analysis of bounded source collections |
| [Elicit](/compare/elicit) | Cloud research notebooks and evidence tables | Literature search, screening, and extraction | Systematic reviews |
| [SciSpace](/compare/scispace) | Cloud academic workspace | Discovery, deep review, PDF explanation, writing | End-to-end academic research assistance |
| [Zotero](/compare/zotero) | Local-first reference library | Community AI plugins | Open-source citation management |
| [Recall](/compare/recall) | AI-organized knowledge graph | Automatic summaries, relationships, and quizzes | People who want low-effort organization |

## Best personal research library: ForeverLM

ForeverLM keeps full sources across formats instead of reducing research to papers or highlights. A notebook can hold a paper, the author's podcast appearance, a book chapter, a lecture, and your meeting notes. Chat can compare them, and an MCP assistant can retrieve material, manage the schedule, or save a completed review.

Its defining feature is the learning record. Sources move from pending to scheduled to reviewed, with the review transcript linked back to what was covered. The trade-off is platform reach: the full workflow is Mac-centered.

## Best academic reference library: Papers

Papers is the strongest choice when bibliography quality, related-paper discovery, shared libraries, annotations, and cite-while-you-write are essential. Its Pro AI can ask questions across a selected set of papers and point back to evidence. ForeverLM is broader; Papers is deeper at formal scholarly production.

## Best free citation manager: Zotero

Zotero remains the open-source default for capturing references, repairing metadata, organizing attachments, and citing in manuscripts. Community plugins can add AI, but the experience is less integrated and less predictable than a product designed around AI from the start.

## Best private document archive: DEVONthink

DEVONthink is ideal when the library includes email, scans, records, feeds, office files, and long-lived document databases. Its automation and search are exceptional. It is an information manager first, so users must design their own learning and review process.

## Best research agent: Elicit or SciSpace

Elicit is the better fit for systematic evidence workflows. SciSpace is broader across discovery, explanation, deep reviews, and academic writing. Both are cloud research services rather than private lifetime libraries.

## Evaluation checklist

- Does it store complete sources or only notes, embeddings, and highlights?
- Can AI answer across the whole library and show its evidence?
- Can you choose the model or export to another assistant?
- Are citation and manuscript tools required?
- Does it include articles, audio, video, and books as well as PDFs?
- Where are files stored, and can you leave with them?
- Does the system track what you understood, not just what you saved?

The best research library is the one whose permanent object matches your work: citations, documents, notebooks, or understanding.

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/notebooklm.md -->

# ForeverLM vs NotebookLM (Gemini Notebook)

NotebookLM, renamed **Gemini Notebook** in July 2026 and now at notebook.google.com, is Google's source-grounded AI assistant: upload documents into a notebook, chat with them, and generate impressive artifacts — most famously the podcast-style Audio Overviews. It's polished, generous at the free tier, and backed by Gemini. But it's built for *generating study material*, not for *learning over time* — and everything you put in lives on Google's servers, processed only by Google's models.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | NotebookLM |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free tier (capped); higher limits via Google AI bundles: $7.99/mo Plus, $19.99/mo Pro, $99.99+/mo Ultra |
| **AI costs** | Your own OpenRouter key, billed by OpenRouter at cost with nothing added, for any model in Chat (free models cost nothing); or an AI subscription you already pay for, over MCP | Included, but capped per day/tier (chats, overviews, quizzes) |
| **Platforms** | Native macOS app (macOS 14+) | Web + iOS + Android apps; no desktop app |
| **Data storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container | Google's servers — every source must be uploaded |
| **AI models** | Any MCP-compatible AI (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok), or any model in-app through your own OpenRouter key | Gemini only, no model picker, no bring-your-own-key |
| **Source ingestion** | Automatic: Safari reading list, Apple Podcasts, PDFs, papers, books, YouTube, X posts | Manual upload per notebook (plus Drive links and Deep Research discovery) |
| **Podcasts** | Follow shows, full episode transcripts as sources | Not supported (it *generates* podcast-style audio; it can't ingest your podcast feed) |
| **Knowledge accumulation** | Notebooks drawing on one persistent library — a source is added once and can be in any number of notebooks | Isolated notebooks with per-notebook source caps (50–600 by tier) |
| **Retention** | Cards you keep from your sources, brought back on a spaced schedule across every notebook, plus review sessions with saved history | One-shot flashcards/quizzes — no spaced repetition, no tracking over time |
| **Export** | Files stay on your Mac; SQLite you can open | Notes to Google Docs/Sheets, audio as WAV; notebook structure and chats effectively locked in |

*Prices verified July 2026, limits October 2026. Google reshuffles these often: since September 2026 a personal account's usage refills every five hours up to a weekly cap instead of fixed daily counts. Check [Google's limits page](https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16213268) for current numbers.*

## Pricing: free-but-capped bundles vs your own AI key

Gemini Notebook itself is free, with up to 100 notebooks of 50 sources each and usage that refills every five hours up to a weekly cap; Google no longer publishes the numbers for personal accounts. Raising the limits means a Google AI plan — **$199.99/yr for AI Pro**, with 300 sources per notebook and four times the standard usage — that bundles much more than Gemini Notebook, and the limits still exist, just higher. You're paying a flat annual fee for permission to do more, not for what you did.

ForeverLM is **free** and has no daily caps of its own; only MCP is paid, **7 days free, then $19 once** (no subscription). There are no tiers to upgrade through: bring your own OpenRouter key, pick any model in the in-app Chat, and OpenRouter bills you at its cost with nothing added by ForeverLM, or use free models and pay nothing. Or connect the Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok subscription you already pay for over MCP: that subscription covers the inference, and ForeverLM charges nothing per request. In the app, a little also goes to background work like transcript cleanup, billed the same way; search embeddings are made on your Mac, for free. Every conversation's cost is shown to the cent.

## Where NotebookLM is better

- **Audio and Video Overviews.** The generated podcast-style discussions are best-in-class and genuinely delightful. A ForeverLM notebook's audio overview is one narrator reading a script written from its sources (a deep dive, a brief or a critique), and Text to Speech reads you the *actual source*; there is no two-host show, and ForeverLM's videos are short explainer films of one concept rather than a video overview of a notebook.
- **Genuinely free AI, forever, with no key.** A Google account is the only requirement, and within the daily caps the free tier costs nothing indefinitely. ForeverLM is free too, and its built-in AI runs on your own OpenRouter key: free models cost nothing, paid ones cost what OpenRouter charges.
- **Cross-platform.** Web, iOS, and Android apps. ForeverLM is Mac-only today.
- **Google-scale polish** and Drive/Docs integration if you live in Workspace.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **Your data never leaves your control.** ForeverLM's library is a local SQLite database plus files in your private iCloud container, synced through your Apple account. NotebookLM requires uploading everything to Google, with no local copy and a weak export story.
- **Any AI, not one AI.** ForeverLM works with Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, or any model through your own OpenRouter key — use the subscription you already pay for, switch anytime. NotebookLM is Gemini-only with no model visibility at all.
- **A learning system, not a generator.** NotebookLM produces flashcards and quizzes as one-shot artifacts — nothing schedules review, nothing tracks what you've mastered. ForeverLM keeps the cards you choose, brings them back on a spaced schedule across every notebook, runs review sessions where you explain sources back and the AI probes your gaps, and keeps the full review history per source. See [Why Quizzing?](/why-quizzing)
- **One library for life, under every notebook.** NotebookLM silos knowledge into notebooks capped at 50–600 sources, each with its own uploads. A ForeverLM notebook draws on a single accumulating library — five years of reading, listening, and studying in one searchable place — so a paper is added once, can be in any number of notebooks, and a notebook's Add sources searches the whole library first.
- **Real podcast support.** Follow your shows, get full transcripts, read/listen/review. NotebookLM can't subscribe to a podcast feed at all.
- **Sources flow in automatically** from your Safari reading list, Apple Podcasts, and reference managers — no per-notebook uploading ritual.
- **Your notebooks come with you.** Paste a notebook's link into ForeverLM and it becomes a ForeverLM notebook: its sources, its chats and its notes, kept in your own library. See [Importing a Gemini Notebook](/studio#importing-a-gemini-notebook).

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Gemini Notebook** for ad-hoc research sprints: dump twenty documents into a notebook, chat with them, generate an Audio Overview for the commute — especially if you're not on a Mac, or you'd rather have AI that stays free indefinitely inside its caps than AI you meter.

Choose **ForeverLM** if learning is ongoing, not one-off: you want everything you read, watch, and hear accumulating in a library *you* own, reviewed on a schedule, with proof you actually understood it — using whichever AI you already trust.

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/heptabase.md -->

# ForeverLM vs Heptabase

Heptabase is a visual thinking tool: whiteboards and cards for mapping out complex topics, with PDF annotation, a Zotero workflow, and a growing credit-based AI layer including an AI tutor. It's one of the best sense-making canvases available. ForeverLM shares its local-first values, and it now has a Canvas too, but its centre of gravity is different: it tracks the sources you consume and verifies, through AI review, that you understood them. Its Canvas is where you lay out your own ideas over that library.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Heptabase |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | No free tier. Pro $107.88/yr; Premium $215.88/yr; Premium+ $647.88/yr (monthly billing higher) |
| **AI costs** | Your own OpenRouter key, billed by OpenRouter at cost with nothing added, for any model in Chat (free models cost nothing); or an AI subscription you already pay for, over MCP | Credit-metered: 100 credits/mo on Pro (Gemini only), 1,800 on Premium; no bring-your-own-key |
| **AI tutor** | Review with any MCP assistant or in-app Chat — no tier required | AI tutor requires Premium ($215.88/yr) |
| **Platforms** | Native macOS app (macOS 14+) | Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS, Android, web |
| **Data storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container, CloudKit sync | Local-first database; sync via Heptabase's AWS cloud (US, not end-to-end encrypted) |
| **Source ingestion** | Automatic: Safari reading list, Apple Podcasts, PDFs, papers, books, YouTube, X posts | Manual: PDF import, web clipper, YouTube transcripts, Zotero, Readwise |
| **Podcasts** | Follow shows, full episode transcripts | Not supported |
| **Canvas** | Ideas-first Canvas over the whole library: Ideas, regions inside regions, arrows, sources as evidence (in beta releases) | Mature card-first whiteboards: cards, sections, mind maps, nested whiteboards |
| **Spaced review** | Weekly Schedule + saved review history per source | On the roadmap, not shipped |
| **Export** | Files on your Mac; SQLite you can open | Strong: full Markdown + JSON export, automatic daily local backups |

*Pricing verified July 2026 (Heptabase's May 2026 price list) — check [heptabase.com/pricing](https://heptabase.com/pricing) for current numbers.*

## Pricing: credit tiers vs your own AI key

Heptabase has **no free tier** and its AI is credit-metered. The plan most learners would want — unlimited PDFs plus the AI tutor and non-Gemini models — is Premium at **$215.88/yr billed annually** ($23.99 month-to-month). Heavy AI use points to Premium+ at $647.88/yr. The credits are Heptabase-denominated, they reset every month whether you used them or not, and there's no bring-your-own-key escape from the meter.

ForeverLM is **free**, with no subscription and no tiers to pick between: the whole app is open, with every model on your own OpenRouter key. Only MCP is paid: **7 days free, then $19 once**. Two ways to use AI, mixable: any model in the in-app Chat on your OpenRouter key, billed by OpenRouter at its cost with nothing added by ForeverLM (free models cost nothing); or the Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok subscription you already pay for, connected over MCP. Your subscription covers the inference, and ForeverLM charges nothing per request. The in-app route also spends a little on background work (transcript cleanup, paper metadata extraction), billed the same way, with the model configurable per task. The app records every token and shows costs to the cent.

The three-year comparison is lopsided in a way that's worth stating plainly: Heptabase Premium is ~$648 before you've done anything, while ForeverLM is free, or $19 once if you also want MCP, plus whatever OpenRouter bills your own key for what you use (nothing on free models).

## Where Heptabase is better

- **A mature, card-first whiteboard.** Heptabase is built around its whiteboards: years of polish, cards you write once and place on many boards, nested whiteboards, mind maps, and journals. ForeverLM's Canvas is newer (in beta releases today) and ideas-first: your Ideas, regions and arrows on one plane over the library, with sources hanging off them as evidence, rather than a board of cards you write.
- **Cross-platform.** Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS, Android, and web. ForeverLM is Mac-centered, with an iPhone app and a web library for reading and listening.
- **Note-taking depth.** Heptabase is a full PKM app; ForeverLM deliberately isn't one.
- **Academic PDF workflow.** Annotation, OCR parsing (Premium), and Zotero integration are strong for paper-heavy research.
- **Exemplary export.** Automatic daily Markdown + JSON backups on your own disk set the standard for exit-friendliness.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **The retention loop exists today.** Heptabase's spaced repetition has been on the roadmap for years and remains unshipped; its AI tutor is a guided-session feature on the $215.88/yr tier. ForeverLM ships the whole loop (weekly Schedule, review, per-source understanding history) in the one app, with no tier to climb. See [Why Quizzing?](/why-quizzing)
- **No credit tiers.** Credits are a second subscription inside the subscription, denominated in Heptabase's own currency and refilled monthly whether you need it or not. ForeverLM uses real provider costs instead: in-app Chat runs on your own OpenRouter key at OpenRouter's cost with nothing added, or on free models for nothing; or drive it over MCP from an assistant you already subscribe to. No feature is gated behind which tier you're on.
- **Sources arrive automatically.** Heptabase ingestion is pull-based: clip, import, drag. ForeverLM discovers sources from your Safari reading list, Apple Podcasts follows, and reference managers.
- **Podcasts.** Full episode transcripts as first-class study sources; Heptabase has no podcast pipeline.
- **Model freedom at every price.** Heptabase locks non-Gemini models behind Premium. ForeverLM works with Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok from day one.
- **Sync through your own cloud.** Both apps are local-first, but Heptabase syncs through its US-based AWS (readable by the vendor); ForeverLM syncs through your personal iCloud account, and its servers never store your library.
- **A canvas wired to its sources.** On ForeverLM's Canvas a paper can show only its figures, a passage card opens the paper at that passage, a box drawn around a figure in the Reader drags straight onto the board, and Claude or ChatGPT can lay a canvas out over MCP.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Heptabase** if your bottleneck is *making sense* of complex material and you think in cards you write and arrange: its whiteboards are the most mature. Or if you need Windows, Linux, or Android.

Choose **ForeverLM** if your bottleneck is *remembering* what you consume: you want automatic source capture (podcasts included), a scheduled review loop that exists today, and AI costs that track what you actually used instead of climbing credit tiers.

Some people use both: Heptabase to map a topic while learning it, ForeverLM to track the sources and verify the understanding sticks.

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/anki.md -->

# ForeverLM vs Anki

Anki is the standard-bearer of spaced repetition: free, open source, fifteen-plus years old, and beloved by med students and language learners. If your goal is memorizing thousands of discrete facts, Anki is hard to beat. ForeverLM aims at a different target: understanding and retaining the *sources* you consume — articles, papers, podcasts, books — by explaining them back to an AI tutor rather than flipping self-graded cards.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Anki |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free on desktop and Android; AnkiMobile for iOS is $24.99 one-time |
| **AI costs** | Your own OpenRouter key, billed by OpenRouter at cost with nothing added, for any model in Chat (free models cost nothing); or an AI subscription you already pay for, over MCP | No built-in AI; desktop-only community add-ons, bring-your-own-key |
| **Platforms** | Native macOS app (macOS 14+) | Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, web review |
| **Data storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container | Local SQLite; free AnkiWeb sync or self-hosted sync |
| **Source ingestion** | Automatic: articles, papers, podcasts, books, YouTube, X posts | None — cards only; you author or import decks |
| **Review method** | Review dialogue: explain it back, AI probes gaps | Self-graded flashcards (Again/Hard/Good/Easy), SM-2 or FSRS |
| **Adaptivity** | AI rephrases, follows up on weak spots, asks *why* | Cards are static; scheduling adapts, questions don't |
| **Export** | Files on your Mac; SQLite you can open | Excellent: .apkg/.colpkg/plain text, open format |

*Pricing verified July 2026 — see [apps.ankiweb.net](https://apps.ankiweb.net/).*

## Pricing: neither one has to be a subscription

This is one comparison where the funding models nearly agree: neither app has to bill you every month. Anki is free (or $24.99 once on iOS). ForeverLM is free too; only MCP, the connection for an outside assistant, costs anything: 7 days free, then $19 once, with no subscription. AI is a separate bill you control: bring your own OpenRouter key and pay models at cost, or use free models and pay nothing.

There are two ways to use AI, and you can mix them. Use the in-app Chat with any model you like on your own OpenRouter key, and OpenRouter bills you at its cost with nothing added by ForeverLM. Or connect the Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok subscription you already pay for over MCP: your subscription covers the thinking, and ForeverLM charges nothing per request. Anki, of course, charges nothing to run at all, because it has no AI to bill you for.

## Where Anki is better

- **Cost and platform reach.** Free almost everywhere — Windows, Linux, and Android included — and it will never send you an AI bill, because there's no AI in it.
- **Rote memorization at scale.** For vocabulary, anatomy, drug names, dates — thousands of discrete facts — self-graded flashcards with FSRS scheduling are the proven tool.
- **Shared decks.** Decades of community decks (med school, languages) you can download and start reviewing today.
- **Total ownership.** Open source, local files, self-hostable sync. The strongest possible longevity story.
- **Zero AI dependency.** Works offline forever, no API keys, no cloud anything.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **Understanding, not recognition.** Anki asks "do you remember this card?" and you grade yourself. ForeverLM asks you to *explain the concept from scratch* while an AI tutor with the full source text checks your explanation, probes gaps, and asks follow-ups. Static cards can't probe a gap they don't know about — see [Why Quizzing?](/why-quizzing)
- **No card authoring.** Anki's hidden cost is the hours spent making good cards. ForeverLM skips the authoring step entirely: the source itself is the study material, and questions are generated fresh from it every session.
- **Sources flow in automatically.** Safari reading list, Apple Podcasts follows, PDFs, papers, books, YouTube — ForeverLM tracks what you actually consume. Anki has no concept of a source.
- **A study planner, not just a review queue.** The weekly Schedule assigns sources to days and tracks completion and review history — closer to a study system than a card queue.
- **Modern native Mac experience.** Reader, Text to Speech, in-app Chat — versus Anki's famously dated UI.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Anki** for high-volume rote memorization — exams with thousands of facts, language vocabulary — especially on Windows, Linux, or Android, or if you want a zero-cost, zero-cloud tool that will outlive every startup.

Choose **ForeverLM** if your problem is the flood of articles, papers, podcasts, and books you consume and forget — and you want to be tested on real understanding without spending evenings authoring flashcards.

They're complementary: several ForeverLM users keep Anki for pure memorization and use ForeverLM as the comprehension loop over their reading.

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/remnote.md -->

# ForeverLM vs RemNote

RemNote is an all-in-one student platform: notes that auto-generate flashcards, PDF annotation, exam schedulers, and a growing AI layer. It's arguably the most feature-complete study app for coursework. ForeverLM is narrower and more opinionated: track every source you consume, schedule it, and verify understanding through an AI review dialogue — with your data in your own iCloud and the AI you already pay for.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | RemNote |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free tier (capped); Pro $96/yr; Pro + AI $216/yr; $395 lifetime (AI still +$10/mo) |
| **AI costs** | Your own OpenRouter key, billed by OpenRouter at cost with nothing added, for any model in Chat (free models cost nothing); or an AI subscription you already pay for, over MCP | Metered AI credits included in tiers (1,000/mo on Pro, 20,000/mo on Pro + AI); no bring-your-own-key |
| **Platforms** | Native macOS app (macOS 14+) | Web, Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS, Android |
| **Data storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container | RemNote's cloud by default; local-only knowledge bases on desktop lose sync |
| **Source ingestion** | Automatic: articles, papers, podcasts, books, YouTube, X posts | PDFs, slides, lecture recordings, web clipper — no podcasts or YouTube |
| **Review method** | Review dialogue with an AI tutor | Spaced-repetition flashcards (SM-2/FSRS), AI-generated cards, AI quizzes and grading |
| **Model choice** | Any MCP-compatible AI (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok), or any model in-app through your own OpenRouter key | OpenAI/Anthropic/Google behind RemNote's credit system |
| **Export** | Files on your Mac; SQLite you can open | Markdown/JSON export; rich structure and scheduling history don't survive cleanly |

*Pricing verified July 2026 — check [remnote.com/pricing](https://www.remnote.com/pricing) for current numbers.*

## Pricing: subscription + credits vs a free app + your own AI key

Meaningful AI use on RemNote costs **$216/yr** (Pro + AI), and even the $395 lifetime license excludes AI credits — AI stays a $10/mo add-on forever. The credits are RemNote-denominated: you can't bring your own key or your existing ChatGPT/Claude subscription.

ForeverLM is **free**, and its AI takes two routes, mixable: any model in the in-app Chat, on your own OpenRouter key, billed by OpenRouter at its cost with nothing added (free models cost nothing); or drive ForeverLM over MCP from the Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok subscription you're already paying for. The inference is on that subscription, and MCP is the one paid part of ForeverLM: 7 days free, then $19 once. Per-conversation costs in the app are shown to the cent.

Three years of RemNote Pro + AI is ~$648 committed up front. ForeverLM's equivalent number is $0 for the app, or $19 once if you add MCP, plus whatever OpenRouter bills for the AI you chose to run. That is the honest answer, not a dodge: usage is the one line item you control directly.

## Where RemNote is better

- **Course-based studying.** Annotating lecture slides and PDFs, auto-deriving flashcards from your note outline, exam schedulers that compress reviews before a test date — for a semester with exams, RemNote is purpose-built.
- **Every platform.** Web, Windows, Linux, Android, iOS. ForeverLM is Mac-only.
- **Integrated notes.** RemNote is a real outliner/note-taking app; ForeverLM deliberately isn't.
- **Usable free tier.** Unlimited notes, flashcards, and devices for $0 (with caps on PDFs and AI).
- **Built-in flashcard scheduling.** If you want classic spaced repetition with image occlusion and clozes, it's all there.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **Explaining beats grading cards.** RemNote's review is still fundamentally flashcards — even its AI grading scores your answer to a fixed card. ForeverLM's review is a conversation: you explain the source from scratch and the AI probes gaps it discovers along the way. See [Why Quizzing?](/why-quizzing)
- **Your whole consumption stream, not just coursework.** Podcasts with full transcripts, Safari reading list articles, books, papers, YouTube, X posts — auto-discovered, not manually uploaded. RemNote has no podcast or YouTube ingestion at all.
- **Real money, not a private currency.** RemNote credits are RemNote-denominated, refilled monthly, and spendable nowhere else. ForeverLM's in-app Chat runs on your own OpenRouter key, billed at what OpenRouter actually charges with nothing added, or on free models for nothing; or lean on a subscription you already have, over MCP. Any model, switch anytime, and the ledger is in dollars you can check.
- **Data in your iCloud.** RemNote's synced knowledge bases live on their servers (local-only mode exists but gives up sync). ForeverLM syncs through your own Apple account; the app's servers never store your library.
- **Simpler by design.** RemNote is famously dense — rems, portals, descriptors, templates. ForeverLM has one loop: track, schedule, read or listen, explain it back.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **RemNote** if you're a student working through structured courses with exams, want notes + flashcards + PDF annotation in one place, or need Windows/Android.

Choose **ForeverLM** if you're on a Mac and your learning is source-driven — articles, papers, podcasts, books — and you'd rather own your data outright and pay for AI by the token you actually spent, instead of renting credits by the year.

# ForeverLM vs Quizlet

Quizlet is a large study platform built around flashcard sets, Learn mode, practice tests, textbook solutions, and shared course material. ForeverLM starts with the original sources you want to understand and uses AI dialogue to test whether you can explain them, without requiring you to turn everything into cards first.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Quizlet |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free tier; Plus $35.99/year; Plus Unlimited $44.99/year |
| **Starting material** | Full papers, articles, books, podcasts, videos, and courses | Flashcard sets, notes, uploaded class material, and textbook content |
| **Study mode** | Source-grounded review dialogue and scheduled review | Flashcards, Learn, tests, games, and homework help |
| **Authorship** | Import sources and let the tutor question your understanding | Create sets or use material made by other users and publishers |
| **AI** | Choose models or connect an external assistant through MCP | Built-in Quizlet study and tutoring features |
| **Platforms** | Mac-centered with synced iPhone access | Web, iOS, and Android |
| **Best for** | Deep understanding of authentic sources | Memorization, exam practice, and shared class resources |

*Quizlet pricing checked against its [official upgrade page](https://quizlet.com/upgrade) in August 2026.*

## Where Quizlet is better

- **Fast memorization.** Flashcards are efficient for vocabulary, formulas, dates, and other discrete facts.
- **Huge shared catalog.** Many courses and textbooks already have community or publisher-created material.
- **Practice formats.** Learn mode, tests, games, and textbook solutions provide more structured exercise types.
- **Classroom use.** Teachers can create sets and activities that work across almost any student device.
- **Cross-platform reach.** Quizlet is easier to deploy across schools with Windows, Chromebooks, and Android.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **No card-authoring bottleneck.** Import the real source and start discussing it instead of atomizing it first.
- **Understanding over recognition.** Explaining an idea from scratch reveals gaps that multiple-choice recognition can hide.
- **The tutor sees the source.** Follow-up questions remain grounded in the paper, chapter, transcript, or article being reviewed.
- **Research accumulates.** The same library supports reading, listening, comparison, planning, and later review.
- **Model choice and ownership.** Use different AI models while keeping source files in your own iCloud.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Quizlet** if your goal is memorizing facts, drilling for an exam, or studying from shared classroom sets.

Choose **ForeverLM** if your goal is understanding complete sources and being able to explain their arguments, mechanisms, and limitations in your own words.

They are complementary for many students: use ForeverLM for conceptual understanding and Quizlet for the facts that still require repetition.

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/speechify.md -->

# ForeverLM vs Speechify

Speechify is a specialist text-to-speech app: give it a webpage, PDF, document, or scan and it turns the text into polished audio on almost any device. ForeverLM can also read articles, papers, books, and other text sources aloud, but listening is one step in a larger workflow: save the source, schedule it, read or listen, ask questions, and then test whether you understood it.

The short version: choose Speechify when the voice reader itself is the product. Choose ForeverLM when listening should stay connected to the rest of your learning.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Speechify |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI and voices on your own OpenRouter key at cost (free voices cost nothing) | Free voice-reader tier; Premium is $29/month on the monthly plan |
| **Platforms** | Mac for the full library and reader; synced listening and voice interaction on iPhone | Web, Mac, Windows, iPhone, iPad, Android, Chrome, and Edge |
| **What it reads** | Articles, papers, books, and transcript-only sources already organized in your ForeverLM library | Webpages, PDFs, documents, scans, and text imported from cloud drives |
| **Voices** | Every speech model OpenRouter serves, from many makers; free ones cost nothing | Premium advertises 1,000+ voices in 60+ languages |
| **Playback** | Pause, 15-second seek, 0.75–2x speed, cached audio, iCloud sync | Up to 1.5x on Free and 5x on Premium, with synchronized highlighting |
| **AI conversation** | Source-grounded Chat inside the app, or Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok through MCP | Premium AI summaries, chat, and a general voice assistant |
| **After listening** | Put the source on Schedule, run a review, and keep the review linked to it | No learning schedule or source-linked active-recall history |
| **Storage** | Source files and the library live locally and in your private iCloud container | Account-based cloud service with cloud-drive integrations |

*Speechify features and pricing checked against its [official pricing page](https://speechify.com/pricing/) in August 2026. Plans change, so check the current offer before subscribing.*

## Speechify is a voice reader. ForeverLM is a learning loop.

Both apps can turn a paper or article into audio. What happens around the audio is different.

In Speechify, the main job is frictionless listening: import nearly any text, choose from a very large voice catalog, and play it across devices at high speed. Its scanning, browser extensions, and cloud-drive integrations make it especially useful for accessibility and for people who want everything read aloud.

In ForeverLM, the source already belongs to a library that includes articles, academic papers, books, podcasts, videos, courses, and meetings. You can [listen with Text to Speech](/text-to-speech), pause and [ask questions in Chat](/in-app-chat), add the source to a notebook, schedule it for today, and finish with an AI review that asks you to explain the ideas back. The audio is not a detached conversion; it stays attached to the source and its learning history.

## Where Speechify is better

- **Text-to-speech breadth.** Speechify is built around listening and accepts more ad hoc inputs, including scans and cloud documents.
- **Voice selection.** Its advertised catalog of more than 1,000 voices and 60 languages is much broader than any single ForeverLM provider.
- **Platform coverage.** Speechify works on Android, Windows, browsers, and mobile devices. ForeverLM's full library workflow is Mac-centered.
- **Very fast playback.** Premium supports speeds up to 5x; ForeverLM stops at 2x.
- **Accessibility focus.** If dyslexia, visual strain, or reading difficulty makes high-quality narration the primary need, Speechify is the more mature specialist.

## Where ForeverLM is more complete

- **One library for every learning source.** The same place holds the paper you listen to, the podcast you heard yesterday, the article you saved for Friday, and the chat where you connected their ideas.
- **Listening leads somewhere.** Schedule the source, track whether it is pending or reviewed, and use [review dialogue](/why-quizzing) to check understanding instead of treating playback as completion.
- **Chat stays integrated.** Ask about the current selection or the full source without exporting it into a separate workflow. Completed reviews remain linked to the sources they covered.
- **Choose the voice.** Pick any speech model OpenRouter serves, from many makers, and one of its voices; free ones cost nothing. You are not locked into one voice catalog or subscription.
- **Reusable audio.** Cloud narration can be cached and synced through iCloud so the iPhone can play the prepared source without regenerating every chunk.
- **Your source library stays yours.** Files and metadata live in your iCloud and local SQLite database, not in a required vendor reading account.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Speechify** if your main question is, “What is the best way to have almost any text read aloud on all my devices?” Its specialist voice experience, language breadth, scanning, and cross-platform reach are hard to beat.

Choose **ForeverLM** if your question is, “How do I keep up with everything I want to learn, listen when reading is inconvenient, and still remember it later?” Text to Speech is included in the same system as your reading list, papers, notebooks, Schedule, source-grounded chat, and review history.

If you only need occasional narration on a Mac, start with a free voice in ForeverLM. If listening is the center of your day across Android, Windows, and the web, Speechify will probably fit better.

# ForeverLM vs ElevenReader

ElevenReader is ElevenLabs' mobile reading app for turning articles, PDFs, EPUB books, newsletters, scans, and pasted text into natural-sounding speech. It also creates conversational GenFM podcasts from imported content. ForeverLM reads many of the same sources aloud, but listening remains connected to a research library, source-grounded chat, notebooks, scheduling, and review.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | ElevenReader |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI and voices on your own OpenRouter key at cost (free voices cost nothing) | Free mobile app; separate ElevenLabs services have their own pricing |
| **Platforms** | Full workflow on Mac, synced listening on iPhone | iPhone, iPad, and Android |
| **Inputs** | Saved articles, papers, books, and transcripts in the library | PDF, EPUB, TXT, web links, scanned text, and pasted text |
| **Voices** | Every speech model OpenRouter serves, from many makers; free ones cost nothing | Hundreds of ElevenLabs voices in 32 languages |
| **Generated podcasts** | A notebook's audio overview, one narrator over its sources; real podcasts kept as sources with transcripts | GenFM creates AI-hosted podcasts from imported content |
| **Chat** | Source-grounded Chat and external MCP assistants | Listening-focused rather than a persistent research chat system |
| **After listening** | Schedule, review, and keep learning history | Build a listening library and reading habit |

*ElevenReader capabilities checked against the [official ElevenReader page](https://elevenlabs.io/text-reader) in August 2026.*

## Where ElevenReader is better

- **Voice quality is the center of the product.** ElevenLabs offers a large, expressive voice catalog across 32 languages.
- **Mobile-first capture.** Scan a page, paste text, or add a link directly from a phone.
- **Android support.** ForeverLM does not have an Android app.
- **A broader casual-reading library.** ElevenReader includes classics, indie titles, newsletters, and curated feeds.
- **Generated audio shows.** GenFM is useful when a conversational summary is more appealing than straight narration.

## Where ForeverLM is more complete

- **The text remains a research source.** The PDF or article stays searchable, in its notebooks, and available to Chat after narration ends.
- **Listening connects to action.** Put a source on Schedule, mark it complete, and review it through an AI dialogue.
- **Many voice makers.** Pick any speech model OpenRouter serves rather than depending on one provider's voices.
- **Podcasts are original sources too.** Follow real shows, keep full transcripts, and discuss them beside papers and articles.
- **A long-term knowledge library.** ForeverLM is designed to accumulate years of reading and listening in your own iCloud.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **ElevenReader** if natural mobile narration is the main job, especially on Android or across many languages.

Choose **ForeverLM** if listening is one part of a larger research and learning workflow. The source remains available for comparison, discussion, scheduling, and review instead of ending at playback.
