# ForeverLM vs Readwise Reader

Readwise Reader is one of the best read-it-later and highlight-management products available. It brings articles, newsletters, RSS, PDFs, EPUBs, videos, and social posts into a polished cross-platform reader, then sends highlights into Readwise for resurfacing and export.

ForeverLM overlaps with that first job: it gives you a reading list for articles and other sources without charging a reading-list subscription. It then focuses on what happens after saving—planning the source, discussing it alongside the rest of your library, and checking whether you can explain it.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Readwise Reader + Readwise |
|---|---|---|
| **Reading-list price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | 30-day trial, then $9.99/month billed annually or $12.99/month billed monthly |
| **AI costs** | Your own OpenRouter key, billed by OpenRouter at cost with nothing added, for any model in Chat (free models cost nothing); or an assistant subscription you already use, over MCP | Ghostreader is included; external assistants use your own ChatGPT, Claude, or other MCP client account |
| **Platforms** | Mac-centered library with synced iPhone reading, listening, and voice access | Web, Mac, Windows, iOS, Android, browser extensions, and e-ink viewing |
| **Capture** | Safari, Chrome, and Brave reading lists; URL paste; local files; plugins; MCP | Browser extensions, share sheet, email newsletters, RSS, file upload, and imports |
| **Content** | Articles, papers, books, podcasts, videos, courses, meetings, and X posts | Articles, newsletters, RSS, PDFs, EPUBs, videos, podcasts, and X posts |
| **Listening** | Any speech model OpenRouter serves (free ones cost nothing), cached audio, iPhone voice control | Natural AI voices, adjustable speed, and many languages across platforms |
| **AI conversation** | Multi-source in-app Chat with model choice, plus full-library MCP read/write tools | Ghostreader in Reader, plus MCP access for external assistants to read and organize documents |
| **Review method** | Source-linked review dialogue: explain the ideas, answer follow-ups, and keep the transcript and result | Daily Review resurfaces highlights; Mastery cards are self-graded |
| **Storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container | Readwise cloud with full exports available |
| **Exports** | Source files stay in iCloud; drag sources into any major AI assistant | Excellent exports to Obsidian, Notion, Roam, CSV, Markdown, OPML, and zipped files |

*Readwise features and pricing checked against its [official Reader page](https://readwise.io/read/) in August 2026. Readwise offers 50% discounts to several eligible groups.*

## A free app versus a reading subscription

Readwise Full costs **$119.88 per year** on annual billing or **$155.88 per year** month-to-month. That subscription pays for a highly polished cross-platform reader, newsletter and RSS workflows, text-to-speech, Ghostreader, highlight aggregation, Daily Review, and best-in-class exports.

ForeverLM's reading list comes with the app, which is **free**. Articles saved in Safari, Chrome, or Brave flow into Studio, where you can read them, organize them into notebooks, and put them on Schedule without a subscription. Papers, books, podcasts, videos, courses, and meetings share the same library.

Beyond that, only AI and voices cost anything inside the app, and ForeverLM never charges for them. Free voices cost nothing. In-app Chat runs on your own OpenRouter key, billed by OpenRouter at its cost with nothing added, or on free models for nothing. Connecting a Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok subscription through MCP is the one paid part: 7 days free, then $19 once. A quiet reading month adds nothing to your OpenRouter bill.

## Where Readwise is better

- **Cross-platform reading.** Reader has mature apps across the web, Mac, Windows, iOS, Android, and e-ink devices. ForeverLM's complete library workflow remains Mac-centered.
- **Capture breadth.** Newsletters get their own inbox, RSS feeds update automatically, and the browser and mobile capture tools are excellent.
- **Highlight aggregation.** Kindle and highlights from more than 20 sources flow into one Readwise account for review.
- **Reading experience.** Typography, annotation, offline reading, document triage, and text-to-speech have been refined specifically for power readers.
- **Exports.** Continuous sync into Obsidian, Notion, Roam, and other note systems is a Readwise strength, and the service offers comprehensive data exports.
- **Kindle and e-ink workflows.** Reader can send documents to Kindle and supports dedicated viewing modes for devices such as BOOX and Daylight.

## Where ForeverLM is more complete

- **The reading list is free.** Saving and organizing articles costs nothing, not $119.88 every year.
- **Sources become a plan.** Schedule specific items for specific days, move unfinished work, and see pending, reviewed, and completed sources rather than maintaining an endless queue.
- **Review tests understanding.** Readwise resurfaces what you highlighted. ForeverLM asks you to reconstruct the source in your own words, probes gaps, and saves the review back against the sources it covered.
- **Chat is part of the notebook.** Discuss one source or combine papers, articles, podcasts, meetings, and videos in the same conversation. In-app Chat supports model choice, and MCP lets external assistants search and operate the library.
- **Podcasts and meetings are first-class sources.** Full transcripts can be read, searched, scheduled, discussed, and reviewed alongside written material.
- **Local ownership by default.** The knowledge base lives in local SQLite and your private iCloud container instead of requiring a vendor cloud account for the library.
- **Choose how listening works.** Pick any speech model OpenRouter serves, free ones included; cached audio remains attached to the source and syncs through iCloud.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Readwise Reader** if you want the most polished cross-platform reading inbox, rely heavily on RSS and newsletters, collect highlights from Kindle and many other services, or need continuous export into a notes app. The subscription buys a broad and mature reading experience.

Choose **ForeverLM** if you want a reading list on Apple devices with no subscription and your real problem is the queue after capture: what to read today, how it connects to the rest of your research, and whether you retained it. It covers saving, reading, listening, source-grounded chat, planning, and active review in one local-first workflow.

They can also work together. Keep Readwise as the universal highlight and feed inbox, and use ForeverLM for the sources important enough to schedule, discuss deeply, and review for understanding.

# ForeverLM vs Matter

Matter is a polished read-later app for articles and newsletters on iPhone, iPad, and the web. It offers a clean reader, highlighting, feeds, and listening. ForeverLM includes a reading list, but expands it into a research library for papers, books, podcasts, videos, and courses with notebooks, chat, scheduling, and review.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Matter |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free |
| **Platforms** | Mac-centered, with synced iPhone access | iPhone, iPad, and web |
| **Best for** | Managing and learning from many source types | A focused queue for articles and newsletters |
| **Capture** | Reading lists, URLs, files, feeds, reference tools, podcasts, and plugins | Share sheet, browser, email newsletters, and feeds |
| **Listening** | Narration from any speech model OpenRouter serves, tied to the source | Built-in article listening |
| **AI** | Cross-source Chat and MCP assistants that can operate the library | Reading assistance inside the article workflow |
| **Retention** | Schedule plus source-linked review | Highlights and reading history, without an active-review loop |

*Matter's current free model and platform scope checked against [Matter](https://www.getmatter.com/) in August 2026.*

## Where Matter is better

- **Focused reading design.** Matter is built around making an article queue pleasant and frictionless.
- **Mobile-first experience.** Saving and reading on iPhone or iPad is the center of the product.
- **Newsletter handling.** A dedicated inbox keeps subscriptions away from the normal email queue.
- **Simple pricing.** Matter is free, with no AI meter or plan decision.
- **Less machinery.** If all you need is a calm place to read web articles, a research system can be unnecessary.

## Where ForeverLM is more complete

- **The reading list is only one source stream.** Papers, books, podcasts, YouTube, courses, meetings, and X posts belong to the same library.
- **Notebooks connect formats.** Keep an article with the paper it references and the podcast where the author explains it.
- **AI reaches across sources.** Ask for agreements, contradictions, or missing evidence across a whole notebook.
- **Reading becomes scheduled work.** Assign sources to days and track completion instead of accumulating an endless queue.
- **Review tests understanding.** Explain the source in your own words and preserve the resulting dialogue.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Matter** if you mainly want a beautiful, free read-later experience for articles and newsletters on mobile.

Choose **ForeverLM** if articles are one part of a wider research practice and you want listening, cross-source chat, planning, and review around them.

# ForeverLM vs Instapaper

Instapaper is a long-running read-later service that turns web content into a clean, offline reading queue across phones, tablets, browsers, Kindle, and Kobo. Premium adds PDF reading, full-text search, permanent archives, unlimited notes, and AI voice playlists. ForeverLM includes a reading list and narration, then connects those articles to a broader research and learning system.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Instapaper |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free tier; Premium $6/month or $60/year |
| **Platforms** | Mac-centered with synced iPhone access | Web, iPhone, iPad, Android, Kindle, and Kobo workflows |
| **Content** | Articles, papers, books, podcasts, videos, courses, and more | Articles, videos, long email, X saves, and PDFs on Premium |
| **Listening** | Any speech model OpenRouter serves, free ones included | AI voice playlists and text-to-speech on Premium |
| **Archive** | Local source files and extracted content in iCloud | Permanent web archive on Premium |
| **AI** | Cross-source Chat and MCP assistants | Reading and narration features rather than full-library research chat |
| **Review** | Schedule and source-linked review dialogue | Highlights, notes, speed reading, and reading history |

*Instapaper pricing and Premium features checked against its [official documentation](https://www.instapaper.com/docs/premium/overview) in August 2026.*

## Where Instapaper is better

- **Read-later simplicity.** Saving, opening, and reading an article is fast and familiar.
- **E-reader delivery.** Kindle digests and Kobo integration serve people who prefer dedicated reading hardware.
- **Cross-platform access.** Android and broad web support make it easier outside the Apple ecosystem.
- **Permanent archives.** Premium preserves saved articles even if the original page disappears.
- **Reading-specific tools.** Speed Reading, playlists, tags, folders, highlights, and notes are mature.

## Where ForeverLM is more complete

- **Articles join the rest of the research.** A saved essay can live beside papers, podcasts, books, videos, and meetings.
- **Listening offers many voices.** Pick any speech model OpenRouter serves, free ones included.
- **Chat sees the full context.** Ask about one article or compare it with a whole notebook.
- **An assistant can plan the work.** MCP tools expose the learning schedule and let an external AI move and complete sources.
- **Review goes beyond resurfacing.** Explain the source and keep a record of what you understood.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Instapaper** if you want a focused, cross-platform read-later queue, especially with Kindle or Kobo delivery.

Choose **ForeverLM** if saved articles are research inputs that should stay connected to other sources, AI conversation, scheduling, and active review.

# ForeverLM vs Raindrop.io

Raindrop.io is a polished bookmark manager for saving, organizing, highlighting, searching, archiving, and sharing almost anything found online. Its generous free plan supports unlimited bookmarks, collections, highlights, and devices. ForeverLM includes a reading list, but is designed around consuming and understanding sources rather than maintaining a universal bookmark archive.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Raindrop.io |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free plan; optional Pro subscription |
| **Best for** | Learning from a curated source library | Organizing a broad, durable bookmark collection |
| **Capture** | Reading lists, URLs, files, podcasts, papers, books, and plugins | Browser extensions, share sheets, apps, integrations, and uploads |
| **Organization** | Notebooks, status, source types, relationships, and Schedule | Collections, nested structure, tags, filters, highlights, and collaboration |
| **Search** | Metadata, extracted content, and semantic source search | Full-text search and permanent archive on Pro |
| **AI** | Cross-source Chat and MCP assistants | AI Assistant and suggestions on Pro |
| **Review** | Review dialogue and saved learning history | No active-review workflow |

*Raindrop.io features checked against its [official pricing page](https://raindrop.io/pro/buy) in August 2026. Local pricing is shown at checkout.*

## Where Raindrop.io is better

- **Bookmark management.** It handles a much larger universe of links, including design inspiration, shopping, tools, images, and references you may never read linearly.
- **Free cross-platform access.** Unlimited bookmarks and devices work across Mac, Windows, iOS, Android, and major browsers.
- **Collection design.** Nested collections, tags, filters, icons, sharing, and collaboration are more flexible.
- **Web preservation.** Pro keeps permanent archived copies and finds duplicate or broken links.
- **Integrations.** Thousands of automation and import/export connections make it an excellent bookmark hub.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **Saved items become complete sources.** Articles are extracted for reading, listening, chat, and later review.
- **The library includes offline and spoken material.** Papers, books, podcasts, courses, meetings, and videos share the same notebooks.
- **The queue is intentional.** Schedule what matters rather than treating every bookmark as equal.
- **AI works across whole notebooks.** Compare arguments and retrieve evidence from the sources you are actively studying.
- **Progress has meaning.** Pending, completed, and reviewed states describe learning progress, not only an archive.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Raindrop.io** if you want the best general-purpose bookmark organizer with generous free limits and broad platform support.

Choose **ForeverLM** if the links you save are material you intend to read, listen to, discuss, and remember.

# ForeverLM vs Glasp

Glasp is a social web highlighter for collecting passages and notes from articles, PDFs, YouTube, and Kindle, then exporting or sharing what you found. Its AI features include summaries, transcription, private highlights on paid plans, and an AI clone built from your collection. ForeverLM stores complete sources rather than centering the highlight, and uses them for cross-source research and active review.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Glasp |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free tier; Pro $15/month or $150/year; Unlimited $36/month or $360/year |
| **Primary object** | The complete source and its learning history | The highlight, note, summary, and public knowledge profile |
| **Capture** | Articles, papers, books, podcasts, videos, courses, meetings, and more | Web articles, PDFs, YouTube, and Kindle highlights |
| **Social layer** | Private personal library | Public profiles, following, discovery, and shareable highlights |
| **AI** | Configurable cross-source Chat and MCP assistants | Summaries, transcription, recommendations, and an AI clone |
| **Export** | Source files plus structured database and plugin access | Exports to Notion, Obsidian, Markdown, and other note systems |
| **Review** | Scheduled review dialogue with saved history | Highlight resurfacing and AI interaction without the same review record |

*Glasp pricing checked against its [May 2026 pricing announcement](https://blog.glasp.co/price-update-2026-05-01/) and product materials in August 2026.*

## Where Glasp is better

- **Highlight capture.** The browser extension makes it fast to save and annotate passages without leaving the page.
- **Social discovery.** Public profiles and shared highlights expose what other curious readers found valuable.
- **Knowledge export.** Strong Notion, Obsidian, and Markdown workflows suit people who already maintain a note system.
- **YouTube and Kindle workflows.** Highlights and summaries are built around popular reading and viewing surfaces.
- **Shareable artifacts.** Quoteshots and public collections make excerpts easy to publish.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **Complete sources remain available.** Chat and review can inspect the full paper, article, transcript, or book rather than only highlighted passages.
- **Privacy is the default.** The library lives in your iCloud instead of starting from a public knowledge profile.
- **More source types share one workflow.** Podcasts, courses, meetings, and academic papers are first-class records.
- **AI can organize and schedule.** MCP assistants do more than summarize or imitate a knowledge profile.
- **The learner must explain.** Review asks for reconstruction in your own words and records the result.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Glasp** if highlighting, public knowledge sharing, and exporting excerpts into a note system are the center of your workflow.

Choose **ForeverLM** if you want a private library of complete sources with cross-source chat, listening, planning, and active review.

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/zotero.md -->

# ForeverLM vs Zotero

Zotero is the open-source standard for collecting references, managing citation metadata, annotating PDFs, and generating bibliographies. ForeverLM overlaps on building and organizing a paper library, but it is aimed at a different outcome: reading, listening to, discussing, and remembering the research alongside all your other learning sources.

This is not a claim that ForeverLM replaces Zotero for academic writing. It does not. If your next step is inserting a perfectly formatted citation into a manuscript, Zotero is the better tool. If your next step is understanding how the paper changes your thinking, ForeverLM carries the workflow further.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Zotero |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free and open source; 300 MB file sync free, then $20/year for 2 GB, $60/year for 6 GB, or $120/year unlimited |
| **Platforms** | Mac-centered library with synced iPhone access | Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS, Android, and web library |
| **Paper capture** | Browser reading lists, URL paste, local PDFs, MCP, and custom plugins; open PDFs fetched when available | Excellent browser plugin, DOI/ISBN lookup, database translators, file import, and feeds |
| **Organization** | Notebooks, source types, search, status, tags, and a day-by-day Schedule | Collections, tags, related items, saved searches, duplicate detection, and group libraries |
| **PDF reading** | Built-in reader, extracted text, figures, Text to Speech, and source-grounded Chat | Mature PDF reader with highlights, notes, image annotations, and annotation-to-note workflows |
| **Citations** | Stores paper metadata, but no manuscript citation or bibliography plugin | Best-in-class Word, LibreOffice, and Google Docs citation workflow with thousands of CSL styles |
| **AI** | In-app multi-source Chat, model choice, web search, MCP library tools, and saved source-linked review transcripts | Community plugins can add AI workflows; AI is not the core Zotero learning loop |
| **Learning** | Schedule, source chat, review, scores, and linked review history | No built-in study schedule or active-recall workflow |
| **Storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container | Local-first; optional Zotero Storage or WebDAV for attachment sync |

*Zotero capabilities and storage pricing checked against its [official guide](https://www.zotero.org/support/quick_start_guide) and [storage page](https://www.zotero.org/support/individual_storage) in August 2026.*

## Where Zotero is better

- **Citations and bibliographies.** Zotero inserts and updates citations in Word, LibreOffice, and Google Docs, switches styles across an entire manuscript, and generates the bibliography automatically. ForeverLM does not do this.
- **PDF annotation.** Highlights, notes, image annotations, and annotation-backed notes are a mature part of Zotero's research workflow.
- **Reference capture.** Zotero's translators recognize an enormous range of publisher pages, library catalogs, databases, and item types.
- **Collaboration.** Group libraries and shared annotations make Zotero a much better fit for labs, classes, and coauthors.
- **Open ecosystem.** Zotero is free, open source, extensible through plugins, and available across desktop platforms.
- **Bibliographic rigor.** Complex metadata, citation styles, attachment relationships, and reference exports are its home territory.

## Where ForeverLM is more complete

- **The paper is part of a wider knowledge library.** Research sits beside articles, books, podcasts, videos, courses, and meetings instead of living in a paper-only workflow.
- **You can chat with the library directly.** Ask questions about one paper, compare several, search across everything, or let an MCP-connected assistant organize sources and notebooks. The conversation can happen inside ForeverLM and stay linked to the material.
- **Reading and listening are built in.** ForeverLM extracts the full text, exposes paper figures in Chat, and can turn a paper into cached audio while removing bibliography and citation noise from narration.
- **Planning is first-class.** Put papers on specific days, move unfinished work, and see whether a source is pending, reviewed, or complete.
- **Review tests understanding.** Instead of stopping at highlights and notes, explain the paper back to an AI tutor that can probe the methodology, evidence, limitations, and conceptual gaps.
- **Full-text retrieval is part of ingestion.** ForeverLM attempts direct open-access downloads, PubMed Central copies, and configured institutional access, while recording paywall status when a PDF cannot be obtained.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Zotero** if you are writing papers, dissertations, or reports and need precise citations, bibliographies, annotation, collaboration, or a cross-platform open-source reference manager. It is exceptional at that job and costs nothing unless you want more hosted file storage.

Choose **ForeverLM** if paper management is the beginning rather than the end: you want research mixed with the rest of your source library, scheduled into your week, available to AI conversation, listenable on the go, and followed by active review.

For many researchers, the honest answer is **both**. Keep Zotero as the citation system of record. Use ForeverLM for the smaller set of papers you intend to understand deeply and connect to articles, talks, books, and ongoing notebooks.

## Why ForeverLM does not sync with Zotero

There is no Zotero plugin in ForeverLM, and none is planned. Everything ForeverLM does with a paper, from search and Chat to Text to Speech and review, works on a PDF that lives in your own iCloud library. A plugin that only pointed at your Zotero records would enable none of it. So the route is a one-time move: choose your Zotero data folder in setup's Papers step (**Coming from a reference manager?**), or ask an assistant with the ForeverLM plugin to migrate the library. Either way the Zotero data folder, or a BibTeX or RIS export with its files, is read and each paper goes through the normal pipeline. Zotero is read, never changed, and the papers are yours in ForeverLM from then on. See [Papers → Coming from a Reference Manager](/papers#coming-from-a-reference-manager).

---

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/paperpile.md -->

# ForeverLM vs Paperpile

Paperpile is a polished, cloud-based reference manager for collecting papers, managing PDFs, and citing them in Google Docs, Microsoft Word, and LaTeX workflows. ForeverLM also collects and organizes papers, but folds them into a broader system for source-grounded chat, listening, planning, and active review.

Paperpile helps you move from **paper to citation**. ForeverLM helps you move from **paper to understanding**.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Paperpile |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Regular $99.60/year; Expert $138/year; eligible academics pay 50% less after a 30-day trial |
| **Platforms** | Mac-centered library with synced iPhone access | Web, iOS, and Android; browser extensions for Chrome, Safari, and Firefox |
| **Paper capture** | Browser reading lists, URL paste, local PDFs, MCP, and custom plugins; automatic open-PDF retrieval | One-click browser import, database and publisher integrations, identifier search, automatic PDF retrieval |
| **Organization** | Notebooks, source types, search, tags, status, and Schedule | Folders, labels, stars, filters, duplicate merging, full-text search, and shared libraries |
| **PDF workflow** | Reader, extracted text and figures, Text to Speech, Chat, and review | PDF reader; notes, highlighting, and collaboration on Expert |
| **Citations** | Stores paper metadata, but no cite-while-you-write plugin | Word and Google Docs plugins, BibTeX/LaTeX, 10,000+ styles, and Overleaf integration |
| **AI workflow** | Chat inside ForeverLM or connect any MCP assistant to search and operate the full library; sessions and reviews can be saved back | Ask AI beta uploads selected PDFs and prompts into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, or NotebookLM |
| **Beyond papers** | Articles, books, podcasts, videos, courses, meetings, and X posts share the same notebooks and Chat | Focused on references, PDFs, and academic writing |
| **Storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container | Account-based service with unlimited research PDF storage and optional Google Drive/OneDrive sync |

*Paperpile pricing and features checked against its [official pricing page](https://paperpile.com/pricing/) and [Ask AI documentation](https://paperpile.com/h/ask-ai/) in August 2026. All individual plans are billed annually.*

## AI is where the workflows diverge

Paperpile's Ask AI feature is a useful bridge. Select one or more PDFs, choose a research prompt, and Paperpile opens ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, or NotebookLM with the files attached. It is a pragmatic way to bring a paper into the assistant you already use.

ForeverLM supports that lightweight workflow too: drag selected sources into an AI chat. But it also goes further in two directions.

First, Chat is built into the source library. You can discuss the current paper or several sources, search the web, inspect paper figures, and keep the conversation alongside the notebook. Second, the MCP connection is persistent and two-way: an assistant can search the full library, retrieve content, organize notebooks, manage the Schedule, and save a completed review transcript back to ForeverLM. Paperpile says its MCP server is still in development, and its current Ask AI responses cannot automatically be saved back as library notes.

## Where Paperpile is better

- **Cite while you write.** Paperpile is designed for inserting citations and formatting bibliographies in Google Docs and Word, with strong BibTeX and Overleaf support. ForeverLM is not a manuscript citation tool.
- **Academic discovery and capture.** Its browser extension, database integrations, metadata repair, proxy support, and automatic PDF retrieval cover the messy long tail of scholarly publishing.
- **PDF annotation and collaboration.** Expert adds notes, highlights, shared folders and libraries, permissions, and collaborative PDF annotations.
- **Cross-platform access.** The web app and iOS/Android clients work well for researchers who are not Mac-only.
- **Unlimited hosted PDFs.** Every paid individual plan includes unlimited research PDF storage.
- **Google-centered workflows.** If your lab lives in Google Drive and Google Docs, Paperpile fits naturally.

## Where ForeverLM is more complete

- **Everything belongs to the same research context.** A paper can sit in a notebook with a podcast interview, an article, a conference video, meeting notes, and a book chapter—and Chat can reason across them together.
- **AI is not an export step.** Source-grounded conversation lives in the app, while MCP gives external assistants structured access to the full library instead of attaching a few PDFs to one thread.
- **The result comes back.** Review sessions retain their transcript, summary, score, and source links. The library records what was covered rather than forgetting the interaction when the external tab closes.
- **Papers can be heard as well as read.** Text to Speech cleans academic text for narration, skips citation clutter and reference sections, caches the audio, and syncs it to iPhone.
- **The reading queue is actionable.** Schedule papers for specific days, move them when plans change, and connect completion to a real review.
- **No reference-manager subscription.** The paper library, notebooks, Schedule, local reading, Text to Speech and built-in AI all come with the free app; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once. AI and voices run on your own OpenRouter key at OpenRouter's cost.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Paperpile** if your center of gravity is academic writing: browser capture, clean metadata, PDF annotation, team libraries, and citations flowing into Google Docs, Word, BibTeX, or Overleaf. It is particularly compelling for Google-centric labs.

Choose **ForeverLM** if you want papers integrated with everything else you learn and you care more about asking, comparing, listening, scheduling, and remembering than cite-while-you-write.

They can also be complementary. Keep the full canonical bibliography in Paperpile, then bring the papers that matter to ForeverLM for cross-source research and review. If you want a free, open-source citation manager instead, see [ForeverLM vs Zotero](/compare/zotero).

## Why ForeverLM does not sync with Paperpile

There is no Paperpile plugin in ForeverLM, and none is planned. Everything ForeverLM does with a paper, from search and Chat to Text to Speech and review, works on a PDF that lives in your own iCloud library. A plugin that only pointed at your Paperpile records would enable none of it. So the route is a one-time move: export BibTeX from Paperpile into the `Paperpile` folder Paperpile syncs to Google Drive, and choose that folder in setup's Papers step (**Coming from a reference manager?**), or ask an assistant with the ForeverLM plugin to migrate it. Each paper goes through the normal pipeline, and papers without a synced PDF are added by DOI. Paperpile is never changed, and the papers are yours in ForeverLM from then on. See [Papers → Coming from a Reference Manager](/papers#coming-from-a-reference-manager).

# ForeverLM vs Papers (ReadCube)

Papers is a mature reference manager for discovering, organizing, annotating, sharing, and citing academic literature. Its AI Assistant can explain one PDF or find themes across a set of papers. ForeverLM also manages papers and chats across them, but puts those papers beside articles, books, podcasts, videos, and courses in a library designed for learning.

Papers moves research from **search to citation**. ForeverLM moves sources from **capture to understanding**.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Papers |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Essentials $65/year; Pro $130/year; 40% academic discount |
| **Library** | Papers plus articles, books, podcasts, videos, courses, meetings, and more | Academic references and research files |
| **AI** | Chat with any selected sources or the wider library using configurable models and MCP assistants | Chat with one PDF on Essentials; up to 20 papers and AI search on Pro |
| **Citations** | Stores scholarly metadata, but no cite-while-you-write plugin | SmartCite for Word and Google Docs, with 10,000+ styles |
| **Listening** | Reads papers aloud and keeps audio attached to the source | No comparable paper-listening workflow |
| **Review** | Schedule sources and save review history | No source-linked active-review system |
| **Platforms** | Mac-centered, with synced iPhone access | Web, desktop, iOS, and Android |

*Papers pricing and features checked against its [official pricing page](https://www.papersapp.com/pricing/) in August 2026.*

## Where Papers is better

- **Reference management.** Papers is purpose-built for bibliographies, metadata repair, related-paper discovery, shared libraries, and academic collaboration.
- **Cite while you write.** SmartCite inserts and formats citations directly in Word and Google Docs.
- **Research discovery.** Pro searches more than 150 million publications through Dimensions and turns natural-language requests into structured searches.
- **Cross-platform access.** Researchers can work across Windows, macOS, the web, iOS, and Android.
- **Team workflows.** Shared libraries, transferable seats, permissions, and institutional plans serve labs better than ForeverLM does today.

## Where ForeverLM is more complete

- **Research is not limited to papers.** A literature notebook can include the authors' podcast interviews, conference talks, books, articles, and meeting notes.
- **AI can operate the library.** An MCP assistant can search sources, retrieve content, organize notebooks, manage a learning schedule, and save a review transcript back to ForeverLM.
- **Listening is integrated.** Read a dense paper aloud, pause to ask questions, and continue without creating a detached audio file.
- **Understanding is recorded.** Scheduling, completion state, and reviews turn reading into a repeatable learning loop.
- **No annual research-software fee.** The library is free, instead of an annual tier; only using it from Claude or ChatGPT over MCP is paid, $19 once after 7 free days. The built-in AI runs on your own OpenRouter key: pay models at cost, or use free models.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Papers** if you need a professional reference manager, cite-while-you-write tools, research discovery, and collaboration across a lab.

Choose **ForeverLM** if you want papers integrated with every other source you learn from, with listening, cross-source conversation, scheduling, and active review.

They work well together: keep a canonical citation library in Papers, then bring the papers you are actively learning into ForeverLM.

# ForeverLM vs Mendeley

Mendeley is Elsevier's reference manager for storing, organizing, annotating, sharing, and citing academic papers. Its paid plans now add a Reading Assistant, cross-library questions, experiment comparison, and larger storage. ForeverLM also manages and chats with papers, but treats them as one part of a broader research and learning library.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Mendeley |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free with 2 GB; Plus $55/year; Pro $110/year; Max $165/year |
| **Paper storage** | Local files and metadata in private iCloud | Elsevier cloud, from 2 GB to unlimited by plan |
| **AI** | Configurable models, multi-source Chat, and MCP assistants | Reading Assistant; Ask My Library and Compare Experiments on Pro and Max |
| **Citations** | No cite-while-you-write plugin | Mendeley Cite for Microsoft Word |
| **Organization** | Notebooks, tags, source status, Schedule, and relationships | Collections, tags, annotations, notebook, and research groups |
| **Beyond papers** | Articles, books, podcasts, videos, courses, and meetings | Academic references and research papers |
| **Review** | Source-linked review dialogue | No comparable learning schedule and review history |

*Mendeley pricing and AI features checked against its [official pricing page](https://www.mendeley.com/pricing/) in August 2026.*

## Where Mendeley is better

- **Citation workflow.** Mendeley Cite inserts references and bibliographies in Word.
- **Research discovery.** Recommendations and Elsevier's scholarly ecosystem help find related work.
- **Generous free entry.** The free reference manager includes 2 GB of storage and limited Reading Assistant questions.
- **Cross-platform academic workflow.** Desktop, web, and browser tools support researchers outside the Apple ecosystem.
- **Collaboration.** Research groups and shared material fit labs and course teams.

## Where ForeverLM is more complete

- **Every research format belongs together.** A paper can share a notebook with interviews, lectures, articles, books, and meeting notes.
- **The library is not tied to a publisher cloud.** Files and metadata remain local and in your private iCloud container.
- **AI choice is explicit.** Select models per task or use an assistant subscription you already have through MCP.
- **Papers can be listened to.** Narration, source chat, and reading stay attached to the same record.
- **Understanding is tracked.** Schedule the paper, run a review, and keep the transcript and completion state.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Mendeley** if you want a cloud reference manager with Word citations, scholarly recommendations, collaboration, and Elsevier-connected research services.

Choose **ForeverLM** if citation formatting is secondary to reading, listening, connecting, discussing, and retaining the paper alongside everything else you learn.

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/endnote.md -->

# ForeverLM vs EndNote

EndNote is Clarivate's established reference manager for large scholarly libraries, full-text retrieval, citation formatting, collaboration, and manuscript workflows. EndNote 2025 adds an AI Research Assistant. ForeverLM is not a citation-production replacement. It focuses on collecting the sources you are actively learning from and connecting them to chat, listening, planning, and review.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | EndNote 2025 |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | $275 full license; $150 student; $125 upgrade |
| **Primary job** | Source library and active learning | Professional reference management and academic writing |
| **Citations** | Metadata storage without cite-while-you-write | Cite While You Write and more than 6,000 bibliographic styles |
| **AI** | Configurable source chat and external MCP assistants | EndNote Research Assistant for paper and library questions |
| **Library** | Many learning formats in notebooks | Large scholarly reference collections and PDFs |
| **Storage** | Local SQLite and private iCloud files | Desktop library with EndNote Web sync and sharing |
| **Review** | Scheduled review dialogue with saved history | No equivalent source-understanding record |

*EndNote pricing checked against its [official purchase page](https://endnote.com/buy) in August 2026.*

## Where EndNote is better

- **Citation production.** EndNote remains a specialist for inserting, formatting, and changing references across manuscripts.
- **Style breadth.** Thousands of maintained bibliographic styles support journals and institutions around the world.
- **Large academic libraries.** Deduplication, metadata updates, full-text retrieval, groups, and search serve long-running research programs.
- **Publisher workflow.** Journal matching and Clarivate integrations help researchers move toward submission.
- **Institutional adoption.** Universities and labs can license, teach, and support a familiar standard tool.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **It follows the learning process.** Capture, read, listen, ask, schedule, and review without leaving the source record.
- **Research includes more than citations.** Podcasts, courses, videos, books, articles, and meetings share context with academic papers.
- **AI is not tied to one vendor.** Choose the model and use external assistants through MCP.
- **The tutor asks you questions.** A review session evaluates your explanation instead of only answering a query.
- **A lower one-time price.** ForeverLM itself is free, so you can build the library without buying a $275 desktop license; only MCP costs anything ($19 once after 7 free days).

## Which should you choose?

Choose **EndNote** if citation accuracy, journal styles, manuscript integration, and institutional scholarly workflows are non-negotiable.

Choose **ForeverLM** if you need to understand and retain sources across formats rather than produce a final bibliography.

For many academics the right answer is both: EndNote owns the canonical references, while ForeverLM owns the active reading and learning.

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/elicit.md -->

# ForeverLM vs Elicit

Elicit is an AI research assistant for finding literature, screening papers, extracting structured evidence, and producing research reports. ForeverLM starts later in the lifecycle: it keeps the papers and other sources you have chosen, lets you work across them, and helps you understand and remember them.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Elicit |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free Basic; Plus $132/year; Pro $480/year; Scale $1,068/year |
| **Core job** | Persistent source library and learning workflow | Literature discovery, screening, extraction, and systematic review |
| **Corpus** | Your papers, articles, books, podcasts, videos, and other sources | Search across more than 138 million papers plus imports and uploads |
| **AI output** | Source-grounded conversation and review | Reports, evidence tables, extraction columns, screening, and paper chat |
| **Organization** | Notebooks, Schedule, status, source relationships, and review history | Research workflows, tables, reports, alerts, and review notebooks |
| **Citations** | Keeps paper metadata and source links | Evidence-backed answers and research exports, not cite-while-you-write |
| **Storage** | Local files and SQLite in your iCloud | Cloud service |

*Elicit pricing and limits checked against its [official pricing page](https://elicit.com/pricing) in August 2026.*

## Where Elicit is better

- **Finding the evidence.** Search a vast scholarly corpus without first assembling a library.
- **Systematic reviews.** Dedicated screening and extraction workflows can process thousands of papers with explicit criteria.
- **Structured synthesis.** Custom columns make it easy to compare methods, populations, interventions, and outcomes.
- **Research reports.** Elicit can build an evidence-backed answer from many academic sources and expose its supporting papers.
- **Team and API options.** Higher plans support larger workflows, collaboration, alerts, and programmatic access.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **Your chosen sources persist together.** Papers live beside the articles, talks, podcasts, books, and meetings that shaped the same notebook.
- **The library belongs to you.** Files and metadata remain local and in your private iCloud rather than requiring a hosted research workspace.
- **AI is model-flexible.** Use several providers or an existing assistant subscription through MCP.
- **Reading and listening are first-class.** Work through the complete source, not only the extracted evidence table.
- **Learning continues after synthesis.** Schedule sources and test your own explanation through a saved review.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Elicit** when the bottleneck is finding, screening, and extracting evidence for a literature or systematic review.

Choose **ForeverLM** when the bottleneck is managing everything you have selected and turning it into durable understanding.

The tools are complementary: discover and screen in Elicit, export the papers that matter, then learn them in ForeverLM.

# ForeverLM vs SciSpace

SciSpace is an end-to-end academic research platform for discovering literature, running deep reviews, chatting with PDFs, generating citations, and assisting with academic writing. ForeverLM is a personal research library for the sources you actually keep, including material beyond scholarly papers, with listening, planning, and active review built in.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | SciSpace |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free Basic with credits; Premium starts at $12/month billed annually |
| **Core job** | Long-term source library and learning loop | Academic search, literature review, PDF explanation, and writing tools |
| **Discovery** | Imports and plugins; not a scholarly search engine | Search and agentic review across scientific literature |
| **AI** | Configurable models, cross-source Chat, and MCP assistants | Literature Review, Deep Review, Chat with PDF, paraphrasing, and AI detection |
| **Sources** | Papers, articles, books, podcasts, videos, courses, and more | Primarily scholarly literature and academic writing |
| **Storage** | Local SQLite and files in private iCloud | Cloud workspace |
| **Review** | Scheduled review dialogue with saved history | Research synthesis rather than learner assessment |

*SciSpace product scope and credit pricing checked against its [official pricing](https://scispace.com/pricing) and [credit guide](https://scispace.com/resources/credits-pricing-guide/) in August 2026.*

## Where SciSpace is better

- **Literature discovery.** It searches beyond your own files and can assemble a review from published research.
- **Academic workflow breadth.** Search, explain, paraphrase, cite, detect AI-written text, and format manuscripts in one web platform.
- **PDF explanation.** Its Copilot-style experience is focused specifically on making academic language and figures easier to understand.
- **Deep research automation.** Agent credits fund longer searches and reviews that would be manual library work in ForeverLM.
- **Web access.** It works wherever a browser is available rather than requiring a Mac for the full experience.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **A broader definition of research.** The decisive source may be a podcast interview, lecture, book, article, or meeting, not another journal paper.
- **Persistent ownership.** The library is stored locally and through your Apple account.
- **Conversation can change the library.** MCP assistants can organize notebooks, schedule work, and save reviews instead of only returning an answer.
- **Listening is part of reading.** Papers and articles can be narrated without leaving the source workflow.
- **Understanding is the outcome.** ForeverLM asks you to explain the material back and records where your explanation broke down.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **SciSpace** for literature discovery, automated academic review, PDF explanation, and writing assistance.

Choose **ForeverLM** for a private, durable research library that joins papers with the rest of your intellectual life and helps you retain what you read.

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/obsidian.md -->

# ForeverLM vs Obsidian

Obsidian is the gold standard for owning your notes: free, local Markdown files, endlessly extensible through community plugins. ForeverLM shares Obsidian's core value — your data lives on your machine, not in someone's cloud — but it solves a different problem. Obsidian is a place to *write and link notes*. ForeverLM is a system to *track what you consume and verify you understood it*. See [Why not a note-taking app?](/why-quizzing#why-not-a-note-taking-app)

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Obsidian |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost; iCloud sync included, no paid sync tier | Free (core app, including commercial use). Sync add-on $4–8/mo; Publish $8/mo |
| **AI costs** | Your own OpenRouter key, billed by OpenRouter at cost with nothing added, for any model in Chat (free models cost nothing); or an AI subscription you already pay for, over MCP | No built-in AI; community plugins, almost all bring-your-own-key |
| **Platforms** | Native macOS app (macOS 14+) | macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, Android |
| **Data storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container, CloudKit sync | Local Markdown files; optional E2E-encrypted paid sync, or DIY iCloud/git sync |
| **Source ingestion** | Automatic: Safari reading list, Apple Podcasts, PDFs, papers, books, YouTube, X posts | None built in — web clipper for articles; everything else via plugins or manual |
| **Podcasts** | Follow shows, full episode transcripts | Not supported natively |
| **Review method** | Review dialogue with an AI tutor | None built in; community spaced-repetition plugins, self-graded |
| **Model choice** | Any MCP-compatible AI, or any model in-app through your own OpenRouter key | Whatever a plugin supports (BYOK, incl. local models via Ollama) |
| **Export** | Files on your Mac; SQLite you can open | Zero lock-in — it's already a folder of .md files |

*Pricing verified July 2026 — check [obsidian.md/pricing](https://obsidian.md/pricing) for current numbers.*

## Pricing: both respect your wallet

Obsidian's core app is genuinely free, and if you sync via iCloud or git, it stays free. Paid Sync is $48–96/yr. AI features require assembling plugins and paying per-token with your own keys.

ForeverLM is free, and iCloud sync is included: there's no paid sync tier to graduate onto. AI is a separate bill you control: the in-app Chat runs on your own OpenRouter key, billed by OpenRouter at its cost with nothing added, or on free models for nothing. Driving the app over MCP from a Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok subscription you already have is the one paid part: 7 days free, then $19 once. Neither product puts a subscription between you and your own data. The difference is that Obsidian leaves the AI wiring to you, and ForeverLM wires your key in for you.

## Where Obsidian is better

- **It runs everywhere**, Windows, Linux, and Android included, and its core app costs nothing. ForeverLM is free too, but it is Mac-centered, and its built-in AI needs your own OpenRouter key.
- **Freeform thinking.** Backlinks, graph view, canvas, daily notes — if you want to write, link, and structure your own ideas, Obsidian is built for exactly that. ForeverLM deliberately isn't a note-taking app.
- **Ultimate data ownership.** Plain Markdown on disk beats every other storage model for longevity, including ForeverLM's SQLite-plus-iCloud.
- **The plugin ecosystem.** Thousands of community plugins; if you can imagine a workflow, someone has built it.
- **Local AI.** Plugins can run against Ollama models entirely offline — ForeverLM's AI review requires a cloud provider.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **Capture is automatic.** Obsidian ingests nothing by itself — no articles, no podcasts, no papers, no highlights. ForeverLM auto-discovers sources from your Safari reading list, Apple Podcasts follows, and reference managers. Many Obsidian users pay $120/yr for Readwise just to pipe content in.
- **A learning loop exists out of the box.** Obsidian has no review system; spaced-repetition plugins are self-graded flashcards you configure and maintain yourself. ForeverLM ships a weekly Schedule, AI review sessions, and per-source understanding history — no assembly required.
- **The AI reads your actual sources.** Through MCP, Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok can search your whole library, pull full source text, quiz you on it, and save the review back. Obsidian AI plugins mostly operate on your notes, not on original source material.
- **Sources, not just notes about sources.** ForeverLM tracks the article, the paper PDF, the episode transcript itself — with a built-in Reader and Text to Speech — so review is grounded in what the author wrote, not what you managed to write down.
- **Zero blank-canvas problem.** Obsidian's flexibility is also its tax: you design and maintain your own system. ForeverLM has one opinionated loop: track, schedule, read or listen, explain it back.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Obsidian** if your center of gravity is writing and linking your own notes, you need Windows/Linux/Android, or you enjoy building a personal system from plugins.

Choose **ForeverLM** if you're on a Mac and your problem isn't note storage — it's that you read, watch, and listen to a flood of material and retain too little of it.

Many people run both: Obsidian for thinking and writing, ForeverLM for tracking sources and verifying understanding. Both keep your data local, so neither locks the other out.

# ForeverLM vs DEVONthink

DEVONthink is a powerful document and information manager for Mac and iOS. It archives almost anything, searches large databases, links related material, automates filing, and now includes an AI chat assistant. ForeverLM is narrower: it organizes the sources you intend to learn from and connects them to listening, AI conversation, scheduling, and review.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | DEVONthink 4 |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Standard $99, Pro $199, Server $499; one-time license with one year of updates |
| **Primary job** | Research library and learning loop | General document archive and information manager |
| **Storage** | Local SQLite and files in your private iCloud container | Local databases with flexible sync options |
| **AI** | Configurable in-app models plus Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok through MCP | AI chat with supported local or external models |
| **Automation** | Automatic source plugins and AI-operable notebooks and Schedule | Deep rules, smart groups, scripts, actions, and triggers |
| **Source types** | Learning-specific handling for papers, articles, books, podcasts, videos, courses, and meetings | Broad file, email, feed, web, scan, and document support |
| **Review** | Scheduled review dialogue with saved history | No equivalent source-understanding workflow |

*DEVONthink pricing checked against [DEVONtechnologies](https://shop.devontechnologies.com/apps/devonthink/pricing) in August 2026. Licenses do not expire, but continued updates are sold separately.*

## Where DEVONthink is better

- **Document management depth.** It is built for very large, heterogeneous archives rather than a curated learning queue.
- **Automation.** Filing rules, smart groups, scripts, OCR, triggers, and integrations can support demanding professional workflows.
- **Search and classification.** DEVONthink has decades of experience finding and relating material across databases.
- **Scanning and records.** Pro is a stronger home for receipts, email archives, legal files, and scanned office documents.
- **Flexible ownership.** Local databases, multiple sync methods, durable exports, and a perpetual license appeal to privacy-conscious Mac users.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **It understands learning sources.** A podcast episode, paper, book, and course are not generic files. Each gets source-specific ingestion, reading, and playback behavior.
- **The queue has a purpose.** Schedule what to learn this week and track whether it was reviewed, not merely archived.
- **AI interaction is portable.** Use in-app Chat or let an external MCP assistant operate the library and save the resulting review.
- **Active understanding is built in.** Review dialogue probes gaps and preserves the session against the sources covered.
- **A lower one-time price.** ForeverLM itself is free; MCP is the only paid part, $19 once after 7 free days, against $99 for DEVONthink Standard.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **DEVONthink** if you need a serious Mac document archive, advanced automation, OCR, email capture, and broad information management.

Choose **ForeverLM** if the important question is not “Where did I file this?” but “Did I understand and retain it?”

Many researchers can use both: DEVONthink as the institutional memory, ForeverLM as the active learning queue.

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/liquidtext.md -->

# ForeverLM vs LiquidText

LiquidText is a deep-reading workspace for pulling excerpts out of PDFs and web pages, arranging them spatially, linking ideas, comparing distant passages, and collaborating around documents. ForeverLM is less visual and less annotation-heavy. Its strength is keeping many source types in one library and turning them into a repeatable workflow of reading, listening, conversation, scheduling, and review.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | LiquidText |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free Basic; paid purchases and Live subscriptions vary by platform and region |
| **Best for** | Long-term research library and learning | Close reading, excerpting, and spatial synthesis |
| **Sources** | Papers, articles, books, podcasts, videos, courses, meetings, and more | PDFs, documents, web pages, and reference-manager imports |
| **Annotation** | Reader, extracted text and figures, notes, and source chat | Rich ink, highlights, margin notes, excerpt workspaces, and live links |
| **Visual thinking** | Notebooks, plus an ideas-first Canvas where sources hang off your Ideas as evidence (in beta releases) | Flexible workspace for arranging and connecting excerpts |
| **Collaboration** | AI assistants can operate the library; human collaboration is limited | Near-real-time shared notebooks and comments on paid plans |
| **Review** | Scheduled review dialogue with saved history | Active reading and synthesis, without the same review loop |

*LiquidText features checked against its [official App Store listing](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/liquidtext/id922765270) in August 2026. Its purchase catalog is complex and regional, so check the current in-app offer.*

## Where LiquidText is better

- **Deep PDF interaction.** Pinch, collapse, compare, excerpt, and annotate dense documents in ways a conventional reader cannot match.
- **Spatial synthesis.** Arrange evidence from multiple documents on a workspace and draw links between it.
- **Handwriting.** Apple Pencil and freeform ink are central, not secondary.
- **Traceability.** Tapping an excerpt returns to its original context, which is excellent for close reading and legal or academic evidence work.
- **Human collaboration.** Shared workspaces support comments and near-real-time co-editing.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **The library goes beyond documents.** Podcasts, videos, books, courses, and meetings belong beside PDFs.
- **Source capture is broader.** Reading lists, podcast follows, plugins, URLs, files, and MCP assistants can feed the same system.
- **AI can compare complete sources.** Discuss a notebook without first extracting every relevant passage to a canvas.
- **Listening is built in.** Read papers and articles aloud while keeping playback connected to the source.
- **The workflow closes with review.** Schedule a source, explain it back, and preserve the assessment.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **LiquidText** if your work depends on close PDF annotation, handwriting, visual evidence arrangement, and passage-level comparison.

Choose **ForeverLM** if you need one private library for every source format and want AI-assisted learning to continue after reading.

The combination is natural: synthesize difficult documents in LiquidText, then retain the source set and review it in ForeverLM.

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/marginnote.md -->

# ForeverLM vs MarginNote

MarginNote 4 combines PDF and EPUB reading, highlighting, mind maps, flashcards, OCR, video notes, and AI assistance on Apple devices. It is one of the closest comparisons for students who want reading and review in the same product. ForeverLM trades MarginNote's detailed visual annotation system for broader source capture, cross-source AI, podcasts, listening, and an assistant-accessible Schedule.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | MarginNote 4 |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Pro $12.99 lifetime on iPhone/iPad; Max $16.99/year or $51.99 lifetime |
| **Platforms** | Mac-centered with synced iPhone access | Mac, iPhone, and iPad, depending on plan |
| **Reading** | Papers, articles, books, and transcripts | Deep PDF and EPUB reading with OCR and visual extraction |
| **Knowledge structure** | Notebooks, source relationships, search, and Schedule | One card can be a highlight, mind-map node, and flashcard |
| **AI** | Configurable models, source chat, and external MCP assistants | Credit-based summary, Q&A, OCR, translation, and card generation |
| **Review** | Review dialogue grounded in complete sources | Flashcards, FSRS, document recall, and mind-map recall |
| **Beyond documents** | Podcasts, videos, courses, meetings, and X posts | Local and online video notes, but primarily document-centered |

*MarginNote pricing and AI credit rules checked against its [official pricing page](https://www.marginnote.com/en/pricing/) in August 2026.*

## Where MarginNote is better

- **Annotation becomes structure.** A single excerpt can appear as a document highlight, mind-map node, and flashcard.
- **Visual study.** Mind maps, outlines, links, and extended notes make relationships explicit.
- **Handwriting and OCR.** It is designed for iPad study with scanned material and Apple Pencil.
- **Several recall modes.** FSRS cards, hidden annotations, and progressive mind-map reveal support different kinds of rehearsal.
- **Low one-time pricing.** Lifetime options are unusually affordable, though AI remains credit-metered.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **More source streams arrive automatically.** Articles, papers, podcasts, books, videos, courses, meetings, and plugins share one library.
- **Podcasts are first-class.** Follow shows, keep episode transcripts, and review them like any other source.
- **AI can operate across the system.** MCP assistants can retrieve sources, plan days, move work, and save review transcripts.
- **Conversation tests explanation.** Review emphasizes articulating the full idea rather than recognizing a card answer.
- **Data and model flexibility.** Source files stay in your iCloud, and the model can be chosen per task.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **MarginNote** if you study primarily from PDFs and EPUBs and want a tightly integrated system of annotation, mind maps, and flashcards.

Choose **ForeverLM** if your learning spans many formats and you want the library, AI assistants, schedule, listening, and conversational review to work as one system.

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/recall.md -->

# ForeverLM vs Recall

Recall (recall.it, formerly getrecall.ai) is a self-organizing AI knowledge base: save articles, YouTube videos, PDFs, and podcasts; get AI summaries, auto-tagging, a knowledge graph, and spaced-repetition quizzes. It's the closest competitor to ForeverLM in spirit — both are local-first, both cover many source types, both take retention seriously. The differences are in pricing model, platform, and how deep the review goes.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Recall |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free tier (10 AI summaries/mo); Plus $120/yr; Max $456/yr (billed yearly) |
| **AI costs** | Your own OpenRouter key, billed by OpenRouter at cost with nothing added, for any model in Chat (free models cost nothing); or an AI subscription you already pay for, over MCP | Included in subscription; model auto-selected on Plus, model choice only on Max |
| **Platforms** | Native macOS app (macOS 14+) | Web app + browser extensions, iOS, Android — no native desktop app |
| **Data storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container, CloudKit sync | Local-first on device; sync via Recall's cloud (Google Cloud, EU) |
| **Source ingestion** | Automatic: Safari reading list, Apple Podcasts follows, PDFs, papers, books, YouTube, X posts | Manual saves via extension/app: articles, YouTube, PDFs, podcasts, X, Reddit |
| **Review method** | Cards you keep from your sources on a spaced schedule, and review dialogue with an AI tutor that reads the full source | Spaced-repetition quizzes (question/answer style) — paid tier only |
| **MCP / assistant access** | Full MCP control surface: search, schedule, run and save review sessions | MCP + API access (retrieval) |
| **Export** | Files on your Mac; SQLite you can open | Markdown zip export (web app only), API |

*Pricing verified July 2026 — check [recall.it/pricing](https://www.recall.it/pricing) for current numbers; Recall raised Plus pricing at its 2.0 relaunch in April 2026.*

## Pricing: $120+/yr subscription vs a free app + your own AI key

Recall's free tier stores unlimited content but allows only **10 AI summaries a month** — the product's core is effectively paid. Plus is **$120/yr billed yearly**, and choosing which AI model answers you costs **$456/yr** on Max.

ForeverLM has no tiers to climb, because it has no tiers: the app is **free**, and every model in the in-app Chat is open. That Chat runs on your own OpenRouter key, and OpenRouter bills you at its cost with nothing added by ForeverLM; its free models cost nothing. Or connect whichever of Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok you already subscribe to over MCP: your subscription covers the inference. MCP is the one paid part: 7 days free, then $19 once. The in-app ledger accounts for it to the cent. There's no tier where the model picker lives, because the model picker was never behind one.

## Where Recall is better

- **Works everywhere.** Web app, iOS, and Android — save and review from any device. ForeverLM is Mac-only.
- **AI that stays free with no key.** Recall's free tier keeps giving you 10 AI summaries a month indefinitely at $0 with nothing to set up. ForeverLM's app is free, and its built-in AI needs your own OpenRouter key; free models on it cost nothing.
- **Knowledge graph and auto-tagging.** Recall automatically links related saves into a browsable graph; ForeverLM organizes by notebooks, source type, and Schedule instead.
- **Augmented browsing.** Recall's extension surfaces your saved knowledge while you browse the web.
- **Reddit imports.** Recall ingests Reddit threads; ForeverLM doesn't.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **Deeper review.** Recall's spaced-repetition quizzes are generated Q&A cards. ForeverLM runs an explain-it-back conversation: you explain the source in your own words and an AI tutor with the full text probes for gaps and follows up. And review isn't paywalled behind a higher tier — see [Why Quizzing?](/why-quizzing)
- **Sources arrive by themselves.** Recall ingestion is save-by-save via the extension. ForeverLM auto-discovers from your Safari reading list, Apple Podcasts follows, and reference managers — your library reflects what you actually consume.
- **Podcasts as first-class sources.** Follow shows, get full episode transcripts, read or listen, and get quizzed on them — not just saved links.
- **Your cloud, not theirs.** Both apps are local-first, but Recall syncs through Recall's servers on Google Cloud; ForeverLM syncs through your own iCloud account, and the app's servers never store your library.
- **A study planner.** The weekly Schedule assigns sources to days with completion tracking and review history; Recall has a review queue but no planning surface.
- **No tiers and no caps.** No monthly summary allowance to ration, no model-choice upsell, no subscription needed (the app is free; MCP is $19 once); OpenRouter bills what you actually used, and nothing when you don't.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Recall** if you need Android, Windows, or the web — or you want a free place to pile up saves with light AI summaries and are happy with card-style quizzing at $120/yr.

Choose **ForeverLM** if you're on a Mac and want the deeper loop: automatic source capture including full podcast transcripts, a weekly plan, review with the AI of your choice, and a library that lives in your own iCloud — free, plus $19 once if you want MCP after its 7 free days, plus only what your AI use actually costs.

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/snipd.md -->

# ForeverLM vs Snipd

Snipd is the best-known AI podcast player: tap your headphones mid-episode and it captures a "snip" with transcript, AI summary, and chapter context. It's a capture tool for your ears. ForeverLM treats podcasts differently — full episodes become study sources with complete transcripts, scheduled alongside your articles and papers, and reviewed with an AI tutor afterwards. The two solve different halves of the same problem.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Snipd |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost | Free (AI on 2 episodes/week); Premium advertised from $6.99/mo; US App Store shows ~$11.99/mo monthly, annual plans vary by region |
| **AI costs** | Your own OpenRouter key, billed by OpenRouter at cost with nothing added, for any model in Chat (free models cost nothing); or an AI subscription you already pay for, over MCP | Included in Premium, capped at 900 min of AI processing/month |
| **Platforms** | Native macOS app (macOS 14+) | iOS, Android, Apple Watch, CarPlay — no Mac, Windows, or web app |
| **Data storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container | Snipd's cloud; App Store privacy label lists identity-linked usage data, including for advertising |
| **Scope** | Podcasts *plus* articles, papers, books, YouTube, X posts — one library | Podcasts only (Premium adds own audio files and YouTube) |
| **Podcast model** | Follow shows via Apple Podcasts, full episode transcripts as readable sources | Streaming player with tap-to-snip highlights, AI summaries, chapters |
| **Review method** | Review dialogue with an AI tutor | None — snips export to Readwise/Notion/Obsidian for someone else to resurface |
| **Export** | Files on your Mac; SQLite you can open | Good: auto-sync of snips to Readwise, Notion, Obsidian; markdown |

*Pricing verified July 2026 — Snipd's price varies by region and billing period; check [snipd.com/pricing](https://www.snipd.com/pricing) and your local App Store.*

## Pricing: subscription with a cap vs your own AI key

Snipd Premium runs roughly **$70–$100+/yr** depending on region and billing period (the website advertises from $6.99/mo; the US App Store lists ~$11.99/mo billed monthly), with a 900-minute monthly cap on AI processing. The free tier limits AI features to two episodes a week. You pay a fixed amount and still hit a ceiling.

ForeverLM is **free**, and podcast transcripts are simply part of the app. AI is a separate bill you control: bring your own OpenRouter key, which OpenRouter bills at its cost with nothing added, or use free models. Review through the assistant you already subscribe to (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok over MCP) is the one paid part, 7 days free then $19 once, with your subscription covering the inference; review in the in-app Chat costs what OpenRouter bills your key for it. Transcript cleanup and other background work bills the same way.

## Where Snipd is better

- **Capture while listening.** Tap your headphones while driving or walking and the moment is saved with context. ForeverLM has no listening-time capture gesture — it's not a podcast player.
- **Mobile-first.** iPhone, Android, Apple Watch, CarPlay. ForeverLM focuses on Mac and iPhone.
- **Listening experience.** Speaker-labeled transcripts, AI chapters, episode Q&A, personalized digests — a genuinely great player.
- **Note-app integrations.** Snips flow automatically into Readwise, Notion, and Obsidian.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **Retention actually happens.** Snipd captures highlights; it has no review system — remembering is outsourced to whatever app you export to. ForeverLM closes the loop: episodes land on your weekly Schedule and you review them in a review dialogue with an AI that has the full transcript. See [Why Quizzing?](/why-quizzing)
- **The whole episode, not just the moments you caught.** A snip is the sentence you reacted to. ForeverLM ingests the complete transcript — readable, searchable, quotable in review — so the AI can quiz you on the argument, not the soundbite.
- **Podcasts beside everything else.** Your podcast episodes sit in the same library and same review loop as articles, papers, books, and videos. Snipd is podcasts-only.
- **Privacy posture.** Your library lives in your iCloud; ForeverLM servers don't store it. Snipd's processing is cloud-side, and its App Store privacy label discloses identity-linked data collection including for advertising.
- **No ceiling to hit.** Snipd stops at 900 AI minutes a month no matter what you paid, and a heavy listening month is exactly when you'd want more. ForeverLM has no cap of that kind — a busy month simply adds to your OpenRouter bill, and a quiet one adds nothing.

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Snipd** as your podcast *player* — especially if you listen on the go and want frictionless highlight capture on iPhone or Android.

Choose **ForeverLM** if the goal is *learning from* podcasts: full transcripts as study sources, scheduled review, and an AI tutor that verifies you understood the episode.

Honestly, they stack well: listen and snip in Snipd, then let ForeverLM's Apple Podcasts integration pull the same shows in as transcripts for scheduled, deeper review on your Mac.
