<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/paper-ac.md -->

# ForeverLM vs Paper (paper.ac)

Paper (paper.ac) is a study workspace that sets out to replace NotebookLM, Notion, Anki and Quizlet at once. You upload PDFs, lectures, videos and web pages, chat with them, and turn them into notes, FSRS flashcards, quizzes, podcasts and slide decks, all inside a Notion-style editor. It is free while in beta. ForeverLM overlaps on the study loop. It differs on where the library lives (your iCloud, not a vendor's cloud), which AI runs it (any model, or the assistant you already use), and how sources arrive (on their own, podcasts included).

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Paper |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost, or over MCP from an assistant you already pay for | Free during the beta ("free unlimited credits"); paid plans for heavier use are announced but not priced |
| **Platforms** | Native macOS app (macOS 14+), with an iPhone app and a web library | Web app (works in mobile browsers); a Mac desktop app in testing; a native mobile app planned |
| **Data storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container, CloudKit sync | Paper's cloud (Supabase on AWS, region not stated), encrypted in transit and at rest, not end-to-end |
| **AI models** | Any model through your own OpenRouter key, or Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok over MCP | Grok by default, GPT and Gemini per chat (its roadmap lists Claude as added); no bring-your-own-key yet |
| **Assistant access** | A full MCP server: search, add sources, run reviews, write Pages | No MCP; a public API is on the roadmap |
| **Sources** | Papers with their PDFs, articles, books, podcasts (follow shows, full transcripts), YouTube, X posts, meetings; reading lists and Apple Podcasts arrive on their own | What you upload or link: PDF (with OCR), audio, video, EPUB, Word, PowerPoint, Markdown, web pages, YouTube, Notion and Outline imports |
| **Flashcards** | Cards drafted from what you finish, kept or skipped by you, reviewed on a schedule | FSRS flashcards (basic and cloze), up to 75 per generation |
| **Review** | Explain a source back to a tutor that reads its whole text; saved per source | Quizzes and self-graded review sessions of 8–15 questions |
| **Audio** | A one-narrator audio overview (deep dive, brief or critique); Text to Speech reads the source itself | Generated podcasts, solo or two hosts, up to 60 minutes |
| **Export** | Files on your Mac; SQLite you can open | Notes as Markdown; a full-account export by email request |

*Checked against paper.ac's own pages (FAQ, How it works, Security, Docs, Roadmap and Changelog) in October 2026. Paper is in beta and changes quickly, so check [paper.ac](https://paper.ac) for its current state.*

## Pricing: a free beta vs a free app and your own key

Paper costs nothing while it is in beta, with no key to bring. Its terms already describe monthly billing for paid features, and its own pages say paid tiers may come later for heavy use, large libraries and teams. No prices are published yet, so Paper's cost today is $0 and its long-term cost is unknown.

ForeverLM is free, with no subscription and no tiers; only MCP, the connection for an outside assistant, is paid: 7 days free, then $19 once. The models run on your own OpenRouter key, which OpenRouter bills at its own price with nothing added by ForeverLM. You can also connect the Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok subscription you already pay for over MCP. The app shows what every conversation cost, to the cent.

## Where Paper is better

- **It is free today.** No key and nothing to pay during the beta.
- **It runs anywhere there is a browser.** Windows, Linux, Chromebooks and phones all work. ForeverLM is Mac-centered.
- **Two-host podcasts and slide decks.** Paper's podcasts can have one or two hosts and run up to an hour, and it makes slide decks from any source. ForeverLM's audio overview has one narrator, and it makes no slides.
- **FSRS with four ratings.** Paper schedules cards with FSRS and rates them Again, Hard, Good or Easy, with cloze cards for definitions. ForeverLM's cards have two buttons, Forgot and Remembered.
- **A writing and team workspace.** A Notion-style block editor, boards with timelines, and channels and direct messages for working with others.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **Your library stays in your iCloud.** Paper keeps everything on its own cloud, without end-to-end encryption or a SOC 2 report, and a full export means emailing them. ForeverLM's library is a SQLite database and files in your private iCloud container, and its servers never hold it.
- **Any model, and the assistant you already use.** Paper chooses among Grok, GPT and Gemini, with no key of your own. ForeverLM runs any model on your OpenRouter key, and Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok can work in your library over MCP.
- **Sources arrive on their own.** Safari, Chrome and Brave reading lists, Apple Podcasts episodes with full transcripts, X bookmarks, YouTube likes and meeting transcripts. Paper holds what you upload or paste.
- **Review that checks understanding.** You explain a source back to a tutor that has read all of it and probes the gaps, and the result stays with the source. Cards are drafted for you as you finish things. See [Why Quizzing?](/why-quizzing)
- **A price you can read today.** ForeverLM states what it costs now. Paper's paid tiers are announced but not priced.
- **Gemini Notebook moves in whole.** Paste a notebook's link and its sources, chats and notes arrive as a ForeverLM notebook ([Importing a Gemini Notebook](/studio#importing-a-gemini-notebook)).

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Paper** if you want a free, browser-based study workspace with podcasts, slides and FSRS flashcards today, and you don't mind your library living on its cloud.

Choose **ForeverLM** if you're on a Mac and want one private library you keep for years: sources that arrive on their own, any model you like, and review that checks you understood what you read, watched or heard.

# ForeverLM vs Memo (memo.cards)

Memo (memo.cards, formerly PDF2Anki) was built by medical students to turn study material into flashcards. It has grown into an AI study workspace: upload lectures, PDFs, slides and videos, then get FSRS flashcards, practice tests, notes, mind maps, podcasts and guided voice walkthroughs, with export straight to Anki. It runs on almost every platform. ForeverLM is aimed at a different job: one private library of everything you read, watch and listen to, kept in your own iCloud, with review that checks you understood it.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Memo |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost, or over MCP from an assistant you already pay for | Free plan (limits not published); Pro $20/mo or $120/yr; Max $50/mo or $300/yr. Usage draws on a monthly "energy" balance with no fixed number of generations |
| **Platforms** | Native macOS app (macOS 14+), with an iPhone app and a web library | Web, Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS; Android as a web app; Chrome extension |
| **Data storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container, CloudKit sync | Memo's cloud; hosting provider and region not stated; a copy of your data on request |
| **AI models** | Any model through your own OpenRouter key, or Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok over MCP | Standard, Thinking and Pro modes; the models are not named; no bring-your-own-key |
| **Assistant access** | A full MCP server: search, add sources, draft cards, run reviews | None documented |
| **Sources** | Papers with their PDFs, articles, books, podcasts (follow shows, full transcripts), YouTube, X posts, meetings; reading lists and Apple Podcasts arrive on their own | What you upload or link: PDF, Word, PowerPoint, spreadsheets, EPUB, audio, video, images, YouTube, web pages; lecture recordings through its extension |
| **Flashcards** | Cards drafted from what you finish, kept or skipped by you, reviewed with Forgot and Remembered | FSRS scheduling; basic, quiz, cloze and image-occlusion cards; Anki (.apkg) and RemNote export |
| **Review** | Explain a source back to a tutor that reads its whole text; saved per source | Practice tests and AI tutors, including a voice tutor |
| **Audio** | A one-narrator audio overview (deep dive, brief or critique); Text to Speech reads the source itself | Podcasts of about 3 to 15 minutes; guided voice walkthroughs (Track Mode) |
| **Export** | Files on your Mac; SQLite you can open | Cards to Anki and RemNote; notes as PDF, Markdown or text |

*Checked against memo.cards's pricing, FAQ, help center and download pages and its App Store listing in October 2026. Prices are the web prices; the iOS app lists different in-app prices, so check [memo.cards](https://www.memo.cards/en/pricing) for the offer where you buy.*

## Pricing: an energy meter vs your own key

Memo's free plan needs no card, and its paid plans are Pro at $20 a month ($120 billed yearly) and Max at $50 a month ($300 billed yearly). What a plan buys is a monthly balance of "energy", and Memo says a plan does not promise a fixed number of generations. You find out how far it goes by using it.

ForeverLM is free, with no subscription and no tiers; only MCP, the connection for an outside assistant, is paid: 7 days free, then $19 once. The models run on your own OpenRouter key, which OpenRouter bills at its own price with nothing added by ForeverLM, and the app shows what every conversation cost, to the cent. You can also connect the Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok subscription you already pay for over MCP.

## Where Memo is better

- **Flashcards are its core.** FSRS scheduling, cloze and image-occlusion cards, and export to Anki with image occlusion intact. For exam memorization, such as medical school, it is the stronger card tool.
- **Every platform.** Web, Mac, Windows, Linux and iOS, with Android as a web app. ForeverLM is Mac-centered.
- **More output styles.** Mind maps, infographics, several note formats (Cornell among them), podcasts and guided voice walkthroughs.
- **A free plan with no key.** You can start without an API key or a card.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **Your library stays in your iCloud.** Memo keeps your material on its own cloud and names neither its hosting provider nor most of its AI providers. ForeverLM's library is a SQLite database and files in your private iCloud container, and its servers never hold it.
- **Any model, and the assistant you already use.** Memo's modes don't say which model answers. ForeverLM runs any model you choose on your own key, and Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok can work in your library over MCP.
- **Costs you can read.** An energy balance makes cost a guess. ForeverLM records every call's price.
- **Sources arrive on their own.** Reading lists, Apple Podcasts episodes with full transcripts, X bookmarks, YouTube likes and meeting transcripts. Memo holds what you upload.
- **A library, not decks.** Every source lives once in your library and can sit in any number of notebooks, with a Schedule and a review dialogue tied to the source. The tutor reads the whole source and probes the gaps a card can't know about. See [Why Quizzing?](/why-quizzing)
- **Gemini Notebook moves in whole.** Paste a notebook's link and its sources, chats and notes arrive as a ForeverLM notebook ([Importing a Gemini Notebook](/studio#importing-a-gemini-notebook)).

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Memo** if you're memorizing for exams, you want FSRS cards with cloze and image occlusion that export to Anki, or you need Windows, Linux or Android.

Choose **ForeverLM** if you're on a Mac and want a private, lasting library of everything you consume, with any model you like and review that checks understanding rather than recall alone.

They can sit side by side: make exam decks in Memo, and keep the papers, lectures and podcasts behind them in ForeverLM.

# ForeverLM vs Sapience

Sapience is a local knowledge workspace built around a visual canvas. Each "space" is a folder on your computer, drawn as a board of cards, concept maps and mind maps. Notes, canvases and AI chats are all plain text files, and it can open an existing Obsidian vault. Its AI researches a topic, explains material, builds a learning curriculum and gathers sources, and it keeps its skills and memories as notes you can read. It is in invite-only early access, and little beyond that is published yet. ForeverLM shares the local-first values and now has a Canvas of its own. Its centre is different: a library that fills itself, and review that checks you understood it.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Sapience |
|---|---|---|
| **Availability** | Available now for macOS; the newest features reach beta releases first | Invite-only early access (100 tester places announced for Q2 2026) |
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost, or over MCP from an assistant you already pay for | Not published; "start free", no card needed for sign-up |
| **Platforms** | Native macOS app (macOS 14+), with an iPhone app and a web library | Not stated (its screenshots show a Mac app) |
| **Data storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container, CloudKit sync | Plain text files in folders on your computer; sync not stated |
| **Canvas** | Ideas-first Canvas over the whole library: Ideas, regions inside regions, arrows, sources as evidence (in beta releases) | The centre of the app: every folder is a canvas of cards, concept maps and mind maps, and chats can sit on a board |
| **AI models** | Any model through your own OpenRouter key, or Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok over MCP | Not stated |
| **Sources** | Papers with their PDFs, articles, books, podcasts (follow shows, full transcripts), YouTube, X posts, meetings; reading lists and Apple Podcasts arrive on their own | Books, papers, websites and YouTube videos, "and more" |
| **Retention** | Weekly Schedule, cards drafted as you finish sources, and a review dialogue saved per source | None stated; its AI can draw up a learning curriculum |
| **Export** | Files on your Mac; SQLite you can open | Nothing to export: notes, canvases and chats are already plain files |

*Checked against sapience.so in October 2026. Sapience is in early access and publishes little so far, so this page will change as it does; check [sapience.so](https://sapience.so) for its current state.*

## Where Sapience is better

- **Plain files, no lock-in.** Everything is a text file in your own folders, and an Obsidian vault opens as it is. ForeverLM's library is open too, a SQLite database and files in your iCloud, but it is a database, not a folder of notes.
- **The canvas is the app.** Sapience is canvas-first, with cards, concept maps and mind maps on every space. ForeverLM's Canvas is newer and still in beta releases.
- **AI memory you can read.** Its AI keeps its skills and memories as notes in your workspace, so you can see and edit what it knows.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **Available, and documented.** ForeverLM ships today, with its platforms, prices and models stated. Sapience is invite-only, and says nothing yet about its platforms, models or price.
- **The library fills itself.** Reading lists, Apple Podcasts episodes with full transcripts, X bookmarks, YouTube likes and meeting transcripts arrive without being dragged in.
- **Saving leads to remembering.** A Schedule, cards drafted as you finish sources, and a review dialogue in which a tutor who has read the whole source checks that you understood it. See [Why Quizzing?](/why-quizzing)
- **A canvas wired to its sources.** On ForeverLM's Canvas a paper can show only its figures, a passage card opens the paper at that passage, and a figure boxed in the Reader drags onto the board.
- **Any model, and the assistant you already use.** Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok can search your library, add to it and run your reviews over MCP.
- **On every Apple device.** Your library syncs through your iCloud to your other Macs, the iPhone app and the web library.
- **Gemini Notebook moves in whole.** Paste a notebook's link and its sources, chats and notes arrive as a ForeverLM notebook ([Importing a Gemini Notebook](/studio#importing-a-gemini-notebook)).

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Sapience** if you think on a canvas, want every note to stay a plain file in your own folders, already work in Obsidian, and can get an early-access place.

Choose **ForeverLM** if you want a library that gathers what you read, watch and hear by itself, with any model you like, and review that makes it stick.

# ForeverLM vs Gistr

Gistr calls itself an AI-native notebook. You save YouTube videos, podcasts, PDFs and articles, ask questions about them in threads, and write notes that link back to the exact timestamp or page, grouped into collections. Plans are credit-based, with stronger models and deep research on the higher tiers. ForeverLM shares the "keep what you watch and hear" idea. It differs on where the library lives (your iCloud), which AI runs it (any model, at what it costs), and what happens after saving: a schedule, cards and review.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | Gistr |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost, or over MCP from an assistant you already pay for | Free (500 credits/mo, 5 collections, 5 sources per thread); Curious $8/mo; Explorer $16/mo; Thinker $40/mo; yearly billing gives two months free |
| **Platforms** | Native macOS app (macOS 14+), with an iPhone app and a web library | Web, Chrome extension, Android; iOS in development; no desktop app |
| **Data storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container, CloudKit sync | Gistr's cloud; hosting provider and region not stated; says your content is never used for training |
| **AI models** | Any model through your own OpenRouter key, or Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok over MCP | By tier: fast models on Free, frontier Claude, GPT and Gemini from Explorer ($16/mo); no bring-your-own-key |
| **Assistant access** | A full MCP server: search, add sources, run reviews, write Pages | None documented |
| **Sources** | Papers with their PDFs, articles, books, podcasts (follow shows, full transcripts), YouTube, X posts, meetings; reading lists and Apple Podcasts arrive on their own | What you save or upload: YouTube (playlists from Explorer), podcasts from Apple Podcasts or Spotify links, web pages, PDF, Word, PowerPoint, EPUB, Markdown, audio, images |
| **Retention** | Weekly Schedule, cards drafted as you finish sources, and a review dialogue saved per source | One-click quizzes; no flashcards or spaced repetition documented |
| **Notes** | Pages in notebooks, linked to the passages they cite | Notes linked to timestamps and pages, in threads and collections |
| **Export** | Files on your Mac; SQLite you can open | Notes as PDF, image or Markdown; other data on request |

*Checked against gistr.so's pricing, FAQ, privacy policy and terms, and its Chrome Web Store and Google Play listings, in October 2026. Check [gistr.so/pricing](https://gistr.so/pricing) for current numbers.*

## Pricing: credit tiers vs your own key

Gistr meters AI in credits: 500 a month free, 2,500 on Curious ($8), 10,000 on Explorer ($16) and 55,000 on Thinker ($40), with unused credits rolling over up to a cap on paid plans. The tier also decides the model: the most capable Claude, GPT and Gemini models start at Explorer. On the free plan, content you haven't touched for three months goes cold and has to be processed again before you can ask about it.

ForeverLM is free, with no subscription and no tiers: the whole app and every model are open. Only MCP, the connection for an outside assistant, is paid: 7 days free, then $19 once. The models run on your own OpenRouter key, which OpenRouter bills at its own price with nothing added by ForeverLM, and the app shows what every conversation cost, to the cent. You can also connect the Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok subscription you already pay for over MCP, which is what the $19 covers.

## Where Gistr is better

- **Video and podcast notes.** Notes that jump to the exact moment in a video or episode are Gistr's centre, and it takes Spotify podcast links. ForeverLM reads podcast transcripts from Apple Podcasts only.
- **Cheap to start, and on Android.** A free plan, an $8 tier, and apps for the web and Android. ForeverLM is Mac-centered.
- **Deep research built into the tiers.** Explorer and Thinker run deep research across the web from inside a thread.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **Saving is not the end.** ForeverLM schedules what you saved, drafts cards as you finish sources, and runs a review dialogue in which a tutor who has read the whole source checks that you understood it. Gistr documents quizzes, but no flashcards or spaced repetition. See [Why Quizzing?](/why-quizzing)
- **Every model, no tiers.** No tier decides which model you may use, and nothing goes cold.
- **Your library stays in your iCloud.** ForeverLM's library is a SQLite database and files in your private iCloud container, and its servers never hold it. Gistr's library lives on its cloud.
- **Sources arrive on their own.** Reading lists, Apple Podcasts episodes with full transcripts, X bookmarks, YouTube likes and meeting transcripts, without a save button.
- **The assistant you already use.** Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok can search your library, add to it and run your reviews over MCP.
- **Gemini Notebook moves in whole.** Paste a notebook's link and its sources, chats and notes arrive as a ForeverLM notebook ([Importing a Gemini Notebook](/studio#importing-a-gemini-notebook)).

## Which should you choose?

Choose **Gistr** if you mostly learn from YouTube and podcasts, want notes pinned to timestamps, and use Android or the web.

Choose **ForeverLM** if you're on a Mac and want what you watch, read and hear to land in one private library on its own, and then to stick, through a schedule, cards and review.

<!-- Source: docs-site/compare/anythingllm.md -->

# ForeverLM vs AnythingLLM

AnythingLLM, from Mintplex Labs, is an open-source (MIT) app for chatting with your documents. It comes as a free desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux or as a self-hosted Docker server. You put documents into workspaces and ask about them with any of 40-odd model providers, including fully local models that never leave your machine, and its agents can browse, query databases and call MCP tools. It is the usual pick for people who want document chat without a vendor's cloud. ForeverLM is a different kind of tool: a library of everything you read, watch and listen to, built for learning it and remembering it.

## At a glance

| | ForeverLM | AnythingLLM |
|---|---|---|
| **Price** | Free; MCP is 7 days free, then $19 once (no subscription); AI on your own OpenRouter key at cost, or over MCP from an assistant you already pay for | Desktop app free (an optional Pro subscription lifts the daily limits on its system-wide dictation, highlight-to-ask and autocomplete); self-hosting free; hosted cloud $50/mo Basic, $99/mo Pro, Enterprise by quote |
| **Platforms** | Native macOS app (macOS 14+), with an iPhone app and a web library | Mac, Windows and Linux desktop apps; Docker server; an Android app with on-device models |
| **Data storage** | Local SQLite + files in your private iCloud container, CloudKit sync | Local folders on your machine, or your own server; no built-in sync between devices |
| **AI models** | Any model through your own OpenRouter key, or Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok over MCP | 40+ providers (OpenRouter among them) plus fully local models: built in, Ollama or LM Studio |
| **MCP** | An MCP server: Claude, ChatGPT and other assistants work in your library | An MCP client: its agents call other MCP servers; it is not a server itself |
| **Sources** | Papers with their PDFs, articles, books, podcasts (follow shows, full transcripts), YouTube, X posts, meetings; reading lists and Apple Podcasts arrive on their own | Files you add (PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, EPUB, Markdown, images, audio and video transcribed), website crawls, YouTube transcripts, GitHub and GitLab repositories, Confluence, Obsidian vaults |
| **Retention** | Weekly Schedule, cards drafted as you finish sources, and a review dialogue saved per source | None: no flashcards, quizzes or spaced repetition |
| **Outputs** | Audio overviews, reports whose claims link to their passages, courses, paper walkthroughs, explainers, Pages | Chat answers, generated documents, agent results; text to speech and dictation |

*Checked against anythingllm.com, docs.anythingllm.com and the Mintplex-Labs/anything-llm repository (release 1.17.0) in October 2026. Check [anythingllm.com](https://anythingllm.com) for current plans.*

## Where AnythingLLM is better

- **Fully local and open source.** With a local model nothing leaves your machine, and the MIT-licensed code can be read, changed and self-hosted for a whole team. ForeverLM's AI runs through OpenRouter or your assistant.
- **Every desktop platform.** Mac, Windows, Linux, and a Docker server for a team. ForeverLM is Mac-centered.
- **Agents and connectors.** Web browsing, SQL, the file system, Gmail, Calendar and Outlook skills, no-code Agent Flows, scheduled jobs, and any MCP server as a tool.
- **Free to start.** The desktop app is free and needs no account.

## Where ForeverLM is better

- **Built for learning, not only retrieval.** AnythingLLM answers questions about your documents. ForeverLM also schedules what you take in, drafts cards as you finish sources, and runs a review dialogue in which a tutor who has read the whole source checks that you understood it. See [Why Quizzing?](/why-quizzing)
- **Sources arrive on their own, in full.** Reading lists, Apple Podcasts episodes with full transcripts, papers with their PDFs and metadata, X bookmarks, YouTube likes and meeting transcripts land in the library without being uploaded to a workspace.
- **One library on every Apple device.** It syncs through your iCloud to your other Macs, the iPhone app and the web library. AnythingLLM's desktop app keeps its data on one machine.
- **Works from the assistant you already use.** ForeverLM is an MCP server, so Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok can search your library, add to it and run your reviews from their own chat.
- **Study outputs.** Audio overviews, reports whose every claim links to its passage, courses, walkthroughs of a paper's figures and spoken explainers, made from your notebook's sources.
- **Gemini Notebook moves in whole.** Paste a notebook's link and its sources, chats and notes arrive as a ForeverLM notebook ([Importing a Gemini Notebook](/studio#importing-a-gemini-notebook)).

## Which should you choose?

Choose **AnythingLLM** if privacy means local models on your own hardware, you're on Windows or Linux, or you want a self-hosted document chat with agents for a team.

Choose **ForeverLM** if you're on a Mac and want a library that gathers what you read, watch and hear, syncs across your Apple devices, and helps you remember it.

---

<!-- Source: docs-site/changelog.md -->

# Changelog

All notable changes to ForeverLM are documented here. Dates are in YYYY-MM-DD format.

ForeverLM follows [semantic versioning](https://semver.org) against its public surface: the MCP tool contracts, the knowledge-base/sync format, and licensing compatibility. While the version is 0.x, minor releases may include breaking changes to that surface; patch releases never do.

## Unreleased

- **Clicking on a Page puts the caret where you clicked.** Right after you type, a click no longer jumps the caret back to where you typed when the page saves, and a click in the margin beside the text goes to that line: its start on the left, its end on the right. Drag down the margin to select line by line.

## 0.166.0 (build 246) — 2026-10-22

**Highlights:**
- **Selecting text on a Page highlights what you meant.**

- **Selecting text on a Page highlights what you meant.** A drag that ends in the space under a line selects up to that line's end instead of jumping to the start of the next one, and the highlight no longer flicks back and forth as you drag down past each line. A drag that starts just under the end of a line starts there.

## 0.165.0 (build 245) — 2026-10-22

**Highlights:**
- **Click at the end of a line on a Page and the caret goes there.**
- **Updates get through networks that block the update address.**

- **A click just under the end of a line on a Page puts the caret at its end.** A click in the gap between two lines goes to the nearer one, where you clicked, instead of the start of the line below; a click just above an empty line lands on it.
- **No Unlinked References in a Page's foot.** A page titled with a common word no longer fills its foot with other Pages' prose; the foot shows the day's activity, Linked References and a daily note's earlier days.
- **Updates get through a network that blocks the update address.** When the feed cannot be read, the app checks foreverlm.com/releases instead, so Check for Updates offers the newest build with no error.

## 0.164.0 (build 244) — 2026-10-19

**Highlights:**
- **Panes hold tabs: drag a tab to the side to view it beside the rest.**
- **Show Answer flips a card to grade yourself.**
- **More flashcards carry a picture, on the iPhone too.**

- **Panes hold tabs; pins are gone.** What a pane stops showing stays one of its tabs, so opening something never covers another surface for good. A pane with two tabs or more shows them in a strip at its top, each with a ×; middle click or Close Tab closes one too. A sidebar click brings a tab already open forward, and opens anything else as a new tab in the pane you last clicked in. Drag a tab to the side of the window to view it beside the rest; drop it on another pane's strip to move it there. A third pane appears only when you drag one there.
- **Show Answer flips a card.** In a card review you can turn a card over without typing or speaking, and grade yourself Forgot or Remembered, beside the typed answer.
- **More flashcards carry a picture.** A walkthrough or course-quiz question you miss keeps the picture it was asked with, and a lecture video's slides are pictures a drafted card may show. On the iPhone every card picture now shows: this Mac renders slides, video frames, article images and drawings and hangs them on the card.
- **A book's cover reaches your other Mac.**
- **A source you save is searchable within seconds**, not only after the next launch.
- **Articles render as written.** Two dollar amounts in one sentence no longer turn into italic math.
- **A notebook window has one sidebar toggle at the top left**, and Studio's own toggle sits at the right, where the panel is.
- **A paper's cleanup no longer fails on a long chunk**, and a cleanup still queued is no longer reported as a stalled ingestion.

## 0.163.0 (build 243) — 2026-10-17

**Highlights:**
- **A figure in the chat opens beside the chat.**
- **An open animation reloads when it is saved again.**
- **A retired image or video model is replaced and you are told.**

- **A figure in the chat can open beside the chat.** Hover it for **Open beside**: the picture takes the notebook's document slot, big, with the question still on the left.
- **Dragging a picture out of the chat no longer lights "Drop into this chat".**
- **An open animation reloads when it is saved again.** A chat, Claude or Codex that saves an animation or a site while you have it open now replaces the page you see; before, it stayed as it was loaded until you chose Reload. The animation list's way in is a compose button beside its search, and it opens the animation chat; the lone link glyph on the pane's top line is gone.
- **A retired image or video model is replaced, and you are told.** When OpenRouter stops serving the model you chose for pictures or videos, the default (or the first suggested model it serves) takes its place, a toast names both, and Settings shows the same.
- **The picture sheet has a head.** Copy Image is the one primary action, a ⋯ holds Show in Finder and Move to Trash, and the prompt carries its own copy glyph.
- **Running work links to its model.** A running step in the activity list shows Change Model… and opens the setting for that task.

## 0.162.0 (build 242) — 2026-10-17

**Highlights:**
- **A Board in the Space** with a Today view for planning the day.
- **Video overview films a video**, Mnemonic Reading is made per source, and the Feynman Technique is a chip in the notebook's chat.
- **Folded Sources and Studio columns leave the notebook window.**
- **ForeverLM is free; MCP is the paid part.**

- **Video overview makes the video.** The notebook's Studio tile used to open a file panel ("Select video overviews to add to …"); it now films one, as NotebookLM does (product owner, 2026-10-17: "it should GENERATE video"). It reads the ticked papers and articles, asks the price, films in the background, and files the finished video among the notebook's sources, listed as its Video overview. A notebook with no paper or article ticked says so instead of filming from its title. Bringing in a file you already have moved to **Make ▸ Add Video File…**. Mac only; the film lives in the Mac's library folder.
- **Mnemonic reading is made from one source.** The notebook's Studio tile and the Make menu's **Mnemonic Reading…** are gone: they wrote one reading across every ticked source (170 questions over nine sources, in one sheet). Open a source and use the Reader's **⋯ ▸ Make Mnemonic Reading…** instead, for that source, or for a book's chapter or whole book. Readings you already made are unchanged.
- **Feynman Technique moves to the notebook.** It was a Studio tile that asked you to pick one paper. It is now a chip beside **Quiz me on it** in the notebook's chat: it asks what you know about the notebook, from memory, and when you have tried it fills in the gaps, naming the source each came from. Say "I want to do the Feynman Technique" in a notebook's chat and it opens too. Its answers are pictures from your sources and one short question, never a wall of text.
- **ForeverLM is free; MCP is the paid part.** The Mac app, the iPhone and iPad apps and the web library, with sync, in-app Chat, reviews and every AI feature, never lock. AI still runs on your own OpenRouter key, billed by OpenRouter at its cost with nothing added by ForeverLM, and free models cost $0. Connecting an outside assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini, Claude Code or any MCP client) is free for 7 days from your first sign-in, with no card and nothing to click, then $19 once, the Early user deal, with no subscription, in Settings › Billing on the Mac. When the free days end and nothing is paid, only MCP locks: the connection stops and an assistant's tool calls are refused, while the app keeps working and nothing is deleted. Paying brings the connection back by itself. The in-app Chat is not MCP and is never locked. Settings › Billing now reads "MCP: 7 days free, then $19 once. No subscription.", the account menu counts "MCP free: 6 days left", and Setup's welcome line says "The app is free. MCP: 7 days free, then $19 once. No subscription." The iPhone shows no price and no way to buy, since it has no MCP connection. `get_billing_settings` now describes MCP's plan, and `own_key_allowed` is gone from `get_billing_settings` and `get_own_router_key`.
- **A Board in the Space.** The Space has a Trello-style **Board**: columns of cards you drag between, and a **Today** view for planning the day. A card is a task of a notebook kept for the board; the drop line clears itself after a drop.
- **Folded columns leave the notebook window.** Fold a notebook's Sources or Studio column and it goes, with no second icon strip left behind; both toggles sit top left in the window's sidebar controls. Dragging the Sources edge no longer re-typesets the chat on every move.
- **Notebooks from chats, and a rename tool.** Turning a chat into a notebook brings its Pages and takes every source the chat linked or read, and the notebook chat can rename its notebook with `update_notebook`. Notebooks keep their emoji by default; a cover you ask for is drawn as an emoji.
- **The notebook column names the notebook.** The name leaves the crowded titlebar and heads the column.
- **Free requests used up, said plainly.** Settings says when the day's OpenRouter free-model requests are used up, and AI Usage now says API keys and opens on today's total spend. Activity's "Turn off…" opens the exact setting, scrolled to and highlighted.
- **Menus show their icons again on macOS 27**, and the toast banner centres its text with Undo and icons on one line.
- **Library and sources.** The Hidden footer of a sources list expands in place and lists every hidden book; papers with different DOIs never merge on an identical title; podcast episodes with no cover get Apple's cover, and unhiding fetches it; Reader sign-ins survive a quit.
- **To Check and cards.** A card on several sources lists them in a popover with larger pictures and a detail line each; "more sources to come" is recounted rather than a day-old snapshot.

## 0.161.0 (build 241) — 2026-10-16

**Highlights:**
- **Back in To Check** undoes the last Keep, Skip or Remove Source.
- **A chat sees every window:** the Reader and the card open in another window go with each message.

- **To Check has a Back.** Clicked the wrong thing? Back, beside the count, undoes the last decision: after I Don't Know or Check it returns to the question with what you typed still there; after Skip, Keep, Edit, Keep All or Skip All it deals that card again, unanswered, and each press steps one further back; after Remove Source it puts the source back with its cards while the removal's Undo is still open. Back also shows under "All checked". Decisions are saved once you pause for 30 seconds, close the pane or leave the app.
- **Ask in Chat from the card you are checking.** A quiet **Ask in Chat** under a card in To Check opens a new chat beside it that already sees the card, so "why is this wrong?" needs no pasting.
- **A chat sees what every window shows.** Each message now carries the sources open in a Reader and the card open in To Check in any ForeverLM window, the chat's own window first, and the chips above the composer list them all. A video playing in another window pauses when you start typing.
- **An assistant asked to open a source that is already open comes to it.** `open_in_app` brings forward the window whose Reader already shows that source instead of opening it a second time, and says so in its answer.
- **A source id a model prints becomes a citation.** Some models print a library id in their answer instead of citing; it now draws as a numbered citation with the source's card, in new replies, replies still streaming and chats saved before.
- **Quieter account menu and To Check.** The account menu no longer has the "Your own key" or "Usage is paid for" row (the OpenRouter mark already says who pays), and the hint line under To Check's buttons is gone.

## 0.160.0 (build 240) — 2026-10-16

**Highlights:**
- **One list of sources, in the Library:** card counts on every row, a **No Cards** pill, and Make Cards or Not Worth Keeping under the pointer. Memory's Sources section is gone.

- **The sources and their cards are one list, the Library's.** Memory's Sources section is gone; the Library's rows now say how many cards each source has ("3 cards", quietly at the row's end), a **No Cards** pill beside the search lists the sources in the tab that have none, with their count, and under the pointer each row offers **Make Cards** (**Make More Cards** once it has some) and **Not Worth Keeping**, which removes the source with Undo; both are on the row's right-click menu too. With **No Cards** on, **Make Cards for 10** sits at the head. The corner card's **Choose Sources** opens the Library with the pill on.

**Highlights:**
- **To Check grades your answer:** Right, Partly or Not quite, with one line, from the same check Review runs.
- **Remove Source** under a card you are checking drops the source with Undo and skips its other cards.

- **To Check grades your answer.** Answer a card you are checking and the same check Review runs says Right, Partly or Not quite with one line, under the fold above the answer. Keep and Skip stay yours.
- **Remove Source while checking a card.** A quiet Remove Source under the card (and in its menu) drops the source from the library as Remove does, with Undo, and skips every card of its that waits in To Check.
## 0.158.0 (build 238) — 2026-10-16

**Highlights:**
- **Memory's Sources section:** every source in your library with how many cards it has; Make Cards or Not Worth Keeping on each row, and Make Cards for 10.
- **The corner card counts sources without cards**, with Choose Sources.
- **Home** lists every chat, first in the icon strip.

- **The Library no longer has a Not in any notebook button.** The toggle beside the search, and the filter it switched on, are gone.
- **A card for the sources that have no cards.** The "Cards to check" card in the corner also counts the sources in your library that no card covers, read or not: "5 sources have no cards yet", with **Choose Sources**, which opens Memory's new Sources section. With nothing to check, the card is titled "Sources without cards". It follows the same switch, Say when drafted cards wait.
- **Memory has a Sources section, for a verdict on every source.** It lists every source in your library with how many cards it has: **No Cards** is what still waits, **All** is everything. Under the pointer each row offers **Make Cards** (**Make More Cards** once it has some) and **Not Worth Keeping**, which removes the source as Remove does, with Undo; **Make Cards for 10** makes cards for the first ten waiting together so they can link their ideas. Assistants list the same sources with the new `list_source_card_coverage` tool and decide with `save_card_drafts` or `remove_source`.
- **Home lists every chat.** The icon strip's first icon is Home, every chat you have, with search and the notebook filter; the Space no longer has a Chats row. Home opens beside, in another window, and can be hidden from Show in Sidebar.
- **Plan today on my clock.** /plan, the Today menu, the Now chip and the first-run guide send one line to the chat; the day-planning rules ride along as a built-in skill the model reads, so the long prompt is gone from the chat.
- **Several accounts per plugin.** The Linear, Notion, YouTube and X pages list every connected account or workspace as its own card, with Disconnect and Add Another; the plugins list says "N connected". Linear and Notion read tools take an optional `workspace`.
- **Google Drive, one card per account.** Each connected Google account is its own card with its folders under it and its own Add Folder; Add Another Account is one quiet action below.

## 0.157.0 (build 237) — 2026-10-15

**Highlights:**
- **Panes:** each pane's top-right corner swaps what it shows, and dropping a place onto a pane replaces it.
- **Cards:** a card can play a saved animation, reads math, and the chat adds a picture to the previous card at once.
- **Copy Conversation** works on every chat.

- **A card can show an animation.** A card's question or answer can carry one of your saved animations, which plays inline under the card's pictures, with its own controls, on the Mac and the iPhone, in Review, To Check and the Knowledge Map's review; an answer's animation stays hidden until the answer shows. It runs sandboxed, with scripts and no network. Assistants put it on a card with `update_card`, `triage_cards` or `save_card_drafts`, by passing the animation's `foreverlm-site://<animation_id>/` address in `front_images` or `back_images` (one per face).
- **Cards can carry math.** A formula or symbol written in LaTeX (`\(…\)` or `$$…$$`) on a card's question, answer or why now reads as math on the Mac and the iPhone (`k_{-1}` as k₋₁, `\frac{a}{b}` as a/b) instead of showing backslashes and braces, and the card writers use it when a card needs a formula.
- **A pane's corner changes what it shows.** Hover a pane and the icons at its top right (Chat, Library, Memory, Browser, Pages) swap what the pane shows; a narrow pane folds them into one menu, and each icon can be dragged to another pane.
- **Drop a place onto a pane to replace it.** Drag a sidebar row, a Space place or New chat onto the middle of a pane and that pane shows it; the edges still open it beside.
- **Add it to the card, even after you moved on.** Ask the chat to put a figure on the previous card and it does, whether you kept that card or it is still waiting in To Check, without asking again.
- **Cards read math.** Formulas on a card read as math, not as raw LaTeX.
- **Copy Conversation everywhere.** Copy Conversation is in the menu bar, the command menu, with ⇧⌘C, and on every chat's sidebar row.
- **Chat points at passages in notes and transcripts.** The chat can open a meeting's notes or a podcast's transcript at the passage it cites.
- **【Title】 citations are links.** A bracketed title in a reply becomes the source's link.
- **Shorter card answers.** Card writers ask what an idea means and answer in one short sentence, and never ask what a source does not claim.
- **Settings General is one column.** One row per setting, labels on the left and the controls in a single column on the right.
- **OpenRouter logo on your own key.** The account menu's own-key row shows the OpenRouter logo.

## 0.156.0 (build 236) — 2026-10-15

**Highlights:**
- **Make me plan:** an option that opens the planning chat by itself each morning and keeps the card until the day is planned.
- **Cards:** a picture can be added to the card you are checking, no more easy/medium/hard label, and the Why reads as part of the answer.
- **To Check:** the iPhone asks before it shows the answer.
- **Show Passage** opens a recording at the words; **AI Usage** sits under the OpenRouter button.

- **Add a picture to the card you are checking.** Ask the chat beside To Check to add a figure it showed ("can you add it to the card?") and the picture goes on the card in front of you. It waits with the card: Keep carries it, Skip drops it. Assistants do it with `update_card` and `back_images` (or `front_images`) on a card still to check.
- **Cards no longer say easy, medium or hard.** A model used to guess a difficulty when it drafted a card and the card wore it, a small MEDIUM over the question, in To Check, in the review and in the deck a chat shows. That guess said nothing about how you find the card, so it is gone, on the Mac and the iPhone, and nothing asks for it any more (`save_card_drafts` and `save_mnemonic_reading` no longer take a `difficulty`). How hard a card is for you is something your answers will show over time.
- **Why the answer holds reads as part of the answer.** On the back of a card it is now one plain sentence under the answer, without the small WHY label, on the Mac's review, To Check and All Cards, on the iPhone, and in Edit Card. Drafted cards are asked to give the cause or the evidence that makes the answer true, not the answer again or what the author did.
- **Make me plan.** Settings → General → Day has a new switch. On a morning when your calendar holds nothing you planned, the planning chat opens by itself the first time you are at your Mac, and the "Plan your day" card cannot be closed or hidden until the calendar holds a plan of yours. Off by default; assistants read and set it as `force_planning_the_day`.

- **AI Usage is under the OpenRouter button.** The sidebar's OpenRouter button opens AI Usage beside what is running now.
- **Show Passage opens at the words.** From a video, podcast or meeting, Show Passage opens the recording at the passage, not at its start.
- **To Check asks before it answers, on the iPhone too.** The iPhone's To Check shows the question and waits for your answer before the back; on the Mac the answer field keeps the keys until the back shows.
- **The morning banner suggests cards for what you added.** It also offers cards for what you added to the library that day.
- **Chat sources are links.** The chat cites a source only as a link, never as a bracketed number with an id; and a bare "this" or "that" beside a card is answered from the previous reply and the card together.
- **Better card openers.** The walk and quiz writers stop opening cards with "In this paper", "In this lecture" or "In this course".

## 0.155.0 (build 235) — 2026-10-15

**Highlights:**
- **Cards on every source that prints them:** one card stands on both sources, and its question has one answer.
- **Edit Card, Copy Card ID, Draw Picture:** the editor is the card itself; a figureless card gets a diagram.
- **Plan my day:** a chat that proposes the day at once and revises as you answer.
- **No unattended AI:** the evening day close and every pass that ran on its own are gone.

- **Draw Picture on a card to check**: a card from a podcast or article, which has no figure to show, can be given a diagram of its answer from the ••• over the card. It is drawn only when you choose it, and kept if you keep the card.
- **The evening day close is gone,** with its "Close the day at" setting and the `close_day` tool. ForeverLM no longer runs AI in the background at the end of the day: no folding chats into understanding documents, no idea extraction, no background card drafting or rewording, no notes written from your day, and no re-checking of kept cards. Cards still draft as you finish a source when that switch is on, and the notes you add yourself stay.

## 0.142.0 (build 216) — 2026-10-11

## 0.141.0 (build 215) — 2026-10-11

**Highlights:**
- **The chat looks like Codex.** A solid composer card with your notebook on a tray behind it, a dark send button, your messages as a light pill with Copy, and replies in Codex's reading rhythm.
- **Cards ask for your answer.** Type or say what you remember, then Check, or press I Don't Know.
- **Setup asks one thing at a time.** Each page has one question and one button.
- **A chat can open a paper and point at what it explains**, and "open my notebook" really opens it.
- **A notebook made from a chat starts with that chat's sources**, and its suggestions follow them.
- **Free mode is gone**, and "What I'm working on" is kept in the background instead of as a page.

## 0.140.0 (build 214) — 2026-10-11

**Highlights:**
- **Memory cards look like cards.** Reviewing, the Memory pane, To Check and a chat's saved cards now show each card as an index card, with a deck that shows how many are left and a strip of how each card went.
- **Papers you marked paywalled stay marked.** Some papers marked paywalled long ago came back as "PDF needed" after the move to the new iCloud sync. A paywalled paper without its PDF now syncs as paywalled; one that already lost the mark needs Mark as Paywalled once.
- **Selected papers stay readable.** Selecting papers in the Library no longer hides their byline and "PDF needed" in the selection colour, and "PDF needed" sits at the end of the byline.

## 0.139.2 (build 213) — 2026-10-11

**Highlights:**
- **Dragging the Library to the edge of the window docks it.** With the Library filling the window, dragging its sidebar row to an edge now docks it there and Chat takes the rest of the window; dropped on the other edge, it moves across.

## 0.139.1 (build 212) — 2026-10-11

**Highlights:**
- **iCloud sync survives a move to another Apple team or container.** A Mac that kept the old container's sync state used to read an empty new container as "your data was removed from iCloud" and stop; it now starts fresh there. A real purge in the same container still waits for you.
- **"Upload my library to iCloud again" uploads everything.** It no longer treats a library as already seeded when only the old container had been.

## 0.139.0 (build 211) — 2026-10-11

**Highlights:**
- **The library is one pane you drag in.** The Sources panel on the right edge is gone. Click **Library** in the sidebar and it fills the window, or drag the row to an edge of the window and it docks beside your chat, a Page or a canvas, with the same tabs, search and row menus. Its sources drag into a chat or onto a canvas.
- **Google Drive asks you to sign in once.** One read-only sign-in, then a folder chooser inside ForeverLM (My Drive, Shared with me, shared drives and search). A disconnected or revoked connection shows **Reconnect Google Drive** above Drive recordings and the Meetings list, and Cancel appears wherever the app waits for Google.
- **Setup's AI step is two short pages.** **Connect OpenRouter**, then **Pick your models**, one question at a time; the data-policy note and Free mode row stay in Settings › AI Usage.
- **A paper's question markers are sharp.** The ?, ✓ and ↻ markers in a PDF's margin are drawn by the Mac at full resolution at any zoom, and clicking one opens its question as before.
- **Clicking the calendar glyph no longer quits ForeverLM.** The pill that names an icon-strip button on hover is measured once, so it can no longer resize itself until macOS ends the app.
- **7 days free, then $19 once.** The paid app's free days are 7, taken from the account server, and the pay screen says "Your free days are over". The account page on foreverlm.com is **Billing** alone: its usage totals and breakdowns are gone, since what your key spends is on OpenRouter's activity page and in Settings › AI Usage.

## 0.138.1 (build 210) — 2026-10-10

**Highlights:**
- **ForeverLM is a paid app: 7 days free, then $19 once. No subscription.** Your first sign-in starts 7 free days of the whole app, with no card. After that, the Early user deal is $19, paid once, in Settings › Billing, and it covers the Mac, iPhone, iPad and web library, unlimited notebooks and sources, and Claude, ChatGPT, Grok or Gemini over MCP. AI runs on your own OpenRouter key, at OpenRouter's cost. ForeverLM adds nothing. Free mode costs $0. An unpaid account locks after its 7 free days and nothing is deleted: your library stays in your iCloud Drive (ForeverLM folder), as plain files you own, and paying restores everything. Believer, Monthly, Yearly and Lifetime are no longer sold.
- **ForeverLM is now published under its own developer account**: the app is signed by ForeverLM and your library moves to a new iCloud store. Nothing is lost: your library stays on this Mac. Once, choose Settings › iCloud › **Upload my library to iCloud again**, sign in again, allow macOS's permissions again, and enter the keys kept in your Keychain (your own OpenRouter key, Google and Zoom) once more. Narration made before the move comes with you.
- **The Space is home**: notebooks, pages, sites, lists and chats are items in one place, with your own spaces, a Chats list, and a sidebar like ChatGPT's.
- **Pages work like ChatGPT's**: type / for blocks, footnotes, and a side chat from any page.
- **A quieter window like Codex's**, with one icon rail and the calendar as a glyph above your account.
- **Reading views and cleaner Listen**: articles and papers read cleanly, and Listen cleans every text with a model first.
- **Paper metadata arrives in seconds**, and a preprint and its journal version sit side by side.
- **Change the model behind anything you are charged for**, from Settings › AI Usage › Activity.
- **Sites stay in your library**: nothing is published to the web any more.

## 0.108.0 (build 174) — 2026-09-30

- **Your day is your Mac's Calendar**: the Planner is gone, the chip at the bottom left shows today's calendar, and a chat plans your day by adding events to it once you agree. The chip's popover lists today's events, joins a Teams, Zoom or Meet call and starts a bout; "Plan your day?" asks on mornings your calendar holds nothing you planned; and ForeverLM never changes an event other people are on. Google Calendar accounts now come through the Mac's Calendar (add them in System Settings › Internet Accounts), and a Teams or Outlook work calendar reaches it the same way, as a Microsoft Exchange account, or as a subscribed published calendar. Learning bouts and the Activity log stay, and tomorrow's memory review is still prepared in the evening; it no longer waits for *Shutdown complete*.
- **Find on YouTube finds a podcast episode whatever its upload is called**: it reads the videos the episode's own page links and the show's channel before it searches, and an assistant can do the same over MCP.
- **Add an Exchange account from ForeverLM**: Settings › Plugins › Calendar opens Internet Accounts to sign in with Microsoft Exchange, and a calendar added after you chose yours shows until you untick it.
- **Walkthroughs read like a textbook**: every card explains in plain words, step by step, a question you miss in a walk comes back in your memory review, a card shows the work it cites, and drawn pictures reach your other Macs and your phone.
- **Sources listed by name, once**: a chat reply that lists sources shows each one's thumbnail, title and byline in a single list, not a row of numbers over a second list.
- **The Reader scrolls again, and long transcripts stay smooth**: an article scrolls and takes clicks, and an hour-long transcript open in another pane no longer freezes the app.
- **A call right after the standup joins it**: a reconnect in your personal meeting room files into the standup's session, even when the standup's recording was stopped early.

## 0.76.0 (build 133) — 2026-09-21

**Highlights:**
- **A citation can open a book at the page.** The text a PDF hands the chat now marks each page, so a reply that cites a passage of a book chapter or a paper can name its page on the link. The Reader opens that page even when it cannot find the exact words, and a claim about a whole page or a figure can cite the page alone.
- **A course imports in minutes, not hours.** Formatting a lecture's captions sent the model one sentence at a time — some 370 calls a lecture. It now sends five.
- **"Open Link in New Window" works on a chat citation.** The context menu on a citation or a Sources row opens the source in a window of its own, or in any other open window, and "Open Link" opens it in the Reader beside the chat.
- **A figure step repeats the sentence in which the authors cite the panel.** Every figure step of a walkthrough quotes the paper's own sentence about that panel, found in the paper's text.

- **The course-import banner can be hidden**, and the course's sidebar row keeps spinning until the import is done.
- **A passage quoted from a reply reads as the reply showed it**, not as TeX.

## 0.75.0 (build 132) — 2026-09-21

**Highlights:**
- **A walkthrough makes one point a step.** A figure step is about one panel, which the Reader outlines while the step reads it; a step that sets up or sums up talks in the chat and marks nothing; bodies are short and a walk runs ten to thirty steps. Write Walkthrough Again gives a paper the new shape.
- **The chat follows the walk.** Back, Next and the strip's jump bring that step's row to the top of the chat, the current step's kicker draws in colour, pressing a panel letter says what that panel shows, and the strip's × leaves the walk with the steps kept in the chat. The wait before a step is named instead of blank.
- **A memory review asks a chatted-about source only what you chatted about.** A source in the review only because you discussed it is graded on the ideas that conversation reached; the rest is context the tutor never asks or grades. The tutor is told how far into a source you got, and a source's contour is graded once.
- **Figure titles are whole again.** A figure's caption is read as its printed paragraph, so a walkthrough step's figure title no longer stops where the column wrapped, and a panel's caption reads across the line breaks. Papers are re-indexed on use.
- **Science and medRxiv PDFs.** Science's red PDF button now attaches the PDF. The reader no longer sends its own request for a PDF the pipeline is already fetching, and waits out a publisher's HTTP 429 instead of showing it.
- **The chat header has a ⋯** with Open in Other Window and Copy Link, so a chat open in front of you no longer has to be found in the sidebar first.

- **No more "Running late".** A block past its end says running long while it may still be going, and "Not closed out" once it cannot be.

## 0.73.0 (build 128) — 2026-09-20

**Highlights:**
- **A stretch of reading ends in a review.** After half an hour or more of reading, listening or watching that you then put down, the Planner draws a short **Review:** block for exactly those sources on the next free quarter hour and asks *Review what you just read?*, with **Review now** on the notification. Once per stretch, never for what you already reviewed; off under Settings → Appearance → Planner → Review what you read.
- **The Planner's clock draws your day.** Settings → Appearance → Planner → Your day sets the first and last hour the clock draws, six to midnight unless you change it; the setting follows your account, and a block outside the hours still widens the clock to hold it. `set_planner_settings` takes `day_start_hour` and `day_end_hour`.
- **A meeting's block asks what you want to talk about.** Where a meeting is — its Zoom or Meet link, or its room — now lives in its own field, drawn as the Join button or a room line, so the notes are yours: on a meeting the field asks *What do you want to talk about?*, a fresh agenda for each occurrence.
- **A click on a Goal opens the Goal.** The Goals tab's row opens one sheet with **Chat about it** and **Quiz me on it** first, then everything the row says, editable, with Mark done, Archive and Delete in the footer.

- **The Artifacts home is a gallery of pictures.** Every card leads with a picture of the thing — a site or animation photographed at its address, a film's poster, a doc's opening lines — and the kind tiles are filter chips on one row with the search.
- **Hidden chats live behind a right-click.** The standing *Hidden (n)* row is gone; right-click the **Chats** header to show or hide them.

## 0.72.0 (build 127) — 2026-09-20

**Highlights:**
- **Tomorrow's memory review is ready before the morning.** When you mark the day *Shutdown complete*, ForeverLM closes the day for memory: it folds the day's chats into what it knows about each source and prepares tomorrow's review, so it is waiting on your Mac and your phone. Miss the shutdown and it runs at an evening hour you pick in Settings › Memory (22:00 by default), and the morning still catches anything left. **Close the day now** and `close_day` do it on demand.
- **Highlight a figure and chat about it.** Drag over a picture in an article and the same bar appears as over words: Chat puts the figure itself in front of the model, and Highlight outlines it and keeps it with your notes. Over MCP, `create_source_highlight` takes an `image_url`.
- **Ideas: jot a thought down before it has a date.** A new Ideas tab under Goals holds a sentence, a note, and links to the sources, chats and Docs it draws on; **Make this a goal** turns one into a Goal. Six `*_idea` tools match it.
- **The Planner is the clock alone.** The side panel is gone from the Mac; **Shutdown complete** sits in the header, and once the day is shut it opens **Reopen the day** and **Plan tomorrow…**.
- **Artifacts is one row.** Click Artifacts for a page of Docs, Sites, Videos and Animations tiles, each with its count, above everything recent.
- **A removed folder leaves the list at once.** The "1 hidden" footer no longer counts something you just removed while its Undo is still showing.

## 0.70.0 (build 125) — 2026-09-20

**Highlights:**
- **A Zoom recording only Zoom can convert is yours to decide about.** When a meeting ends before Zoom converts its recording, or Zoom was quit first, the raw files stay in Zoom's folder and ForeverLM cannot read them. ForeverLM no longer opens them in Zoom on its own, which put Zoom's unknown-source warning on your screen at every launch. Instead the Meetings tab and Settings › Sources › Zoom Transcripts list each waiting recording with **Convert in Zoom**, your own double-click made once, after which ForeverLM files and transcribes the result, and **Ignore**, for a meeting that did not happen. An assistant can do the same with `list_unconverted_zoom_recordings` and `resolve_unconverted_zoom_recording`.
- **A paper you already have opens from the library.** Clicking a web citation to a paper the library holds, under whatever address it was saved, opens the saved copy with its notes and reading position instead of a publisher's page about it. A PubMed page that turns out to be a saved paper swaps to it once it has loaded, and the Reader's **Add to Sources** button over a page you already have reads **View in Sources** and opens it.
- **"Set up a goal" always makes a Goal.** An assistant asked for a goal without a date now proposes a deadline and confirms it, rather than filing the goal as a Project's open question.

## 0.67.0 (build 121) — 2026-09-20

**Highlights:**
- **Always generate audio for explainers.** **Explainers** is a new switch beside Articles, Papers, Books and Courses under Settings &rarr; Read Aloud &rarr; Automatic audio, on the Mac and the iPhone. An explainer is saved as an article-typed source, but it has a switch of its own, so narrating every explainer never means narrating every article. With it on, an explainer's audio starts the moment its script is written — from the Reader's Explain button, the source's menu, or an assistant's `generate_explainer` — with your selected voice and no cost question. The whole card can now be read and set from an assistant with `get_automatic_audio_settings` and `set_automatic_audio_settings` (`kind: "explainer"`).
- **The Planner's side panel says less and offers more.** Goals the day has no block toward fold into one line, *5 Goals due today, none on the clock*, with **Draw blocks** opening the redraw toward them; a Goal on the clock, or due another day, keeps its row. This week folds its absences into *9 Projects got no time* once they outnumber the planned rows, and a meeting the calendar drew counts toward the Project its series belongs to. Running behind offers **Done** and **Skipped** for a block over by more than its own length instead of fifteen more minutes. `list_goals` and the rail now agree on the days a Goal has left.
- **Animations can be walked through, and a walkthrough step can show a saved animation.** **Walk Through** on an animation in the Animations pane opens the chat beside it and plays the animation's walkthrough one step a message; each step pins the animation to one of its own steps, so the drawing follows the explanation the way a paper's figures do. Any walkthrough's step can also show a saved animation at a chosen step and conditions instead of carrying its own HTML. Over MCP, `get_walkthrough`, `save_walkthrough` and `delete_walkthrough` take `animation` in place of `source_id`, a step takes `animation`, `animation_step` and `animation_conditions`, and `list_animations` reports `has_walkthrough`.
- **Click a walkthrough's outline to see the figure enlarged.** The pointer over the blue outline a step draws on the page is the zoom-in cursor, and a click opens the outlined panel or figure large, titled by the figure's printed title.
- **Opening an animation no longer moves it to the top of the list.** Clicking an animation, a Claude artifact or a Codex site in its list used to save a fresh text copy of the page as it drew — an animation's caption and clock differ every time — which dated the record and re-sorted it to the top. An open now fills only an empty text copy; one that exists stays as it was until you choose **Refresh Text Copy**. Google Docs keep following their export.

## 0.62.0 (build 116) — 2026-09-19

**Highlights:**
- **The Planner has an X to close it.** Its top-right corner now shows the close control every other workspace surface has; closing the Planner when it is the only pane reveals Chat in place.
- **A Doc has a Share button.** Beside the More menu on an open Doc, **Share** opens a popover that is the one place to say who can open it: invite people by email (they read the page; a page reads the same for everyone but its author), an **Anyone with the link** row with Can read or No access, an **Anyone at \<team\>** row per team that shares a copy into the team and admits its members to the page, each reader with a remove control, and one sentence saying who can open the Doc, with **Copy link** beside it. Web Studio's publish dialog has the same rows and the same sentence, and `list_docs` reports it as `published_access_summary`.
- **The memory review is a committed session.** The Review mode sheet says what you are agreeing to before **Start Review**: the goal's minutes (fifteen by default), the window becomes the review, the clock counts while you are in it, and leaving early ends today's session. Leaving by any door — the ✕ by the clock, which asks first, another surface, another chat, or quitting — ends the day's session: the clock goes quiet, the chat can be read back but credits nothing, and there is no second start until tomorrow. Reaching the goal completes the day as before.
- **The Planner holds a Memory review block every day.** Today and every day ahead gets one **Memory review** block, the goal's minutes long, on the first free quarter hour. It is yours to move or delete, is never drawn twice or put back, and is marked done when the day's goal is met on any device; on today its **Chat** is **Start review**.
- **The Planner's side panel reads the log against the plan instead of listing it twice.** By day it shows **Today**, Planned and Logged as two bars, the Logged bar split by how the minutes stood to the plan (in its block, open time, off its block, outside any block), then **Not in the plan**: only the sittings the clock cannot explain, each with the off-the-block answers and, when a later block of the day named that source, **Count toward** that block. Once the day is shut down, or a past day is showing, the panel looks back: **How the day went** with the alignment sentence, **What you did** by thing, Notes, Reopen and Plan tomorrow. Web Studio draws the same two states.
- **A meeting whose transcript arrived is done.** A meeting block is the one block ForeverLM completes on its own: when the session's transcript is stored, however it arrived, the calendar block that meeting occupied is marked done in the same write that links the transcript to it. The clock still completes nothing, and a meeting that left no transcript waits for you to say it happened.
- **A Zoom meeting recorded on this Mac is found whether or not Save Captions was on.** The Zoom watcher reads the recording folders under ~/Documents/Zoom as well as the caption files: a converted recording becomes a session of its series, linked to the calendar block it occupied and transcribed by ForeverLM, a meeting that ran over into a second slot files as two sessions, and a recording Zoom left unconverted is handed back to Zoom to convert. Settings → Sources counts the recordings beside the transcripts.
- **Claude and Codex can see a paper's figures.** `inspect_paper_figure` returns a figure rendered from the paper's own PDF and cropped to it, with its caption and ForeverLM's explanation, or one panel alone; `show_source_image` shows any source's pictures by label, caption words, page or slide. The picture travels in the tool result as an image, so the assistant sees the plot rather than its caption.
- **The Now chip stands in the middle of the titlebar band.** Centred in every window's titlebar, clear of the sidebar toggle and the Sources controls, saying the block's title in full where it fits, with a hairline along its foot showing how far through the block the clock is; it steps aside while the Planner itself is on screen in that window.
- **A block's editor reads as the block, not as a form.** The title is a heading that wraps, the hour is two plain clock fields with the duration beside them, Toward and Project share one column, the block's sources sit in one Reading card, and the notes take the boxed field the Set a goal sheet uses.
- **A Goal set on one Mac survives another Mac's update.** The schema 120 step promotes to Projects only rows created before the day Goals shipped, so a Goal synced in from a newer build keeps its deadline.

- **My Library lists your teams' artifacts beside your own.** The Docs, Sites, Animations and Artifacts homes list what your teams hold as well, each with a small two-person mark naming the team; opening one takes you into that team's library. The Artifacts home now loads its list itself.

## 0.60.0 (build 114) — 2026-09-19

**Highlights:**
- **Goals are their own tab.** A Goals row sits in the rail between Planner and Artifacts and opens one list, nearest deadline first, each goal showing how long is left and how much time the last seven days gave it. **Set a goal** is one sentence and a deadline; a Project is optional, and the deadline is what makes a Goal a Goal.

- **A first robustness pass.** A failing database step is reported instead of silently shortening a list; a malformed numeric argument over MCP is refused instead of crashing the app; `save_animation` reads only files in the folders every other tool may read; a YouTube Short and its watch page are one source.

## 0.59.0 (build 113) — 2026-09-19

**Highlights:**
- **The block you are in, in every window.** A Now chip in every window's titlebar, and in a pop-out Reader's toolbar, says which block the clock is in and how long it has left: filled while the hour is on what the block named, hollow in open time, amber once ten minutes have gone elsewhere, a timer while a bout runs. Click it to open the block's sources and Project, start a bout, mark it done or skipped, give it fifteen more minutes, or answer the drift.
